title: Tag entities with scope-correct identity
description:
Phase 4 of slate-parser-8lv. Closes slate-parser-rsm and slate-parser-9wx.

Tag identity is by name in TypeResolver.tag_names: Vec<HashMap<(TagKind, String), TypeId>>. The scope stack exists but module.rs statement lowering never drives push_scope/pop_scope, so:

- Block-scoped tag definitions are rejected outright by module.rs::declaration, because removing the guard is unsound today: two functions each defining 'struct Local' with different fields collapse onto one TypeId, the type table emits one record, and the second function's field accesses are typed against the first one's layout (rsm). Anonymous local tags are safe since they cannot collide by name.
- A standalone 'struct S;' does not declare an incomplete tag, so 'struct S; struct S *p;' fails with 'unresolved tag name S' (9wx). Same for 'struct A; struct A *f(void);'.

Give tags the same entity treatment keyed by TagId: kind, name, scope, completeness and definition site, with scope-correct lookup. A standalone declaration creates an incomplete entity in the current scope; a later definition in the same scope completes it; a definition in an inner scope creates a distinct entity rather than colliding by name.

Interacts with the C23 compatible-tag-redefinition path from 9ve.6 (same_field_types, and the same_tag_content pre-filter recorded as an exception in wiki/concepts/c-type-layer.md): redefinition compatibility is a same-scope question, so scoping must be settled before that check runs.

Acceptance: rsm's repro gives each local struct its own TypeId and correct field layouts; 9wx's two repros lower; block-scope, file-scope and inner-scope tags of the same name are covered by fixtures; cargo nextest run --release passes.
close_reason: Block-scope tag definitions accepted (the rejecting guard was stale; scopes were already driven correctly), and a bare 'struct S;' declares an incomplete tag in the current scope per C11 6.7.2.3p8, hiding any outer tag. Closed rsm and 9wx. Fixture sema/ir_tag_scopes.c covers forward declaration through a pointer and a return type, forward-then-complete in one scope, two same-named block-scope tags with different layouts, and an inner declaration hiding an outer complete tag. Corpus churn: two error fixtures, both replacing a spurious 'unresolved tag name' with the genuine constraint violation that clang also reports. Gates green. Filed slate-parser-30r for the misleading 'incomplete field type' wording.

title: Declared-entity acceptance sweep and wiki
description:
Phase 5 of slate-parser-8lv.

- Audit that the entity table is the only source of object/tag properties in sema, the way 9ve.6 audited ir::Type comparisons: a documented grep with every survivor accounted for, and any residue filed rather than left implicit.
- Fixtures exercising each property at every declaration site named in the epic's acceptance criteria: file scope, block scope, static local, parameter, field, compound literal.
- Wiki: a concepts page for the entity model, and updates to ir-spec.md for anything that changes what the IR printer emits (alignment on a let, atomic on a declaration), in the same change per the repo rule.
- Close the covered tickets, annotate what each phase actually delivered, and close the epic when its acceptance criteria are met.
- One byte-exact fixture regeneration across the corpus as the final check.
close_reason: Audited both property-source greps (IR object declaration construction; alignment request readers/writers) with every hit accounted for in the new wiki/concepts/entity-model.md, linked from wiki/index.md and ir-spec.md. Residues filed rather than left implicit: slate-parser-dev, slate-parser-eiq, slate-parser-rjy. Tags documented as deliberately outside the BindingId table, with TypeResolver as the tag entity table. New acceptance-matrix fixture sema/ir_entity_sites.c covers file scope, block scope, static local, parameter, field and compound literal against the type, alignment and const/volatile/restrict/_Atomic properties; the three cells C or the printer cannot express are named on the page. Regenerating all fixtures produced zero diff outside the new one; cargo nextest run --release passes.

title: Effective alignment from the entity at every declaration site
description:
Phase 2 of slate-parser-8lv. Closes slate-parser-lh7.2.31 and slate-parser-lh7.2.32.

The alignment request lives in Lowerer.object_requests and is resolved only in resolve_object_requests, a post-pass over module.globals. Two consequences:
- _Alignof/__alignof__ of a declared object folds the type's natural alignment, ignoring the attribute (lh7.2.31). 'int x __attribute__((aligned(16))); int k = _Alignof(x);' gives 4, clang gives 16 -- and 1 for aligned(1), since clang alone lets the attribute lower a variable's alignment.
- Automatic locals have nowhere to put it: ir::Variable has no alignment field, so 'void f(void){ int x __attribute__((aligned(16))); _Alignas(32) int z; }' fails with 'automatic variable attributes or asm label' (lh7.2.32).

With phase 1's entity holding the requested alignment, TypeResolver::effective_alignment applies once, on the entity, and every site reads the result: Global.alignment stops being a post-pass, ir::Variable gains alignment for lets, and alignof of an object reads the entity instead of the type.

The flavor rule is already written and measured (9ve.5): clang honors a request below natural alignment, gcc and MSVC raise it to natural.

Acceptance: fixtures cover an alignment attribute and _Alignas at file scope, block scope, static local and parameter, each with its alignof; the aligned(1) lowering case is covered per flavor; cargo nextest run --release passes.
notes:
Oracle measurements 2026-09-19 (clang 22.1.8, gcc 16.2.1, MSVC 14.51).

__alignof__ of a DECLARED OBJECT, via a running program printing __alignof__ of each:
  aligned(16) global/local, _Alignas(32) global/local -> 16 / 32 in all three.
  aligned(1) global -> clang 1, gcc 1, MSVC 4 (__declspec(align(1)) raises to natural).
  plain int -> 4 everywhere.

IR-level object alignment, via clang -S -emit-llvm:
  @g1 aligned(1) -> 'align 1'; @g16 -> 'align 16'.
  locals: alloca align 16 / 1 / 32 / 4 for aligned(16), aligned(1), _Alignas(32), plain.
  So locals follow exactly the same rule as globals, and TypeResolver::effective_alignment from 9ve.5 applies unchanged.

Correction to a false alarm: clang's ASSEMBLY shows '.p2align 2' for aligned(1), which looks like the request being ignored. It is not -- the LLVM IR carries 'align 1' and the .p2align is a later section-level decision. 9ve.5's rule and the [align=1] in ir_object_attributes.c are right.

Consequence for this phase: there are TWO alignment rules, not one, and they differ in exactly one cell.
  - what the object GETS (effective_alignment, 9ve.5): clang = requested; gcc, MSVC = max(requested, natural).
  - what __alignof__ REPORTS: clang, gcc = requested; MSVC = max(requested, natural).
They differ only for gcc with a request below natural: gcc lays the object out at natural but reports the declared 1. lh7.2.31's description says to reuse the flavor rule from resolve_object_requests; that would report 4 for gcc and be wrong. A separate rule is needed for the alignof side.
close_reason: Alignment moved onto ir::Variable so lets and globals share one field and one print site; automatic locals accept alignment attributes; __alignof__ of an object reads the entity's request via a second flavor rule, declared_alignment, because gcc reports a below-natural request while laying the object out at natural. Closed lh7.2.31 and lh7.2.32. Fixture sema/ir_object_alignment_sites.c covers file scope, block scope and static local with each alignof, all matching clang and gcc exactly. Filed slate-parser-kmq for parameter attributes. Gates: nextest green, clippy and fmt clean, corpus regeneration churn limited to the four [align=] fixtures and positional only.

title: Binding-level qualifiers in IR declarations
description:
Phase 3 of slate-parser-8lv. Closes slate-parser-lh7.2.28.

ir::Variable carries restrict and is_const, hand-set at each declaration site, but no atomic. An _Atomic object's promoted layout is computed correctly (lh7.2.20) but nothing in the default dump says the object is atomic, and no size is printed for a global or a let, so the 4/4 layout cannot be recovered:

  struct odd3 { char a[3]; };
  _Atomic struct odd3 object;
  -> global %1 object: @type0    (identical to a plain struct odd3)

The fact reaches the dump only through accesses (read<..., atomic=seq_cst>), so an object never read or written in the TU carries nothing. Slate needs it to choose the Rust type (AtomicU32 vs a plain field), which is a property of the object, not of one access.

With the entity holding the qualified C type, ir::Variable, ir::Parameter and ir::Global derive const/restrict/_Atomic from it by one rule rather than three hand-written assignments.

Note: lh7.2.28 says to settle this together with lh7.2.16 as the 'const on a variable' case, but lh7.2.16 is actually about unnamed parameters and is already closed. That cross-reference is stale.

Acceptance: a fixture declares an _Atomic global and an _Atomic local with no accesses and each prints the fact on the let/global in the default dump; const and restrict keep their current spelling; cargo nextest run --release passes.
close_reason: ir::Variable and ir::Parameter carry an Access derived from the declaration's qualifiers, printed as a type prefix matching record fields. Closes lh7.2.28: an _Atomic or volatile global/local/parameter now states the fact even with no accesses in the unit. declare_global re-derives const/restrict/access from the merged composite. Fixture sema/ir_declaration_qualifiers.c covers atomic, volatile, both, const, restrict at file scope, block scope and parameters. Gates: nextest green, clippy and fmt clean; all fixture churn is the new prefix (zero added expectation lines without one). ir-spec.md and ir-grammar.md updated in the same change.

title: Compiler personality in layout(): atomic promotion and alignment rules
description:
Phase 5: compiler personality in layout(): atomic promotion and alignment rules (lh7.2.30, lh7.2.29). Shared rules/ctype API/pitfalls: design field of slate-parser-9ve.

WORK
1. Thread unit.flavor (CompilerFlavor, src/compiler_args.rs) into TypeResolver/layout (ctype/layout.rs). The assertion checker (assertion.rs, its own TypeResolver) needs it too: static_assert(sizeof(_Atomic struct{char a[3];}) == 3) must pass under gcc. All three TypeResolver instances (module lowering, resolve_type_module, assertion.rs) must share construction.
2. lh7.2.30: _Atomic storage promotion (target.atomic_storage, applied in TypeResolver::qualified_storage) is clang-only. Rewrite ir-spec "_Atomic changes layout" paragraph; add a gcc prefix to tests/fixtures/sema/ir_atomic_layout.c. Close lh7.2.30.

title: Explicit atomic memory orderings: ordering field on read/write/update, plus compare-exchange and fence nodes
description:
Explicit memory orderings have no IR representation. Plain accesses to an _Atomic object lower with atomic=seq_cst (lh7.2.10), which is correct because C gives them no other ordering. Relaxed, consume, acquire, release and acq_rel only come from explicit operations: the <stdatomic.h> *_explicit functions and fences, which clang's header expands to __c11_atomic_* builtins, plus the GCC __atomic_* builtins that code also calls directly. None of these resolve in sema today.

Repro (2026-09-18):
  printf '_Atomic int c;\nint f(void){ __c11_atomic_store(&c, 1, 3); int a = __atomic_load_n(&c, 2); return a; }\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c
  Observed: unresolved ordinary name `__c11_atomic_store`.
The builtin names are only known to the preprocessor's __has_builtin table (src/pp/has_checks.rs).
design:
Put the ordering on the existing access nodes as a field. Do not add a wrapper node, and do not add CIR-style dedicated load/store/RMW ops. Only compare-exchange and fences get new nodes.

WHY NOT DEDICATED OPS (CIR/LLVM)
LLVM itself is not fully "dedicated ops". Atomic load and store are the ordinary load/store instructions with an ordering attached (load atomic ... acquire), and CIR copies that with an atomic(mem_order) attribute on cir.load/cir.store. Only atomicrmw, cmpxchg and fence are separate instructions. atomicrmw is separate because it has a fixed operation set (add, sub, and, or, xor, nand, min, max, xchg) and cannot hold an arbitrary computation. Our update(place, f(old)) can hold one, so that reason does not apply here.

WHY NOT A WRAPPER NODE
atomic<o>(read(...)) means the same thing as a field, but the wrapper is only valid around three kinds of child. atomic<o>(add(...)) would be expressible and meaningless, and every consumer would have to reject it. A field on the nodes lets the Rust types rule those shapes out, and the printed form stays as it is now (read<i32, atomic=acquire>).

NODE SHAPE
- New enum MemoryOrder { Relaxed, Consume, Acquire, Release, AcqRel, SeqCst, Dynamic(Box<Value>) }.
- Read, Store (and Statement::Write) and Update each get `ordering: Option<MemoryOrder>`. None means a non-atomic access.
- Printing: read<T, atomic=acquire>, write<T, atomic=release>, update<T, result=old, atomic=acq_rel>. A plain _Atomic access prints atomic=seq_cst exactly as it does today.

MAPPING
  atomic_load_explicit(p, o)          read<T, atomic=o>(deref(p))
  atomic_store_explicit(p, v, o)      write<T, atomic=o>(deref(p), v)
  atomic_fetch_OP(p, v, o)            update<T, result=old, atomic=o>(deref(p), OP(old, v))
  __atomic_OP_fetch(p, v, o)          update<T, result=new, atomic=o>(deref(p), OP(old, v))
  atomic_exchange(p, v, o)            update<T, result=old, atomic=o>(deref(p), v)   (computation ignores old)
  nand / min / max                    update with that computation (min/max need an arith op or a compare+select)
  atomic_flag_test_and_set / clear    update / write on the flag's bool
  plain _Atomic access, += , ++       the same nodes with atomic=seq_cst
  __atomic_load(p, ret, o) (generic, non-_n)   write(deref(ret), read<T, atomic=o>(deref(p)))
  __atomic_store / __atomic_exchange (generic) likewise, through the pointer arguments

For Rust, add(old, v) maps to fetch_add and any other computation maps to fetch_update. Slate does that pattern matching, the same way it already matches arithmetic.

A general computation keeps pointer semantics exact. On _Atomic(T*), C11 atomic_fetch_add adds in element units (ptr_offset), while GCC __atomic_fetch_add on a pointer adds bytes. The computation states which one; a fixed fetch_add op would have to encode it separately.

NEW NODES
- CompareExchange: place, expected pointer (written back on failure), desired value, success ordering, failure ordering, weak flag. Result is bool. It is not an update because the write is conditional and the write-back goes to a second location.
- Fence { ordering, scope: Thread | Signal } for atomic_thread_fence / atomic_signal_fence. Statement-level, and it accesses no place.

CHANGES TO lh7.2.10
- Place.access keeps only volatile. Atomicity is a property of the operation, not the place, because GCC __atomic_load_n works on a plain int. A plain _Atomic access sets ordering=SeqCst on the operation, derived from the place's type.
- The pointee "atomic" in ptr<atomic T> stays. It is type information (what *p refers to), and it is how the lowerer knows *p gets seq_cst.
- The hoisting rule that keeps an atomic update whole (effects.rs) switches from place.access.atomic to update.ordering.is_some().
- Volatile atomics: a __atomic_* builtin on a volatile-qualified pointee keeps volatile on the place, so the access is both volatile and ordered.

FIDELITY RULES
- Record the ordering exactly as written. An acquire store, a release load, or a failure ordering stronger than success is undefined behavior, but the input is assumed to compile, so we keep it and do not reject it.
- Keep Consume distinct even though clang treats it as Acquire.
- A non-constant ordering argument is legal C (clang emits a runtime switch), so it becomes MemoryOrder::Dynamic(value). A constant argument folds to the enum; this is a required fold, allowed by the ir-required-constant-folding rule.
- Exchange loses its name when it becomes an update. Attach c_builtin=<spelling> metadata (e.g. __c11_atomic_exchange, atomic_fetch_add_explicit via macro provenance) so the original builtin is recoverable.

SEMA
- Builtins need declarations or a dedicated resolution path. They are type-generic (like __builtin_add_overflow), so they cannot be ordinary prototypes. Resolve them from the pointer argument's pointee type.
- <stdatomic.h> must preprocess with clang's resource include dir on the isystem path. Fixtures use the same ISYSTEM line as ir_add.c.

OUT OF SCOPE
_Atomic size and alignment padding (lh7.2.20). __sync_* legacy builtins, which are always seq_cst full barriers; they can map onto the same nodes later.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture covers every mapping-table row through both the __c11_atomic_* and __atomic_* builtins and through <stdatomic.h> *_explicit calls: each ordering (relaxed, consume, acquire, release, acq_rel, seq_cst) prints on the node, compare-exchange prints both orderings and weak/strong, both fence kinds print, a non-constant ordering prints as dynamic, and _Atomic(T*) fetch_add shows element-unit versus byte arithmetic. Plain _Atomic access output from ir_qualified_access.c is unchanged. ir-spec.md 'Qualified access' is updated in the same change.
close_reason: Closed

title: Model diagnostic severity so -Werror and -pedantic-errors can reject extensions
description:
There is no warning channel anywhere in sema: SemaError is the only diagnostic type, and compiler_args parses no -W flags at all. Extension acceptances are therefore silent.

Two are live as of slate-parser-47s.2: long long in c89 (Availability::Extension on StandardFeatures::long_long_type) and the implicitly-unsigned decimal literal fallback in c99+ (clang's -Wimplicitly-unsigned-literal). Both change the lowered type and neither is reportable.

Note what does NOT need modeling: individual -W names do not change generated code. clang picks the same type with or without -Wc99-compat or -Wimplicitly-unsigned-literal; the flag only controls whether text is printed. The axis that changes output is severity promotion.
design:
Give each extension/compat acceptance a diagnostic identity (a warning name matching clang's: long-long, c99-compat, implicitly-unsigned-literal), add a warning channel alongside SemaErrors, and parse -W/-Wno-/-Werror[=]/-Wno-error=/-Wpedantic/-pedantic/-pedantic-errors into a severity map.

CORRECTION (verified against clang 22, 2026-09-18): the original design claimed -pedantic-errors must make Availability::Extension behave as Rejected, changing integer_candidates. That is wrong. clang -m32 -std=c89 -pedantic-errors still types 4294967296 as long long and reports the *use* of the extension as an error; the candidate list is unchanged. So severity is a pure diagnostic concern and never feeds type selection, and StandardFeatures does not need the severity map.

Observed clang semantics to model:
- -Wlong-long: default off, implied by -pedantic, works standalone, suppressed by -Wno-long-long even under -pedantic.
- -Wc99-compat: default ON in c89 mode; NOT promoted by -pedantic-errors (it is not a pedantic diagnostic); suppressed by -Wno-c99-compat; promoted by -Werror=c99-compat.
- -pedantic-errors promotes only pedantic-group diagnostics to errors.

So: severity(w) = suppressed if -Wno-<w>; else Error if -Werror=<w> or (-Werror and enabled) or (pedantic_errors and w in pedantic group); else Warning if -W<w> or default-on-for-standard or (pedantic and w in pedantic group); else suppressed.
acceptance_criteria: FileCheck fixtures show: (1) an extension-accepted construct emits a named warning, (2) -Werror= on that name fails the TU, (3) -pedantic-errors rejects a c89 long long literal that plain -std=c89 accepts.
close_reason: Closed

title: Stringification inserts spaces between tokens that were adjacent
description: The # operator renders the argument's tokens space-separated instead of reproducing the original spacing. With '#define S(x) #x', S((-307)) yields "( - 307 )" and S(a+b) yields "a + b"; clang and C11 6.10.3.2p2 require "(-307)" and "a+b" -- whitespace appears in the result only where whitespace appeared between the argument's tokens, collapsed to one space, with leading and trailing space deleted. Found while diffing predefined macro expansions against clang -dM; it makes several float-limit predefines (__DBL_MIN_EXP__ and friends) stringify differently from clang on every target and standard.

title: __STRICT_ANSI__ is not predefined in strict standard modes
description: clang defines __STRICT_ANSI__ for -std=c89/c99/c11/c17/c23 and leaves it undefined for the gnu* modes. src/predefines has no mention of it, so real-world headers that branch on it (glibc's features.h picks __USE_GNU vs strict-ANSI declarations off it) take the wrong branch in strict modes. Fixtures cannot currently distinguish gnu-ness from inside a source file for the same reason.

title: Function specifiers and attributes are rejected wholesale; inline has no IR model
description:
sema/module.rs:43 refuses any function carrying attributes, and check_specifiers rejects inline, _Noreturn, and constexpr on both functions and objects.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf 'constexpr int k = 5; int f(void){ return k; }\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c -std=c23
Observed: unsupported in numeric IR lowering: attributes, function specifiers, volatile or atomic access.

ir::Function has id, name, parameters, return_type, linkage (Internal | External), body, fallthrough -- no inline concept at all. That is not just a missing field: gnu89 inline and C99 inline have opposite emission rules. In gnu89, 'inline' emits an externally visible definition and 'extern inline' does not; in C99 it is reversed -- 'inline' alone is an inline definition that emits nothing and 'extern inline' provides the external definition. Both dialects appear in real headers (glibc uses __gnu_inline__ precisely to pin the old behavior), so a single Linkage enum silently produces wrong link-time semantics for one of them. This is the sharpest standard difference the IR currently cannot express, so it belongs here rather than in slate-parser-47s.

C23 constexpr objects are a separate matter: a constexpr object has a constant initializer and is not merely const, which the IR should distinguish once initializers lower.
design: Linkage needs the inline dimension alongside Internal/External -- gnu89 vs C99 resolution reads the standard, the __gnu_inline__ / __always_inline__ attributes, and 'extern' together, so resolve it once in sema and record the outcome (emit a definition / inline definition only) rather than storing the raw specifiers and re-deriving downstream. _Noreturn and [[noreturn]] are a divergence fact about the function, not an optimization hint, so they belong on the node. For the general attribute set, decide which attributes carry translation signal and pass those through as metadata rather than continuing to refuse every function that has any.
acceptance_criteria: A function with attributes lowers rather than erroring; inline resolution is pinned by fixtures in gnu89 and c99 for inline, extern inline, and static inline; _Noreturn and constexpr objects are represented; no lowering path still returns Unsupported for the mere presence of a function specifier.
notes: Implemented InlineSemantics::{SupressDef, ProvideDef}, normalized -fgnu89-inline/-fno-gnu89-inline with last occurrence winning, and matching preprocessing macros. Coalesced declaration history into inlining preference, semantics override, definition-specifier enum, and external-declaration bookkeeping. Added resolved IR emission, noreturn, constexpr marker/implicit const/internal linkage, and function attribute metadata. Generated fixtures cover dialect defaults, flag override/reset/order, gnu_inline override, redeclarations, conflict diagnostics, and MSVC flag rejection. Release FileCheck suite passes.
close_reason: Implemented compiler-controlled inline semantics, coalesced declaration state, function attributes and noreturn, and constexpr object representation; generated FileCheck coverage and quality gates pass.

title: typeof and typeof_unqual declarations fail to lower
description:
The lexer accepts every typeof spelling (see the gcc-typeof-aliases memory) and the parser builds TypeSpecifier::TypeOf / TypeOfUnqual, but sema rejects both.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf 'int f(void){ int x=1; typeof(x) y = x; return y; }\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c -std=c23
Observed: unsupported in numeric IR lowering: type specifier.

Both operand forms need resolving: TypeOfOperand::Type is a plain type name, and TypeOfOperand::Expression must be typed without being evaluated -- the same unevaluated-operand discipline _Generic's controlling expression already uses, including rolling back binding IDs and string-literal globals that typing it would otherwise create. typeof_unqual additionally strips qualifiers from the result, which is only meaningful once qualifiers are modeled (slate-parser-lh7.2.10).
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover typeof of a type name, typeof of an expression with side effects (which must not be evaluated), typeof of an array and of a function, typeof_unqual stripping const/volatile, and the __typeof__/__typeof aliases; the resolved type appears in the dump with the typedef chain metadata other declarations carry.
close_reason: Completed typeof/typeof_unqual sema integration, unevaluated operand rollback, type metadata, and generated acceptance fixtures; clippy, fmt, and release FileCheck suite pass.

title: Lower the remaining ExprKind variants that fall through to 'advanced expression'
description:
sema/expression.rs ends with '_ => Err(ResolveError::Unsupported("advanced expression"))', which currently swallows five parsed-but-unlowerable forms:

- CompoundLiteral -- (int[]){1,2,3}; an unnamed object with block or static storage duration. Depends on aggregate initializer lowering (slate-parser-lh7.2.8).
- StatementExpression -- GNU ({ ... }); the value is the last statement's value. Interacts with the side-effect hoisting pass, since the whole block is already statements.
- VaArg -- __builtin_va_arg(ap, T). Unavoidable for real headers; every varargs consumer uses it.
- TypesCompatible -- __builtin_types_compatible_p; partially tracked by slate-parser-eb8 for its constant folding.
- BitCast -- __builtin_bit_cast.

va_arg is the one that blocks real-world input soonest and can land first; the others can follow independently.
design: Split into separate changes rather than one sweep -- these share only the match arm, not the semantics. Each needs its own IR node decision: va_arg is a type-directed read from an opaque list object, a statement expression is a block with a result value (which the hoisting pass already has a shape for), a compound literal is an anonymous object with a storage duration, and bit_cast is a reinterpretation with a size-equality precondition. Keep the catch-all arm's error text listing what is left so the diagnostic stays specific as arms are added.
acceptance_criteria: Each form has a FileCheck fixture; the catch-all arm no longer covers any of the five; va_arg lowers for both a fixed-type and a struct-typed argument.
notes: 2026-09-18: all five done. VaArg (ir_va_arg.c), CompoundLiteral (compound_literals.c, landed earlier as PlaceKind::CompoundLiteral), TypesCompatible (ir_types_compatible.c), BitCast (ir_bit_cast.c), StatementExpression (ir_statement_expressions.c). Lowerer::expr is now exhaustive over ExprKind; the catch-all arm is removed.
close_reason: All five forms lower with fixtures; Lowerer::expr is exhaustive over ExprKind.

title: Variable length arrays have no IR representation
description:
ir::Type::Array is { element, length: Option<u64> }, where None means incomplete. There is no room for a runtime extent, so a VLA cannot be typed at all.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf 'int f(int n){ int a[n]; return sizeof a; }\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c
Observed: unsupported in numeric IR lowering: nonconstant or unknown identifier.

The AST already carries ArraySize::Star for [*] and an Expression size for the [n] form; both currently have nowhere to lower. Consequences beyond the declaration: sizeof on a VLA is a runtime value rather than a folded constant (so the 'required constant evaluation' rule in ir-spec.md needs a stated exception), pointer arithmetic on a VLA-typed pointer scales by a runtime element size, and a VLA's lifetime ends at the end of its block.
design: Length becomes three-way: Fixed(u64) | Runtime(Value) | Incomplete, rather than Option<u64>. The runtime extent must be captured once at the declaration, not re-evaluated at each use, which means the extent is a value computed by a statement at the point of declaration -- reuse the Evaluation/synthetic-temporary machinery the side-effect hoisting pass already has. [*] in a prototype is a distinct case: it declares that a dimension is variable without naming the extent, so it needs its own marker.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover a one-dimensional VLA local, a multidimensional VLA, sizeof on a VLA, a VLA function parameter, and [*] in a prototype; the runtime extent is evaluated once and visible in the dump.
close_reason: VLA parameters, [*], runtime-stride indexing and VLA pointer compatibility lowered; local VLAs/sizeof were done in er8. Remaining gaps filed as lh7.2.24 and lh7.2.25.

title: Model volatile, restrict, and _Atomic in the IR rather than only as metadata
description:
ir::Type::Pointer carries only is_const. volatile, restrict, and _Atomic survive solely as c_volatile / c_restrict / c_atomic metadata strings on the declaration, and lowering refuses any volatile or atomic access outright.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf 'volatile int g;\nint f(void){ g = 1; return g; }\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c
Observed: unsupported in numeric IR lowering: attributes, function specifiers, volatile or atomic access.

ir-spec.md already promises 'volatile/atomic access behavior is also resolved on the actual accesses' -- that is not implemented. Access-level resolution is the important half: volatile constrains whether a read may be elided or reordered, and Slate needs that on the read/write node, not on the declaration it came from.

restrict is the one C qualifier that carries information nothing else in the IR does: it is an aliasing guarantee about a pointer parameter, and it is unrecoverable from the IR today. Per the parser-preserves-structure memory, Slate owns the Rust translation -- so the requirement here is fidelity, keeping the fact available on the node, not choosing a Rust shape for it.
design: Decide per qualifier where it belongs: pointee const is already in the type because it changes the shown type; volatile and atomic are properties of an access, so they belong on Read/Write/Store/Update nodes; restrict is a property of a pointer binding, so it belongs on the parameter or variable. Resist putting all four in Type just for symmetry -- the IR shows Rust-shaped types and a volatile-qualified type has no Rust type counterpart, only a different access. Check what CIR does before settling the node shape.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture exercises volatile scalar read/write, a restrict-qualified pointer parameter, and an _Atomic object; each fact is visible on the relevant IR node in the default dump; no lowering path still returns Unsupported for a volatile or atomic access.
close_reason: Closed

title: Enumerator typing rules are not gated: pre-C23 enumerators must fit in int
description:
Before C23, every enumerator must be representable as int (C99 6.7.2.2p2 makes a value outside int's range a constraint violation), and each enumerator has type int regardless of the enum's compatible type. C23 lets an enumerator take a wider type when it does not fit and adds a fixed underlying type (enum E : unsigned char).

slate-parser applies the C23 rules in all modes. 'enum E : unsigned char { A = 1 };' is accepted under -std=c89 (verified 2026-09-17); clang and gcc accept the fixed underlying type as an extension before C23, so that spelling may not need gating -- but the enumerator range rule does, since a pre-C23 out-of-int-range enumerator is a diagnosable constraint violation, not an extension.

Also in scope: a trailing comma in an enumerator list is C99+; C89 forbids it (clang -std=c89 -pedantic warns). slate-parser accepts it unconditionally.
design: Check what clang actually does for each of: out-of-int-range enumerator, fixed underlying type, and trailing comma, in c89/c99/c11/c17/c23 and the gnu variants, before deciding which are gated and which are extensions recorded as such per the _BitInt precedent. The underlying-type selection in sema/types.rs must follow whichever rule the mode picks, since it feeds enum_to_int / int_to_enum conversions in the IR.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover an out-of-int-range enumerator, a fixed underlying type, and a trailing comma across c89 and c23; enum underlying type selection and the resulting enum_to_int conversions match clang in each mode.
close_reason: Closed

title: restrict, inline, typeof, and constexpr lex as keywords in every standard mode
description:
lexer.rs recognizes these unconditionally (lines ~708-727), unlike bool/true/false/static_assert/thread_local which are correctly gated on is_c23_or_later. Each is a valid identifier in modes where it is not a keyword, so valid C fails to parse:

- restrict: C99 keyword. In -std=c89, 'int restrict;' is valid. (__restrict/__restrict__ stay keywords in all modes.)
- inline: C99 keyword. In -std=c89, 'int inline;' is valid. (__inline/__inline__ stay keywords.)
- typeof: C23 keyword; clang has it as KEYGNU|KEYC23, so it is a keyword in the gnu* modes and in c23, but NOT in strict -std=c99/c11/c17, where 'int typeof;' is valid. (__typeof/__typeof__ stay keywords in all modes -- see the gcc-typeof-aliases memory.)
- constexpr: C23 keyword. In -std=c17 and earlier, 'int constexpr = 5;' is valid.

typeof_unqual follows typeof. This matters for real-world c89 and c99 headers that use these words as member or parameter names.
design: Gate on StandardFeatures (slate-parser-47s.1), keeping the double-underscore spellings unconditional since both compilers reserve them in every mode. Note that typeof is the one case that depends on the gnu-ness of the mode, not just the version, which is a concrete reason the features struct should be built from flavor+standard rather than the standard alone.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures use each of the four words as an identifier in the modes where it is not a keyword and as a keyword where it is; results match clang in c89, c99, gnu99, c17, gnu17, and c23.
close_reason: Closed

title: Integer literal candidate types are hardcoded to the C99+ list
description:
validate.rs:720 integer_candidates() returns the C99 candidate list in every standard mode. C89 (6.1.3.2) has no long long: an unsuffixed decimal literal is int, long, unsigned long; an unsuffixed octal or hex literal is int, unsigned int, long, unsigned long. C99 and later (6.4.4.1) drop unsigned long from the unsuffixed decimal list and add long long / unsigned long long.

Repro (x86_64 linux, built 2026-09-17):
  echo 'unsigned long x = 18446744073709551615;' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c -std=c89
Observed: semantic analysis failed -- integer literal `18446744073709551615` is too large to be represented in any integer type.
Expected: accepted as unsigned long. clang -std=c89 accepts it with -Wc99-compat: 'integer literal is too large to be represented in type long, interpreting as unsigned long per C89; this literal will be ill-formed in C99 onwards'.

The same function backs both resolve_integer_literal (validate) and the IR literal typing in sema/numeric.rs:83, so the wrong list changes both diagnostics and lowered types.
design: Take the candidate list from StandardFeatures (slate-parser-47s.1) rather than branching on the standard at the call site. Also decide what to do with the LL suffix and long long type in c89 mode: clang and gcc both accept them as extensions there, which by the _BitInt precedent argues for accepting without gating -- but the unsuffixed candidate list still differs and must be gated.
acceptance_criteria: A FileCheck fixture pins unsuffixed decimal, octal, and hex literals at the int/long/unsigned-long/long-long boundaries across c89, c99, and c23; results match clang in each mode.
close_reason: Closed

title: Derive a StandardFeatures struct from LanguageStandard
description:
LanguageStandard exposes ad-hoc predicates (stdc_version, has_control_scopes, is_c23_or_later, allows_implicit_int) that callers in the lexer, parser, and sema each query directly. The rest of slate-parser-47s adds roughly a dozen more such questions, which would scatter is_c23_or_later() calls across three layers. Derive one StandardFeatures value from LanguageStandard (and CompilerFlavor, since clang and gcc accept many features as extensions outside their standard) and thread that instead of the enum.

Each field is a named language question, not a version comparison: keyword_restrict, keyword_typeof, keyword_constexpr, unsuffixed_decimal_candidates, enumerators_must_fit_int, allows_knr_definitions, allows_digit_separators, u8_string_element, and so on. The struct is the single place that records whether a feature is standard, an accepted extension, or rejected -- the three-way distinction _BitInt already needed.
design: One struct built once per TranslationUnit, carried beside standard rather than replacing it (the raw standard is still needed for __STDC_VERSION__ and diagnostics text). Fields are behavior-named so a reader never has to know which standard introduced what. Extension acceptance is a tri-state (Standard | Extension | Rejected) so a later -pedantic implementation has somewhere to hang its warning, as slate-parser-jgf will need for _BitInt.
acceptance_criteria: StandardFeatures is constructed from LanguageStandard + CompilerFlavor; lexer, parser, and sema read fields from it rather than calling is_c23_or_later/allows_implicit_int/has_control_scopes directly; existing standard-mode fixtures still pass byte-identically.
notes:
Implemented 2026-09-17 as src/standard_features.rs.

Deviation from the acceptance criteria as written: StandardFeatures::new takes LanguageStandard only, not LanguageStandard + CompilerFlavor. None of the nine fields migrated here varies by flavor, and an unused parameter is worse than adding one when it earns its place. slate-parser-47s.3 is where flavor first matters (typeof is a keyword in the gnu modes and c23 but not in strict c99/c11/c17), so it adds the parameter along with keyword_typeof.

Fields are split between Availability (a diagnosable acceptance question: may source use this construct) and bool (a semantic rule that is always one way or the other). keyword_bool_true_false / keyword_nullptr / keyword_static_assert / keyword_thread_local / implicit_int are Availability; control_statement_scopes / auto_type_inference / empty_parens_are_prototype / main_implicit_return_zero are bool.

Availability::Extension has no constructor yet -- every feature migrated here is Standard or Rejected. Its first real user is keyword_typeof in 47s.3.

LanguageStandard keeps stdc_version (still needed for the __STDC_VERSION__ macro value in pp); has_control_scopes, is_c23_or_later, and allows_implicit_int are gone, and nothing references them.

Also dropped the redundant c23 parameter from Lowerer::parameters: both callers passed the value already reachable as self.types.empty_parens_are_prototype.
close_reason: StandardFeatures lands in src/standard_features.rs; lexer, parser, const_expr, and sema read its fields; has_control_scopes / is_c23_or_later / allows_implicit_int removed from LanguageStandard with no remaining references. Flavor deferred to 47s.3 per the notes. Fixture corpus byte-identical (two pre-existing unrelated failures filed as slate-parser-45s).

title: Standard-mode fidelity: gate language features on c89..c23
description: From the 2026-09-17 AST/IR review. TranslationUnit.standard currently reaches only five decisions (__STDC_VERSION__, C89 control scopes, C89 implicit int, C23 f() prototypes, C99+ main fallthrough return 0, plus the C23 keyword set in the lexer). Everything else in the lexer, parser, and sema is standard-agnostic, so slate-parser accepts and types constructs differently from clang/gcc in non-default modes. This epic collects the verified divergences and the shared mechanism for expressing them. Spec pages to update in the same changes: wiki/concepts/ast-spec.md and wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md.
design: Each child states the C standard citation, the clang and gcc behavior in every affected -std mode (including the gnu variants and whether the construct is accepted as an extension), and a FileCheck fixture pinning the result. Follow the _BitInt precedent in ir-spec.md: when both compilers accept a feature as an extension in every mode with identical semantics, do NOT gate it; record that decision instead.

title: Local variable of a file-scope enum type fails IR lowering
description: `enum E { A }; int f(void) { enum E e = A; return e == A; }` fails with 'unsupported in numeric IR lowering: block scoped typedef or tag declaration' even though the tag is declared at file scope, not in the block. The declaration-lowering path in src/sema/module.rs appears to treat any local declaration whose specifiers carry a tag specifier as a block-scoped tag definition. Predates slate-parser-5i0.16; found while testing _Generic controlling expressions of enum type.
close_reason: Closed

title: Quadratic-or-worse parse time on long flat expressions
description: A single expression of N '+' terms costs superlinear time: 200 terms 0.13s, 400 0.87s, 800 6.5s, 1600 54s — roughly cubic. clang parses 5000 terms instantly. Suspect Span::cover in const_expr::Parser::node, which re-scans the whole token slice from the expression start on every binary node, plus similar cover work in the AST renderer. Surfaced while fixing slate-parser-87x; not a crash, just unusably slow on machine-generated sources.
close_reason: Fixed. The parser was never slow: the ir path over 1600 flat terms ran in 0.155s and scales linearly. The cubic cost was entirely Renderer::render_debug's format!("{:#?}"), which layers a core::fmt PadAdapter per nesting level so every byte traverses the whole chain (perf: 99.55% in PadAdapter::write_str). Span::cover, named as the suspect when filing, was not involved. render_debug now formats non-alternate and re-lays the flat form out itself. Before: 400/800/1600 terms = 0.86s/6.4s/59s. After: 0.009s/0.021s/0.048s, and 5000 terms in 0.24s. Output verified byte-identical against the previous binary across all 2524 .c fixtures.

title: Constant-fold the remaining integer constant expression forms
description: sema/assertion.rs only validates conditions whose shape ice_shape accepts; everything else is skipped silently so valid C is never rejected. Unsupported forms seen in fixtures: _Generic selection (tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-dg/stdckdint-1.c), call expressions, string/compound literals, comma operator at assertion top level. Clang treats _Generic and constant casts as integer constant expressions, so these should fold rather than be skipped. Extend TypeResolver::constant_value and ice_shape together.
close_reason: Closed

title: Expand macros that are completed by tokens following the expansion
description: expand_macros recurses on a replacement list in isolation, so a function-like macro whose '(' comes from another macro's expansion is never invoked; the remaining source tokens are unreachable during rescanning. tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-dg/c23-digit-separators-1.c leaves 'c0 ( ... )' in the AST as a call expression instead of folding to 0. GCC and clang both support this rescan. Fix needs expand_macros to push replacements back onto a shared token stream rather than recursing on a detached slice.
close_reason: expand_rescanning now carries the enclosing token stream as a tail and reports how many of its tokens an expansion swallowed, so a replacement ending mid-invocation completes out of the caller's stream. Both shapes now match clang: '#define ALIAS IDENTITY' with 'ALIAS (2)', and '#define OPEN ZERO (' with 'OPEN 1)'. gcc-dg/c23-digit-separators-1.c now expands to clang's '_Static_assert (0 == 0);' and its regenerated AST shows only the genuine abort/exit calls. Blue paint is unchanged (the disabled set keeps its insert/remove-around-recursion shape); the fixture covers a self-referential macro and re-expansion of the same macro later on a line whose earlier expansion consumed tail tokens. Splicing is avoided in the common case by expanding in isolation first and only rescanning against the tail when the result has an unbalanced '(' or a trailing function-like macro name, which keeps the benchmark exactly on baseline. Regression fixture tests/fixtures/macro-rescan-into-source.c, cross-checked with clang -std=c23. Surfaced two pre-existing problems, filed separately: slate-parser-87x (stack overflow on long expressions) and slate-parser-y5o (expansion constant factor).

title: Validate static assertions during semantic analysis
description: TranslationUnit::analyze silently skips file and block static assertions. Evaluate supported integer constant conditions with target-aware semantics, diagnose zero/invalid/unsupported conditions at their source location, preserve the AST, and erase successful assertions during IR lowering. Add generated FileCheck regressions; track broader constant-evaluation limitations separately.
notes: Paused at user request: fix underlying constant folding under slate-parser-5i0.6 first. New regression fixtures exist but expectations not generated yet.
close_reason: sema::assertion validates file- and block-scope static assertions with target-aware constant evaluation, diagnoses zero/invalid conditions at their source location, preserves the AST, and erases assertions during IR lowering. Conditions outside the supported ICE shapes are skipped rather than diagnosed to avoid false positives on valid C (_Generic, unexpanded macro calls); tracked as slate-parser-byw and slate-parser-vxc. Closed layout gaps found by the new sizeof coverage: non-plain string literal lengths now re-encode per encoding, and _BitInt(N) gets a bit-precise storage layout. Both cross-checked against clang. Generated FileCheck regressions: tests/fixtures/sema/static_assert_validation.c and ir_static_assert.c.

title: Lower function decay and indirect calls
description: slate-parser-lh7.2.6 mentions function decay as metadata, but sema still rejects function values and indirect calls ('function value or indirect call' at src/sema/expression.rs:297). Acceptance criteria for 7.2.6 (buffer cursor, string walk, out-param) pass without it, so it was deferred. Needs: function designator decay to ptr<fn> value, indirect call through function pointers, and a fixture like tests/fixtures/sema/ir_indirect_calls.c.
close_reason: Closed

title: Prepare AST and label resolution for control-flow lowering
description: Audit before slate-parser-lh7.2.4 found four concrete gaps (all corresponding C inputs accepted by clang -std=gnu23): (1) parser/stmt.rs scans for the first colon/ellipsis in a case label, so case 1 ? 2 : 3: fails; use expression-aware boundaries, including GNU range endpoints. (2) StmtKind only has Attribute(Vec<Attribute>) for attribute-only statements; attributes before a non-null statement are routed to declaration parsing and rejected. Preserve attributed statement attachment, including labels, and align ast-spec with the actual representation. (3) sema/names.rs ignores LocalLabelDecl and uses one function label table, rejecting two sibling blocks with separate __label__ done declarations. (4) collect_labels does not traverse expression-contained statements, so return ({ goto done; done: 1; }); fails name resolution. AST already retains local declarations and statement expressions; the last two are resolver gaps, not missing syntax. Add generated FileCheck coverage and fix these prerequisites before IR work. Audit probes are in /tmp/slate-control-audit.c for this session.
acceptance_criteria: Conditional case expressions/range endpoints and attributed control statements parse with correct structure; GNU local labels resolve to distinct bindings and labels inside statement expressions resolve; existing control-body and scope fixtures pass. No loop or switch canonicalization.
close_reason: Fixed all four audit prerequisites: case expressions and GNU range endpoints now parse via the expression parser instead of the first-colon scan; attributed statements keep attachment through a new StmtKind::Attributed wrapper; GNU local labels get block-scoped resolution with shadowing and duplicate/unresolved diagnostics; labels are discovered inside statement expressions, initializers, types, and asm operands. Generated FileCheck fixtures cover each; existing control-body and scope fixtures pass. No IR work done.

title: Select Windows MSVC OS/ABI profiles and predefines
description: Add explicit OS and ABI environment selection for existing Linux targets and experimental 64-bit Windows MSVC targets. Wire checked-in compiler-specific Windows predefines, preserving Linux behavior. Microsoft aggregate layout and full cl.exe support are explicitly out of scope.
close_reason: OS/ABI environment selection and experimental 64-bit Windows predefine wiring verified by five generated fixtures, minimal preprocessing probe, and release suite. Full MSVC semantics deferred to slate-parser-lh7.1.21.

title: Inline structural types and remove redundant direct function type entries
description: The module dump emits anonymous pointer, array, and direct function type entries even where uses can render structurally and direct fn declarations already carry full signatures. Inline structural types at uses, retain named and recursive identities, and ensure direct functions do not add dead type entries.
acceptance_criteria: Direct extern function signatures appear once; pointer and array uses print inline; named/recursive types retain references; generated FileCheck and release suite pass.
close_reason: Structural pointer, array, and function types are inline; direct functions no longer emit redundant type entries; release FileCheck passes

title: Add compact IR display flag
description: Add an opt-in human-readable IR dump mode that omits conversion reasons and operation policy annotations recursively while preserving typed operations and the existing default FileCheck format.
acceptance_criteria: --compact-ir works with ir and parse --dump-ir, recursively prints typed operations without reason/overflow/rounding/exception policy fields, rejects use without module IR mode, and existing default fixtures remain unchanged.
close_reason: Added opt-in compact module IR display with recursive omission of policy annotations, FileCheck fixture, and documentation; default dump remains unchanged.

title: Use typed compiler-argument rules in option resolution
description: Replace Clap and duplicate raw-string resolution with a declarative compiler-option parser. Canonical flag definitions derive positive/negative single- and double-dash spellings, preserve last-write-wins state, parse typed values, and expose unified downstream settings. Describe mutually exclusive option groups in the schema/rules so GCC and Clang stack-alignment spellings apply through one semantic path.
design: Use canonical option specs as the source of truth for spellings, opposites, value parsing, and semantic keys. Rules validate the parsed typed state after occurrence folding. CompilerOptions must not inspect raw argv.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler flags and values have one declarative definition; positive/negative spellings resolve to one canonical state with last occurrence winning; preferred stack boundary and stack alignment are mutually exclusive but both produce the same validated TargetInfo alignment; compiler argument FileCheck fixtures pass.
close_reason: Replaced duplicate raw-string resolution with canonical Opt parsing and typed CompilerOptions construction; FileCheck passes.

title: Target-family layouts for x86, AArch64, and ARM32
description: Extend TargetInfo and layout rules beyond x86_64 SysV to the x86, AArch64, and 32-bit ARM target families. Define each family's data model, scalar widths and alignments, pointer layout, long-double representation, ABI-specific aggregate rules, and compiler-specific target behavior needed by record layout and compiler-argument validation.
design: Keep target-family policy in TargetInfo/layout descriptions rather than scattering triple checks through sema. Add family-specific behavior incrementally behind target-triple selection and preserve x86_64 SysV behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Each target family can be selected by target triple; scalar and aggregate layout fixtures cover representative structs, unions, arrays, pointers, and long double; results are checked against clang's target-specific layout output with generated FileCheck expectations.
notes: Initial scope requested alongside record layout and local _Alignas/aligned application.
close_reason: Implemented target-family layouts and predefines; generated FileCheck fixtures pass; all 66 record layouts match clang across six triples; clippy, fmt, release nextest and diff checks pass.

title: Refresh README around compiler pipeline
description: Update the README to document the supported lexing, preprocessing, parsing, semantic analysis, and IR pipeline, link each stage to relevant source files, remove polyvariant macro references, describe textual IR metadata with a simple add example, and document CLI flags.
close_reason: Updated README with current pipeline, IR example, and CLI documentation

title: Differential IR execution oracle
description: Preserve the original 2lv IR-interpreter workflow and its existing tasks: pinned Clang executable comparison, freestanding generated corpus, interpreter and observation hooks. This track requires lowering and semantic validation; the sibling structural AST oracle does not.
acceptance_criteria: IR interpreter observations match pinned Clang for the generated corpus; minimized regressions run in nextest without Clang.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add module dump for scalar function bodies
description: Introduce spanned module/function/statement IR and CLI dump, lowering zero-parameter scalar and void functions with numeric expression statements and explicit return conversions. Verify with generated FileCheck fixtures. Remaining declarations and places stay in the parent epic.
close_reason: Implemented structured module dump, scalar/void functions, blocks, linkage, return conversions and generated FileCheck coverage. Clippy, fmt, nextest and direct ir CLI smoke check pass.

title: Finish numeric IR bool promotions and casts
description: Continue conversion enums WIP; lower bool promotion and casts between bool, integer and floating types, generate FileCheck coverage and update IR spec.
close_reason: Implemented bool casts, promotions, scalar conversions and generated FileCheck coverage; full test gate passed.

title: Interpret compiler builtins and the oracle observe hook natively
description: Builtins have no C definition, so implement them in the interpreter (ideally as IR ops): __builtin_va_start/arg/end/copy (abstract list of promoted values), alloca, __builtin_unreachable/trap, overflow builtins, clz/ctz/popcount/bswap, object_size, constant_p. Hints (expect, prefetch, assume_aligned) are dropped or metadata. Also implement the harness observe hook. No libc functions are interpreted or shimmed.
acceptance_criteria: Generated corpus programs that use builtins run without libc; unsupported builtins surface as explicit unsupported errors.
close_reason: Closed

title: IR interpreter core: memory model, control flow, UB traps
description: Tree-walking interpreter over IR modules. Byte-addressed memory with allocation IDs and offsets laid out from sema-computed record layouts; supports places (local/global/deref/field/index), ptr_offset/ptr_diff, ptr_to_int/int_to_ptr, unions, bit-fields, struct copy, VLA extents. Integer and float ops at concrete widths, f80/f128 via rustc_apfloat. Reads required semantics only, never metadata. Operations marked undefined (signed overflow, div by zero, out-of-range shift, out-of-bounds access, unreachable) trap with a located error. Grows alongside lh7: starts once functions, locals, return, and calls exist, with main's exit code as the observable.
design: Decide early how to execute goto into nested statements, switch cases nested in other statements (Duff's device), and computed goto: flatten bodies to blocks inside the interpreter, or support resumption at a label. setjmp/longjmp, signals, threads, volatile/atomic out of scope initially.
acceptance_criteria: Every IR construct lowering emits is either interpreted or reported as unsupported with a Result error; no panics.
close_reason: Closed

title: Generate compiler attribute tables from authoritative sources
description: Build a standalone attribute metadata generator, modeled after slate-intrinsic-gen, that ingests authoritative compiler sources (primarily LLVM Attr.td plus documented GNU and MSVC inventories), extracts compiler flavor, namespace, spelling form, arguments, subjects, and availability, and emits checked-in Rust tables consumed by the parser. Keep this outside the AST-fidelity epic. Support reproducible regeneration from a pinned LLVM checkout/revision, source provenance in generated output, and separate overlays for attributes unavailable in Attr.td. The parser should use generated metadata to recognize GNU, Clang, C23, MSVC/__declspec, and keyword spellings while preserving unknown attributes. Add CI or a verification command that detects stale generated tables without requiring network access.

title: Hook numeric semantic flags and target long double into lowering
description: Thread grouped numeric compiler configuration through parser and TranslationUnit into sema. Resolve signed overflow and independent FP rounding/exceptions, target long double formats and corresponding predefines; generated fixtures verify ordering and direct target precision. Other flag families and scoped pragmas remain follow-ups.

Preserve full spans on IR nodes, expose an expression dump, and add generated FileCheck fixtures under tests/fixtures/sema. Update architecture docs; conversions, full module lowering, and flag/pragma integration remain in existing follow-up issues.
close_reason: Implemented direct AST-to-typed-IR numeric seed under src/sema, preserved full node spans/provenance, added expression/span dumps and generated fixtures in tests/fixtures/sema, and updated architecture docs. cargo clippy --allow-dirty --fix, cargo fmt, cargo nextest run, and git diff --check passed.

title: Extend compiler flag wiki with semantic categories and examples
description: Document agreed dropping of optional transformation permissions, FP environment responsibility split, extensible semantic categories, and illustrative IR/Rust examples.
close_reason: Documented semantic categories, extension rules, examples, dropped permissions, and existing Rust FP analysis responsibilities; git diff --check passed.

close_reason: Recorded discussion notes and open questions in wiki/concepts/compiler-flags.md; linked index and added llog entry. Documentation diff checks passed.

title: Keep fixed underlying type on opaque enum declarations
description: C23 'enum E : unsigned char;' (no body) declares an enum with a fixed underlying type, but TagSpecifier::Reference { kind, name } has nowhere to hold it, so the ': unsigned char' is dropped. ixa.12 only covers enum definitions (TagBody::Enum.fixed_type). Repro: enum E : unsigned char; enum E x; — sema/IR need the underlying type for sizeof(enum E) before the definition is seen. Needs an ast-spec change (Reference or a separate opaque enum declaration form).
close_reason: Preserved fixed underlying types on opaque enum references through AST, parser, sema, reachability, documentation, and FileCheck coverage.

title: Coalesce CommentGroup into a single merged Comment node
description: CommentGroup previously held Vec<Comment> (one entry per physical comment, each with text/kind/loc). Changed to hold a single Comment { text: Vec<String>, loc } representing the whole coalesced block: loc spans from the start of the first comment to the end of the last (covering blank lines between them), text keeps each original comment's raw text as a list entry (avoids embedding raw newlines in Debug output), and CommentKind (Line/Block) was dropped since a merged block can mix styles.
close_reason: Implemented: CommentGroup.comment: Comment { text: Vec<String>, loc: Loc } replaces the old Vec<Comment>/CommentKind shape; src/ast.rs and src/parser/mod.rs updated, all fixtures regenerated via tools/update_filecheck.py, cargo nextest passes.

description: Document proposed concrete representations for C for/while/do-while, goto, switch/case/fallthrough, enums, structs and unions in ir-shape.md. Preserve structured control flow with resolved targets and concrete aggregate layouts; defer function design.

design:
## Assessment (2026-09-15)

Mostly implemented as infrastructure, but not complete against the literal acceptance criterion. Do not build a second sema renderer.

The architecture changed since this ticket was created: src/sema directly produces typed IR, with no intermediate typed AST. The canonical semantic dump is the existing IR module dump. The parent epic's old description of a separate sema tree is superseded by its architecture notes and wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md.

Existing implementation:
- src/main.rs accepts "ir <file>" and "parse <file> --dump-ir"; both call sema::resolve_module and Module::display(show_metadata).
- src/sema/module.rs lowers zero-parameter scalar/void function definitions, expression statements, returns with explicit conversions, and nested blocks.
- src/ir/module.rs owns Module, Function, Statement, and the NodeId-keyed Metadata table.
- src/ir/module_print.rs prints modules, type declarations, globals, function signatures/bodies, and optional metadata.
- src/ir/mod.rs prints nested Value operations and optional per-value metadata through display_metadata.
- --dump-ir-expressions and --dump-ir-names already supply focused diagnostic views. They are not separate authoritative semantic representations.
- tests/filecheck.rs and tools/update_filecheck.py both understand SLATE-FILECHECK-ARGS, including --dump-ir and --show-metadata. Both also support SLATE-FILECHECK-EXAMPLE for constructed IR examples.
- tests/fixtures/sema/ir_module.c checks module boundaries, nested blocks, concrete types, integer/float return conversions, linkage, and required operation semantics.
- tests/fixtures/sema/ir_module_metadata.c checks optional function metadata.
- examples/ir_module.rs exercises expanded declaration nodes and nested metadata. It constructs IR directly; it does not prove C-to-IR lowering of add.c.

Verification during this analysis:
1. python3 tools/update_filecheck.py tests/fixtures/sema/ir_module.c tests/fixtures/sema/ir_module_metadata.c tests/fixtures/sema/numeric_seed.c tests/fixtures/sema/unsupported.c exited 0 with no diff. This verifies regeneration matches committed expectations for these fixtures; it is not a full FileCheck suite run.
2. The built CLI produced byte-identical stdout and exit code 0 for "ir tests/fixtures/sema/ir_module_metadata.c --show-metadata" and "parse ... --dump-ir --show-metadata".
3. cargo run --quiet -- ir tests/fixtures/add.c exited 1: "unsupported in numeric IR lowering: module declaration".
4. add.c contains a stdio declaration, parameters, a local, identifier reads, calls, strings, varargs, and implicit main return. These need lh7.2.2 lowering. That ticket already explicitly owns end-to-end add.c acceptance.

## Scope decision

Use the existing ir command and --dump-ir fixture flag as the semantic dump mode. Do not add "sema" merely to satisfy the example command in the original description; it was illustrative. Do not introduce a second node hierarchy, copied typed AST, Debug dump, or renderer-only inference of semantic facts.

Complete and document the renderer/test contract below using the current lowering slice. Keep full add.c lowering in lh7.2.2. Original acceptance still names add.c, so do not claim it passes based on a constructed example or name dump. If closing this infrastructure ticket before lh7.2.2, explicitly revise acceptance to the supported real-C arithmetic fixture and record that full add.c coverage is owned by lh7.2.2; otherwise leave it open until that existing integration criterion passes.

No dependence on completion of target layout is needed to test the renderer. Print Module.target as currently implemented, and adopt lh7.1.1's compact storage block when that ticket changes the target model.

## Interface and ownership contract

Reuse these existing interfaces:

```rust
pub fn resolve_module(unit: &TranslationUnit) -> Result<Module, ResolveError>;

pub type Metadata = HashMap<NodeId, Vec<(String, String)>>;

impl Module {
    pub fn display(&self, show_metadata: bool) -> DisplayModule<'_>;
}
```

The signatures above illustrate the existing API; ResolveError currently comes from sema::numeric. No public API redesign is required for this ticket.

- Parsing retains source structure and spans.
- Sema assigns concrete types, inserts conversions, resolves operation behavior, and captures available source metadata.
- The printer only reads those results. It does not inspect compiler flags or recompute conversions/types.
- Module owns the target and shared declarations; each node keeps its existing Span/NodeId.
- Required semantics belong in typed node fields. Do not move overflow, rounding, exception behavior, linkage, or storage duration into optional string metadata.
- Optional source metadata uses the existing ordered per-node vector. Traverse nodes structurally and look up by NodeId; never iterate the HashMap to determine output order.
- Do not add speculative per-node facts absent from sema. Full typedef chains, macro provenance capture, future layout metadata, and future operation coverage remain in their owning tasks.
- Source metadata must propagate to nested values, not only expression roots. Reuse the existing Value::display_metadata path.
- Preserve the existing numeric formatting, including exact non-f64 float handling and NaN bit patterns.

The default module dump is semantically readable without optional metadata. With --show-metadata, append available source annotations at their owning nodes, escaping quotes, backslashes, and newlines. This flag must not change types, operations, conversions, ordering, or control flow.

## CLI contract

Canonical commands:
```sh
slate-parser ir input.c
slate-parser ir input.c --show-metadata
slate-parser parse input.c --dump-ir
slate-parser parse input.c --dump-ir --show-metadata
```

The two spellings for each module mode must have identical output and failure behavior.

Existing rules to retain:
- Module, expression, and name dump modes are mutually exclusive.
- --show-metadata requires module IR mode.
- --show-spans currently requires --dump-ir-expressions.
- --show-ids is an AST rendering option; it is not the same as IR binding IDs.
- Parse/early validation/lowering failures return nonzero and diagnostics on stderr.
- Unsupported IR lowering must not fall back to AST output or silently omit unsupported constructs.
- Lower the whole requested module before printing, so a lowering failure cannot produce a successful-looking partial module on stdout.

Adding spans to module printing is not required here. Do not introduce a generic display-options framework solely for this ticket. Preserve current supported modes and document their distinctions.

## Text contract and worked C example

Use the existing nested expression syntax and four-space indentation. A scalar arithmetic function already fits the supported lowering slice:

```c
int add(void) {
    return 1 + 2;
}
```

Its function section must be:

```text
fn %0 @add() -> i32 [linkage=external] {
    return add<i32, overflow=undefined>(const<i32>(1), const<i32>(2));
}
```

This section appears inside "module { ... }" after the effective target header. Do not fold the addition just for prettier output: the numeric seed currently represents the operation. The printer must reflect actual IR.

A conversion example exercises recursive printing:

```c
long promoted(void) {
    return (short)1 + 2;
}
```

On the current LP64 default, the function section is expected to have this shape:

```text
fn %0 @promoted() -> i64 [linkage=external] {
    return widen<i64, reason=return>(add<i32, overflow=undefined>(widen<i32, reason=promotion>(truncate<i16, reason=explicit, fits=always>(const<i32>(1))), const<i32>(2)));
}
```

Generate and inspect the actual output when implementing; do not paste illustrative text into CHECK directives. The required observations are explicit cast narrowing, integer promotion, i32 addition with overflow policy, and i64 return conversion. C types and conversion reasons must not be inferred by the renderer.

Optional source metadata currently prints, for example:

```text
fn %0 @answer() -> i32 [linkage=internal] [c_storage="static"] [c_return="Integer(Ranked { rank: Int, signed: true })"] {
    return const<i32>(42);
}
```

That is the existing spelling, not a new recommended Debug-based semantic format. A later C-type metadata design may improve source-type spelling. This renderer task should not invent a replacement C type model.

Stable rules:
- Preserve declaration/type-table/function order and statement/source order within bodies.
- Use %N for bindings and @typeN for existing type references; keep numeric IDs deterministic for the same input/configuration.
- Print required operation properties even with metadata off.
- Do not introduce generated temporaries or LLVM instruction syntax.
- Output must not depend on HashMap order, wall clock, process ID, or temporary directory names. Optional locations may use stable file IDs; fixture-only path normalization must be narrow.

## FileCheck integration and concrete remaining mismatch

Use existing directives, not a new mode directive:

```c
// SLATE-FILECHECK-DEFINES IR
// SLATE-FILECHECK-ARGS --dump-ir

int add(void) {
    return 1 + 2;
}
```

For metadata coverage, use a separate small fixture with "--dump-ir --show-metadata", or reuse the existing metadata fixture. SLATE-FILECHECK-ARGS applies to the whole fixture, not separately to each prefix.

Important implementation fix: argument order currently differs.
- Python render/render_error append dedicated defines, include paths, flavor, standard, and show-ID arguments before SLATE-FILECHECK-ARGS.
- Rust run_fixture/run_error_fixture put SLATE-FILECHECK-ARGS first.
Repeated options can therefore select different effective configurations when generating expectations versus running FileCheck.

Choose one documented order and implement it identically. Recommended: dedicated configuration options first, then SLATE-FILECHECK-ARGS in source order, preserving order within that list. Thus explicit extra args have final precedence where the CLI supports last-option-wins behavior. Do not sort arguments or convert them to a map.

Also make error-fixture configuration propagation match successful fixtures and the Python generator:
- run_job currently does not pass isystem or show_ids to run_error_fixture.
- error jobs initialize isystem to an empty vector even when the fixture has include-path directives.
- Thread these existing settings through the error path instead of silently losing them.
- Both runners currently split extra arguments on whitespace. Document that limitation; shell-quoted argument support is not required for this ticket.

Preserve current source stripping and error diagnostic normalization. The generator and runner use different temporary-source placement in some cases; new tests should be header-independent unless specifically checking includes. Do not broaden this task into a complete fixture-isolation rewrite.

## Implementation sequence and acceptance evidence

1. Retain and document the existing canonical module dump instead of implementing another frontend mode.
2. Fix success/error argument ordering and error-path setting propagation in tests/filecheck.rs to match tools/update_filecheck.py; change the Python side only if needed for the chosen identical contract.
3. Add a small real-C arithmetic/promotion module fixture if existing ir_module coverage does not capture the contract above. Keep the original tests/fixtures/add.c AST fixture intact.
4. Reuse existing constructed-module coverage to check nested optional metadata and declarations not yet lowered from C. Clearly distinguish this from end-to-end lowering evidence.
5. Add focused FileCheck regression configurations that expose the harness mismatch: conflicting dedicated standard versus extra -std setting with observably different output, and an error fixture whose intended error requires an isystem-provided header. Verify intended diagnostic text, not just any failure.
6. Verify default and metadata modes, explicit conversions, nested blocks, rejection of unsupported lowering, and existing CLI exclusivity. Reuse existing fixtures where they already cover a requirement; no unit tests.
7. Generate expectations with python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <changed fixtures>. Rerun without --in-place to ensure regeneration is stable.
8. Run cargo clippy --allow-dirty --fix, cargo fmt, cargo nextest run when Rust changes. SLATE_CLANG_ORACLE is a separate debugging aid, not required.
9. Update wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md with the canonical commands, fixture directives, implemented coverage, and the separation from future add.c lowering.
10. Follow repository log/commit protocol for implementation and preserve unrelated dirty changes.

Completion summary must distinguish renderer infrastructure from full add.c lowering. This analysis does not close the issue or claim the full test suite passed.

title: IR lowering: AST -> IR nodes
description: Second half of AST -> IR. Lives in src/ir/. Consumes the resolved types and metadata from src/ir/sema and emits IR: statements containing typed expression trees, concrete types shown, C information attached as metadata. Preserves semantics first, then source syntax: while/do/for/switch/goto keep their form; no optimization. Side effects (assignment, ++/--, compound assignment) are hoisted out of expressions into statements; loop-condition side effects become a statement block with a trailing condition. Pointer and array access lowers to ptr_read/ptr_write at an element offset with form and decay metadata. Design: wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md.
design: IR node types + text printer (metadata on/off) come first so every later child is FileCheck-testable. Then grow in vertical slices: functions/externs/returns -> integer arithmetic + conversions -> control flow -> side-effect hoisting -> pointers/arrays -> records/unions/enums/bit-fields -> initializers -> globals/linkage.

title: update_filecheck.py corrupts fixtures that self-#include their own filename
description:
4 gcc-torture fixtures in the wf8.7 batch use the GNU-torture-suite trick of #include-ing their own filename from inside main()'s body to replay macro-driven test cases: vfprintf-1.c, vfprintf-chk-1.c, vprintf-1.c, vprintf-chk-1.c (grep for '#include "<same-basename>.c"' inside tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/ to confirm there are no others in later batches).

Root cause: tools/update_filecheck.py's render() writes the FileCheck-stripped copy it feeds to 'cargo run -- parse' into a randomly-named temp file inside the SAME directory as the real fixture (tests/fixtures/gcc-torture/), via tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=fixture.parent). A quote-include ('#include "vfprintf-1.c"') resolves by searching the including file's own directory first, so it finds the REAL, already-checked-in tests/fixtures/gcc-torture/vfprintf-1.c (with its previous CHECK block still attached) instead of a clean copy of itself. Each --in-place regeneration pass then bakes the prior CHECK block's text into the new one as parsed Comment nodes, so the fixture balloons every time the tool re-runs on it (observed vfprintf-1.c grow past 60,000 lines after two regenerations). This makes these 4 fixtures fundamentally non-idempotent under the current tool and unsafe to include in any future bulk 'run update_filecheck.py --in-place over every fixture' pass.

Separately (related but lower-severity, not blocking): a *top-level* #include of another .c file (outside any function body) currently produces NO declarations from the included file at all in the AST dump -- confirmed with a minimal repro (main.c: '#include "other.c"' where other.c declares a global; the declaration never appears in the parse output) and with pr71626-2.c (#include "pr71626-1.c" at top level yields only pr71626-2.c's own 2 leading comments, none of pr71626-1.c's real declarations). This one is stable/deterministic (doesn't balloon) so it was left as-is and pr71626-2.c was ported with that behavior baked into its CHECK block, but the underlying cause (probably a header/outermost-file provenance filter suppressing decls from included non-header .c files) is worth understanding -- it may be intentional filtering of header noise that overreaches to real included .c sources.

Fix options for the main (exploding) bug: (a) make update_filecheck.py render its temp file in an isolated directory (e.g. tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() elsewhere, or a dedicated scratch subdir) so same-directory quote-includes can't resolve back to the real fixture, then decide what SHOULD happen for these self-include fixtures (probably 'header not found', since the isolated temp dir won't contain a same-named sibling -- would need to confirm that's an acceptable/documented outcome for this class of fixture), or (b) special-case these fixtures entirely (skip auto-regeneration, hand-maintain their CHECK blocks). Once fixed, port vfprintf-1.c, vfprintf-chk-1.c, vprintf-1.c, vprintf-chk-1.c to tests/fixtures/gcc-torture/ (they were left OUT of wf8.7's otherwise-complete batch specifically because of this).
