title: Expose semantic analysis as a TranslationUnit method
description: Refactor the semantic pass public API from a free function to TranslationUnit::analyze, keeping implementation helpers private and updating CLI call sites.
acceptance_criteria: TranslationUnit::analyze accepts -D defines and returns semantic errors; no public free-function entry point remains; CLI behavior and FileCheck coverage are unchanged; cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo clippy pass.
close_reason: Semantic analysis is exposed as TranslationUnit::analyze and the CLI uses it.

title: Implement configuration-aware semantic pass and CLI diagnostics
description: Create the first semantic-analysis pass over the evaluated concrete AST, accepting -D defines and returning multiple structured diagnostics. Hook it into the parse command so semantic errors render through the existing miette diagnostic path after parsing succeeds.
acceptance_criteria: A public semantic API accepts TranslationUnit and -D defines and returns a list of errors; conditionals are evaluated for supplied defines; independent semantic errors aggregate; parse CLI prints semantic diagnostics similarly to parser diagnostics and exits nonzero; valid fixtures remain unchanged and invalid semantic fixtures are covered by generated FileCheck.
close_reason: Implemented configuration-aware semantic validation and CLI diagnostics with aggregated errors and generated FileCheck coverage.

title: Phase 6: configuration-aware semantic validation pass
description: Add a semantic validation phase after preprocessing and AST evaluation. The pass accepts the polyvariant TranslationUnit plus a list of -D defines, evaluates the AST for that configuration, validates that the resulting concrete program is well formed, and returns a list of diagnostics instead of panicking or stopping at the first error. The phase should grow from declaration/type/name validation into broader C semantic checks while remaining separate from parsing and code generation.
design: Run eval once per requested macro configuration, then validate the monomorphic ConcreteTranslationUnit. Keep the polyvariant AST free of semantic conclusions. Represent diagnostics as structured errors with stable messages and provenance, and reserve target/type-system details for child tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A public semantic pass API accepts a TranslationUnit and -D define list and returns an ordered list of semantic errors; conditional branches are evaluated using the supplied defines before validation; multiple independent errors are reported in one run; diagnostics identify the relevant declaration or source provenance; parser behavior remains separate; generated FileCheck or equivalent integration coverage exercises valid and invalid configurations.

title: Parse record and type layout attributes
description: Extend typed attribute parsing for record and type layout attributes based on clang-ir fixtures, including aligned(integer), packed trailing placement, vector_size(integer), mode(name), and field-level packed/aligned forms where the grammar supports them.
acceptance_criteria: Known record/type layout attributes have typed enum variants and preserve source order/payloads on records, typedefs, and fields; generated FileCheck coverage uses clang-ir aligned, packed_aligned, vector, and mode examples; malformed payloads produce diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented typed record/type layout attributes with generated FileCheck coverage, including aligned, vector_size, mode, field attachment, and trailing packed placement.

title: Parse function and declaration attributes
description: Extend typed attribute parsing for GNU declaration attributes used by clang-ir, including visibility(string), section(string), weak, used, retain, noinline, always_inline, noreturn, constructor, destructor, nonnull(indices), annotate(string), target(string), alias(string), weakref(string), malloc, pure, and related declaration/function forms.
acceptance_criteria: Known function/declaration attributes have typed enum variants and attach to functions, declarations, typedefs, parameters, and fields where permitted; before/after placement and ordered lists are preserved; generated FileCheck coverage validates representative clang-ir fixtures and malformed syntax diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented typed function and declaration attributes, parameter attachment, placement handling, and generated FileCheck diagnostics.

title: Parse C23 and unknown attributes losslessly
description: Add C23 [[attribute]] spelling and an opaque/raw typed attribute fallback so unsupported attributes are retained rather than discarded. Cover deprecated(message), noreturn, nodiscard, maybe_unused, fallthrough, and namespace-qualified forms where practical.
acceptance_criteria: C23 attributes parse into typed variants when known and an opaque variant when unknown; placement and arguments are preserved; generated FileCheck coverage includes C23 fixtures and unknown attributes; malformed attribute syntax produces diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented C23 [[...]] and namespace-qualified attribute parsing, typed standard forms, unknown lossless attributes, parser diagnostics, and generated FileCheck coverage.

title: Parse packed attributes on records
description: Implement and test GNU __attribute__((packed)) on struct and union declarations, preserving it as a typed Attribute enum in the polyvariant AST.
acceptance_criteria: Attribute::Packed is present on struct and union records; generated FileCheck coverage validates the parsed polyvariant form; cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo clippy pass.
close_reason: Packed attribute parsing and generated FileCheck coverage were implemented before the attribute work was split into subtickets.

title: Parse GNU and C23 attributes into typed AST enums
description: Add source-level attribute parsing based on the attribute forms exercised by ~/Projects/clang-ir. Represent attributes as a dedicated enum with typed payloads rather than raw strings, and attach ordered attribute lists to structs, unions, enums, functions, declarations, typedefs, and fields/parameters where C permits them. Preserve unknown attributes through an explicit opaque/raw variant so parsing does not discard source information. Initial coverage should include packed, aligned(integer), visibility(string), section(string), weak, used, retain, noinline, always_inline, noreturn, constructor, destructor, nonnull(parameter indices), annotate(string), target(string), and deprecated(message). Support GNU __attribute__((...)) placement before/after declarations and C23 [[...]] spelling where practical. Use clang-ir fixtures such as packed_aligned_struct.c, aligned_struct.c, visibility/main.c, used_retain/main.c, noreturn_prototype.c, nonnull_prototype.c, allocation_attribute_metadata.c, and c23_language.c as parser references.
design: Use a Vec<Attribute> on each declaration-like AST node rather than booleans scattered across node types. Keep semantic interpretation out of parsing. Model attributes with typed enum variants for known forms and preserve unsupported forms in Raw/Opaque(String) so extensions remain lossless.
acceptance_criteria: Attributes are represented by a public typed enum with explicit payloads and an opaque fallback; representative attributes parse on structs/unions/enums, functions, declarations, typedefs, fields, and parameters; source order and placement are preserved in the AST; generated FileCheck fixtures cover GNU and C23 forms and unknown attributes; malformed attribute syntax produces diagnostics; cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo clippy pass.
notes:
Packed slice implemented: Attribute::Packed is parsed on struct/union prefixes and preserved in polyvariant rendering, with generated FileCheck coverage in tests/fixtures/packed.c. Remaining work includes trailing placement and other attribute variants.
Work split into child tickets 1tx.1 through 1tx.4. Child 1tx.1 (packed records) is complete; remaining attribute families are tracked separately.
close_reason: Typed GNU/C23 attributes, opaque/invalid preservation, placement handling, and generated attribute fixtures are implemented; release FileCheck passes.

Ensure the oracle comparison reflects only declarations visited by the evaluated AST and add regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Polyvariant output is not compared to clang; evaluated output is compared to clang under each define configuration; unvisited conditional declarations do not cause mismatches; tests pass.
close_reason: Separated evaluated AST oracle naming and documented the preprocessing/evaluation comparison boundary; verified reachability behavior.

title: Set miette parser diagnostics to C syntax highlighting

close_reason: Removed the redundant eval_translation_unit wrapper; callers now invoke TranslationUnit::eval directly.

title: Move declaration and declarator helpers onto AST impls
close_reason: Moved declaration, declarator, condition, conditional, translation-unit, declaration, and statement evaluation helpers onto their owning types; all checks pass.

title: Filter AST to reachable declarations
description: Included headers currently inject every typedef/declaration into the rendered translation unit. Add a reachability pass so the public polyvariant/concrete AST contains primary-source roots plus transitive declarations needed by referenced names, types, tags, calls, and conditional branches. Preserve the full include environment internally for lookup, but omit unused header declarations such as ULONG_MAX_TYPE and MyConfigType from includes.c.
design: Use provenance to distinguish primary-file roots from included declarations. Index declarations by symbol/tag. Traverse identifiers and type references from roots, recursively marking dependencies. Treat conditional branches as a union for polyvariant reachability; concrete evaluation may then remove inactive branches. Keep macro definitions/preprocessor state separate from declaration reachability.
acceptance_criteria: Unused declarations from included headers are absent from FileCheck output; a source declaration that references a header typedef/tag/prototype retains that dependency; reachability is computed over all possible conditional branches before concrete evaluation and rechecked after branch selection.
notes: Added src/reachability.rs and applied it during parsing. Primary-file declarations are roots; included declarations are indexed by symbol and retained only when referenced through named/ tagged types, pointers, arrays, function return types, or parameters. Conditional branches are filtered after reachability is computed, so possible branch dependencies remain polyvariant and inactive concrete branches disappear. Updated includes.c to prove unused header typedefs are omitted and added includes_reachable.c to prove a referenced header typedef is retained. Clang comparison now requires every exposed summary to exist in clang while intentionally ignoring clang-only unused header declarations. Validation: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, generator freshness, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Reachability filtering implemented and fixture coverage proves unused includes are omitted while referenced typedef dependencies remain.

title: Expand clang oracle coverage for Phase 3 AST shapes
description: Extend the clang comparison tests beyond summarized returns/typedefs to compare normalized declarations, types, declarators, records, arrays, function pointers, and initializers. Pin normalization to the clang version documented by the project.
acceptance_criteria: Each implemented Phase 3 slice has a clang-backed regression test and normalization clearly documents intentionally ignored clang-only details.
notes: The oracle comparison intentionally does not require our AST to mirror clang. It normalizes both sides to semantic facts: declaration identity, base type, array extents, function-vs-function-pointer category, return-pointer status, parameter types, variadicness, typedef types, and evaluated returns. Clang qualType spelling is only an input to this normalization; our FileCheck output remains our own AST shape. This lets clang expose missing behavior without making its AST schema our design.
close_reason: Clang oracle normalizes and compares Phase 3 declarations, types, declarators, records, arrays, function signatures/pointers, initializers, and evaluated returns

title: Parse initializers and designated initializers

acceptance_criteria: Representative initializer forms parse and preserve source order/designators; clang-backed tests cover nested aggregates and designated fields.

title: Implement integer constant expressions for grammar decisions

acceptance_criteria: Supported constant expressions fold consistently with clang for grammar-dependent cases, and unsupported expressions produce explicit diagnostics rather than silent values.
notes: Audit confirms case labels are implemented; old parser blocker is stale. Static assertion validation tracked in slate-parser-33i (in progress). Remaining acceptance gaps reported by read-only audit: preprocessor operator precedence and unsigned comparisons silently misfold, enum casts silently discard narrowing; cross-enum identifiers and enum array bounds explicitly unsupported. Keep this issue open pending independent reproduction and fixes.

Verbatim AST preservation is unaffected; five stale parser fixtures regenerated through tools/update_filecheck.py. Probes match clang: #if 1|2^3, #if -1<1U, enum (unsigned char)257 -> 1. Static assertion validation (slate-parser-33i) remains open and now has correct folding primitives to build on.

title: Parse struct union and enum declarations
description: Add parse-only support for struct/union/enum definitions, forward declarations, fields, enumerators, anonymous records, and references. Track tags and typedef names sufficiently for grammar disambiguation.
acceptance_criteria: Representative record/union/enum declarations parse and match the corresponding clang AST structure; conditional declarations remain represented polyvariantly.
close_reason: Added parse-only struct, union, enum definitions, fields, forward declarations, anonymous records, tag references, typedef-tag aliases, rendering, reachability, and fixture/oracle coverage.

title: Parse arrays and function pointer declarators
description: Add postfix array declarators, multidimensional arrays, parameter lists, function declarators, pointer-to-function and function-returning-pointer composition, including parameter declarations.
acceptance_criteria: Nested array and function-pointer declarations parse with unambiguous AST structure and clang-oracle tests cover declaration permutations.
notes: Implemented declarator parsing in src/parser.rs and lexer support for char/void, pointers, brackets, commas, and ellipses. Added Declaration/ConcreteDecl integration, arrays, multidimensional arrays, function parameter lists, variadics, pointer-to-function, and function-returning-pointer coverage. Added clang type-spelling oracle tests. Validation: cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings pass.

title: Phase 3: full C declarator/type grammar
description: Expand the parser from the Phase 2 conditional/macro surface to the Phase 3 parse-only C grammar described in README.md. Keep the AST polyvariant and defer ordinary type checking to Phase 6. Validate each slice against clang AST output.
design: Implement grammar in dependency order: shared type/declarator representation, records/enums, arrays/function pointers, qualifiers/storage, initializers/designators, then constant-expression folding. Use comment-embedded FileCheck AST expectations for readable fixture tests.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 3 grammar work is decomposed into independently testable parser slices; all slices preserve conditional AST branches and have clang-backed coverage.
close_reason: Closed

title: AST foundation: C types and declarators
description: Define the polyvariant AST representation for named/tagged types, pointers, arrays, function types, qualifiers, storage classes, and declarator composition. Preserve source/provenance and conditional branches without adding sema.
acceptance_criteria: The AST can represent every Phase 3 declarator/type shape needed by downstream parser slices, with structural unit tests.
notes: Added the Phase 3 AST foundation in src/ast.rs: richer CType variants for primitive/named/tagged/qualified/pointer/array/function types, declarator composition, parameters, qualifiers, storage classes, declaration specifiers, and deferred array-size expressions. Added structural unit tests. Updated the existing clang oracle normalization to remain exhaustive while dedicated Phase 3 oracle work is pending. Validation: cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings pass.
close_reason: AST type/declarator foundation and structural tests implemented; cargo test and clippy pass.

title: Model memory-constrained asm operands as addresses, not loaded values
description: IR lowering reads an "m"-constrained input operand as a value (`in 2 "0,m" read<i32>(deref(read<ptr<i32>>(%4)))`), which implies a load happens before the asm. A memory operand means the assembler addresses the object itself; the asm may read or write it at any point. Slate needs the address (and the fact that the object is clobbered) to translate this, not a snapshot load. Multi-alternative constraints make this conditional on which alternative the register allocator picks, so the IR probably has to carry both forms or defer the choice.
acceptance_criteria: Memory-constrained asm operands lower to a form that identifies the addressed object rather than a pre-asm load; sema/ir_asm.c covers an "m" input and an "=m" output.

title: Lower __builtin_shufflevector and __builtin_convertvector
description: tests/fixtures/vector_extension_ops.c fails IR lowering with 'unsupported Clang builtin __builtin_shufflevector'. Both builtins are CustomTypeChecking with generic vector operands and a result type derived from the mask length / target type, so neither fits the derived-signature shapes added in dyd.19: shufflevector takes a vector pair plus constant lane indices and yields a vector of the mask's length; convertvector takes a vector and a type. Needs an IR value for a lane permutation and for a per-lane conversion.
notes:
Done (2378 -> 2379 accepted; vector_extension_ops.c was the only corpus fixture, and it also exercises the swizzles from lh7.2.17.7).

__builtin_shufflevector is CustomBuiltin::Shuffle, lowering to ValueKind::Shuffle { left, right, mask }: the constant-index form takes two vectors of the same type and any number of ICE indices over their concatenation (-1 prints as an undef lane), and the result is a vector of the element type with one lane per index, so a narrowing or widening shuffle is fine. The two-argument form takes a runtime integer mask vector of the same lane count and prints mask=dynamic(..), mirroring the existing dynamic(..) spelling for atomic orders and weak.

__builtin_convertvector needed an AST node, since its second operand is a type: ExprKind::ConvertVector { ty, value }, parsed like __builtin_va_arg. It has the same shape as Cast/BitCast/VaArg, so it joined their existing or-patterns in visit.rs, reachability.rs, sema/names.rs and sema/assertion.rs without new arms; the touchpoints page now records that. Lowering reuses the scalar conversion policy rather than restating it: Context::elementwise_conversion runs emit_arithmetic_conversion over the element types and re-types the resulting chain onto vector operands, so int_to_float/float_to_int/widen/truncate/reinterpret all carry their usual exactness and exception metadata, and an int->int conversion that needs both a resize and a reinterpret keeps both steps.

Verified against clang -ast-dump for shuffle result types (3-, 4- and 6-index forms, the dynamic mask form, GNU vectors) and for each convertvector element pair. ast-spec.md, ast-grammar.md, ast-enum-touchpoints.md, ir-spec.md and ir-grammar.md updated; tests/fixtures/sema/ir_vector.c and vector_extension_ops.c pin the forms.
close_reason: Closed

title: GCC personality: __builtin_ prefix on library builtins
description: GCC accepts __builtin_<name> for any library builtin (__builtin_exit, __builtin_puts, ...). Clang 22 rejects these: 'use of unknown builtin __builtin_exit'. Builtins.td only generates a __builtin_-prefixed alias where AddBuiltinPrefixedAlias is set (5 defs), which is why the registry has no __builtin_exit. Since we default to the Clang personality, rejecting it is currently correct and matches the oracle. Repro: tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-torture/20000105-1.c, a gcc-torture fixture running under the default (clang) flavor. Fix is a CompilerFlavor::Gcc rule in builtins::clang_builtin that strips the __builtin_ prefix and accepts a ClangBuiltinKind::Library match, plus SLATE-FILECHECK-FLAVOR gcc on that fixture. Note the fixture would then be a deliberate slate-accepts/clang-rejects divergence in the --tool both sweep. Also note the GCC semantics: the prefixed spelling bypasses -fno-builtin, which we do not model.

title: Source-location builtins __builtin_FILE/FUNCTION/LINE/COLUMN
description: __builtin_FILE, __builtin_FILE_NAME, __builtin_FUNCTION, __builtin_LINE and __builtin_COLUMN are Clang keywords (TokenKinds.def), not Builtins.td records, so the generated registry does not contain them and sema reports an unresolved ordinary name. Repro: tests/fixtures/gnu_builtin_source.c (1 configuration). Two prerequisites are missing: the enclosing function's name during lowering (shared with slate-parser-dyd.21), and column information, which ast::Provenance does not carry at all (file, kind, line, system_header only) — __builtin_COLUMN cannot be implemented until the lexer/preprocessor tracks columns.
close_reason: All five source-location builtins implemented. Position comes from the callee token's Loc through the new Files source map (Files now carries the preprocessor's line table and a position() accessor) rather than Provenance, which is stamped per logical line and so cannot supply a column. Line and column verified equal to clang.

title: Propagate builtin NoReturn/Const attributes to call sites
description: The typed registry now carries BuiltinAttribute::NoReturn, Const, Pure and NoThrow, but a builtin call lowers to a plain Callee::Builtin with only c_builtin metadata. IR noreturn lives on FunctionSemantics, which a builtin has no declaration for, so __builtin_unreachable/__builtin_abort calls are not marked as terminating. Decide whether call values carry these attributes and update ir-spec/ir-grammar with them.

title: ir::Field has no is_const, so a const record member is invisible in the IR
description: ir::Field carries an Access (volatile + atomic) but no const bit, so 'struct s { const int a; }' prints 'field0 a: i32'. Sema itself is correct: assigning to a struct with a const-qualified member is rejected exactly as clang rejects it, through the C type layer. Only the printed IR loses the fact, which matters because the IR is the handoff to Rust conversion. Found by the slate-parser-8lv.5 entity audit; documented in wiki/concepts/entity-model.md.
close_reason: ir::Field now preserves and prints const-qualified record members; fixtures and documentation updated

title: Linkage, storage duration and symbol attributes live on ir::Global, not on the entity
description: The entity record holds the declared QualType and the alignment/common request. Linkage, storage duration, definition state and symbol attributes are computed per declaration in src/sema/module.rs and merged in place on ir::Global / ir::Function by declare_global / declare_function, so module.globals is a second per-object store keyed by BindingId. The epic slate-parser-8lv listed those properties on the entity. Found by the slate-parser-8lv.5 audit; documented in wiki/concepts/entity-model.md.

title: resolve_parameters duplicates parameter lowering outside the entity table
description: src/sema/types.rs::resolve_parameters lowers ir::Parameter for the standalone resolve_type_module/resolve_module path. It has no Lowerer and so no entity table, hands out BindingIds from a counter, and re-derives restrict/is_const/access from the resolved QualType with a copy of the logic in module.rs::parameters. Found by the slate-parser-8lv.5 entity audit; documented in wiki/concepts/entity-model.md. Either give that path an entity table or factor the projection QualType -> ir::Parameter into one function both call.

title: Parameter attributes are blanket-rejected, including ones MSVC accepts
description:
src/sema lowering rejects any attribute on a function parameter with ResolveError::Unsupported("parameter attributes").

Measured 2026-09-19:
- '_Alignas(16) int p' as a parameter: clang errors ("'_Alignas' attribute cannot be applied to a function parameter"), gcc errors ("alignment specified for parameter 'p'"), MSVC 14.51 accepts it silently with /std:c17.
- 'int q __attribute__((aligned(16)))' as a parameter: clang accepts, gcc errors ("alignment may not be specified for 'q'").

By the project's three-compiler consensus rule neither case may be an error, since MSVC accepts the first and clang accepts the second. Both should lower with a named warning from src/diagnostics.rs instead, and the alignment should have no effect on the parameter.

Found while doing slate-parser-8lv.2, which relaxed the equivalent blanket rejection for automatic locals. Left out of that phase because it needs a new warning and its own oracle work, not just the entity's alignment request.

title: Brace elision decides aggregate initializer compatibility on ir::Type
description:
src/sema/initializer.rs:349 decides whether an initializer expression initializes an aggregate member whole (consuming one item) or is brace-elided into its fields by comparing unaliased ir::Type, not C types.

C23 6.7.11 makes this a compatibility question. Within one TU the two answers agree for every ordinary case, because distinct tags get distinct TypeIds and Defined(id) is nominal. They diverge for a compatible-but-separately-defined tag, e.g. a file-scope 'struct S { int x; }' and a block-scope 'struct S { int x; }': C23 says compatible (initialize whole), the IR comparison says Defined(id1) != Defined(id2) and wrongly brace-elides.

Fix: route through CTypes::compatible_unqualified. Blocked on the initializer walk being shaped over ir::Type Shape rather than QualType, which is why it was left out of slate-parser-9ve.6.

Found by the grep audit in slate-parser-9ve.6; recorded in wiki/concepts/c-type-layer.md under the invariant's residues.

title: MSVC models non-lock-free _Atomic aggregates with a lock member
description:
Measured with tools/cl.exe 14.51 /std:c17 /experimental:c11atomics on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, as size/align of _Atomic struct { char a[N]; }:

N:      1    2    3    4    5    6    7    8    9   16   17
size:   1    2    8    4   12   12   12    8   16   20   24
align:  1    ?    4    ?    4    ?    ?    ?    ?    4    4

The rule: when sizeof(T) is already a lock-free width (1, 2, 4, 8) the layout is unchanged. Otherwise MSVC prepends a 4-byte lock, giving size = 4 + round_up(sizeof(T), 4) and align 4. Every padded case measured has align 4, consistent with an int lock member leading the object.

This differs from BOTH personalities modelled in slate-parser-9ve.5: clang promotes to the next power of two (char[3] -> 4/4), gcc does not promote at all (char[3] -> 3/1), MSVC adds a lock (char[3] -> 8/4).

It is also a bigger change than clang's: it alters the object REPRESENTATION, not just size and alignment, so member offsets and the ABI are affected too, and a faithful model needs a hidden field rather than a StorageLayout adjustment.

9ve.5 deliberately left --flavor=msvc on clang's promotion rule rather than invent a half-model; it is no more wrong than before that phase. Fix here, or decide to reject _Atomic aggregates under --flavor=msvc instead of reporting a size we know is wrong. Note _Atomic is an experimental non-standard opt-in on MSVC (/experimental:c11atomics).

title: Reject taking the address of a register-qualified variable
description:
6.5.3.2p1 forbids & on an object declared with storage-class register; clang errors ('address of register variable requested'). slate-parser accepts it silently. The bit-field half of the same constraint is already rejected ('address of a bit-field').

Blocked on storage-class tracking: StorageClass::Register currently reaches sema only in validate.rs for asm labels; nothing records register-ness per BindingId. Needs a register set (or a storage class on the binding) threaded from declaration lowering, which fits the declared-entity model of slate-parser-8lv better than the conversion rules of 9ve.3.

Split out of slate-parser-9ve.3, where the rest of the 6.3.2.1/6.5.3.2 lvalue constraints landed.
close_reason: register storage is tracked per binding and address-taking now emits a semantic error for objects and parameters

title: Compound literals with variably modified types: (int (*)[n]){p}
description: lh7.2.24 captures VLA bounds for sizeof(type) and casts via ValueKind::Capture, but ExprKind::CompoundLiteral lowers to a Place (PlaceKind::CompoundLiteral), so the value-level wrapper does not reach it and '(int (*)[n]){p}' still fails with 'nonconstant or unknown identifier'. A VLA-typed compound literal itself is a constraint violation (C11 6.5.2.5p1); only pointer-to-VLA and similar variably modified element types are valid. Needs capture hoisting at the place level (or capturing in the literal's initializer).
acceptance_criteria: Fixture covers a compound literal of pointer-to-VLA type; bound evaluated once at the literal.

title: Node metadata prints twice on hoisted synthetic temporaries
description:
With --show-metadata, a value hoisted into a synthetic temporary prints its node metadata twice, e.g. from ir_atomic_stdatomic.c:
  let %N: i32 [synthetic] = update<...>(...) [c_builtin="__c11_atomic_fetch_add"] [c_macro="atomic_fetch_add_explicit"] [c_builtin="__c11_atomic_fetch_add"] [c_macro="atomic_fetch_add_explicit"];
Pre-existing before lh7.2.23 (11 duplicate pairs in that fixture then).

Cause: Hoister::declare (src/sema/effects.rs:44) builds the Statement::Temporary span from source.node.clone(), so the statement shares the initializer's NodeId. The module printer prints the initializer with display_metadata (src/ir/module_print.rs ~line 211) and then the statement's own metadata for the same NodeId, so every key appears twice. Affects any hoisted value with metadata, not just atomics.

Related noise, same root of keying metadata by NodeId: sema/atomic.rs builds inner nodes (old<T>, the arith computation) with the call's Expr, so they carry c_builtin/c_macro too, e.g. old<i32> [c_builtin=...]. Decide whether inner synthesized nodes should get their own ids or suppress metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Each metadata key prints once per hoisted temporary in ir_atomic_stdatomic.c (and other --show-metadata fixtures), with fixtures regenerated.
close_reason: IR nodes synthesized from another span take a fresh NodeId (Span::derive) and metadata is annotated on the owning IR node; hoisted temporaries and their reads no longer repeat the initializer's keys. Covered by ir_atomic_stdatomic.c and ir_metadata_single_owner.c.

title: Alignment attributes on automatic locals have no IR representation
description: Globals got [align=N] in lh7.2.22, but 'void f(void){ int x __attribute__((aligned(16))); _Alignas(32) int z; }' still fails with 'automatic variable attributes or asm label' (sema/module.rs). Statement::Let's Variable has no alignment field. Same flavor rule as globals: clang takes the request as written, gcc/MSVC max with natural.
acceptance_criteria: aligned/_Alignas on an automatic local lowers to an alignment printed on the let, covered by a FileCheck fixture.
close_reason: Automatic locals carry alignment: ir::Variable gained an alignment field, so a let prints [align=N] under the same effective_alignment flavor rule as globals, and the blanket 'automatic variable attributes' rejection now only rejects attributes that are neither vector nor alignment attributes. Verified against clang -S -emit-llvm: alloca align 16/1/32/4 for aligned(16), aligned(1), _Alignas(32) and plain. Fixture sema/ir_object_alignment_sites.c.

title: __alignof__/_Alignof of a declared object ignores its alignment attribute
description: lh7.2.22 records aligned/_Alignas on a global as Global.alignment, but alignof applied to the object still folds the type's natural alignment. Repro: printf 'int x __attribute__((aligned(16)));\nint k = __alignof__(x);\n' > t.c && target/release/slate-parser ir t.c -> k = 4; clang gives 16 (and 1 for aligned(1), per the clang-only rule that the attribute can lower a variable's alignment). The request lives in Lowerer.object_requests (sema/module.rs) and is only resolved after all redeclarations merge, so alignof needs the flavor rule from resolve_object_requests applied to the request seen so far.
acceptance_criteria: __alignof__ and _Alignof of an object with an alignment attribute fold to the same value printed as [align=N] (or natural when absent), covered by a FileCheck fixture.
close_reason: __alignof__ of a declared object now reads the object's alignment request from the sema entity instead of folding the type's natural alignment. Both the constant path (types.rs) and the runtime path (expression.rs) go through TypeResolver::object_alignment. Verified against clang 22.1.8 and gcc 16.2.1: 16/32/1 at file scope and 16/32/1/64/4 at block scope, static local and plain, all matching exactly. Fixture sema/ir_object_alignment_sites.c.

title: Model ARM ISA feature flags (aarch64 SVE, arm32 -mfpu=neon) in predefines and vector ABI
description: slate-parser-qiy added x86 ISA flags (src/target/x86_isa.rs): -m<feature>/-march resolve to TargetInfo.x86_isa, which generates the ISA/CPU predefines at configure time and sets the sysv64 vector register width. ARM targets still reject every ISA option and use baseline captured predefines (__ARM_NEON, __ARM_FEATURE_*). Do the same for aarch64 (-march=armv8-a+sve etc; aapcs64 SVE vectors) and arm32 (-mfpu=neon, -mfloat-abi), stripping the feature macros from the clang aarch64/armv7 headers and emitting them from the resolved ISA. GCC flavor parity for x86 is also partial: __FP_FAST_FMA* and __MMX_WITH_SSE__ are not generated.
close_reason: Arm ISA flags resolve into TargetInfo.isa (TargetIsa::{X86,AArch64,Arm}). AArch64: -march armv8-a..armv9.6-a with curated +ext/+noext and -msve-vector-bits; Arm32: -march armv7-a/armv8-a, -mfpu, -mfloat-abi, -mthumb/-marm. Feature macros stripped from the clang Arm headers and generated at configure; the arm32 float ABI now picks aapcs32 vs aapcs32_hard_float. Matches clang 22 on 1333 Arm combinations. GCC __FP_FAST_FMA*/__MMX_WITH_SSE__ parity not done.

title: _Atomic layout promotion is clang-only; gcc keeps the unqualified layout
description:
slate-parser-lh7.2.20 implemented clang's _Atomic layout promotion unconditionally, so a --flavor=gcc run reports clang's sizes. gcc does not promote atomic aggregates at all. Measured on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (clang 22 vs gcc 16.2.1), as size/align:

  _Atomic struct { char a[3]; }    clang 4/4    gcc 3/1
  _Atomic struct { char a[5]; }    clang 8/8    gcc 5/1
  _Atomic struct { char a[9]; }    clang 16/16  gcc 9/1
  _Atomic struct { char a[17]; }   clang 17/1   gcc 17/1
  _Atomic long long                clang 8/8    gcc 8/8

Scalars agree (natural alignment already satisfies the promotion); only aggregates diverge. gcc's choice is self-consistent: an unpromoted odd-sized atomic object cannot be accessed lock-free, so gcc routes those through libatomic.

This is a personality difference of the kind the project goal statement anticipates, not a target difference, so the feature-availability-not-target-gated memory does not apply -- it is about what the same source means to two compilers, not about whether a feature exists. CompilerFlavor currently reaches sema/validate.rs but not TypeResolver's layout path or TargetAbi, so the plumbing is the real work here.

Same root as slate-parser-lh7.2.29 (argument passing); settle the personality switch once for both.

Acceptance: the ir_atomic_layout.c fixture gains a gcc-flavor prefix whose sizes match gcc; the clang prefix keeps today's values.
notes:
Fixed in slate-parser-9ve.5. TypeResolver now carries CompilerFlavor, set in with_tags from unit.flavor, so all four resolvers (module lowering, resolve_type_module, resolve_module, assertion.rs) share it by construction. TypeResolver::promotes_atomic_layout gates the target.atomic_storage call in qualified_storage: false under Gcc.

Re-measured before implementing (clang 22.1.8 vs gcc 16.2.1, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu), matching this bead's table: _Atomic struct{char a[N];} for N=3,5,9,17 is 4/4, 8/8, 16/16, 17/1 under clang and 3/1, 5/1, 9/1, 17/1 under gcc; scalars agree. Also confirmed the divergence reaches member offsets, which the original table did not cover: struct{char head; _Atomic struct{char a[3];} value; char tail;} is size 12 align 4 offsets 0,4,8 under clang and size 5 align 1 offsets 0,1,4 under gcc. The new fixture pins both.

Acceptance met: tests/fixtures/sema/ir_atomic_layout_gcc.c carries gcc's values (a separate file rather than a prefix on the existing fixture, because SLATE-FILECHECK-FLAVOR is per-file, not per-prefix), and ir_atomic_layout.c keeps clang's unchanged.

MSVC is NOT covered: it prepends a lock word, which matches neither personality. Filed as slate-parser-rol; --flavor=msvc stays on clang's rule meanwhile.
close_reason: Closed

title: _Atomic aggregate arguments: clang passes MEMORY, gcc passes in registers
description:
clang classifies every _Atomic-qualified aggregate argument as MEMORY regardless of size; gcc classifies it exactly as the unqualified record. Measured on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (clang 22, gcc 16.2.1):

  struct s8 { char a[8]; };
  void f8(_Atomic struct s8 v);
  void p8(struct s8 v);

  clang: define void @f8(ptr noundef byval(%struct.s8) align 8)   // stack
         define void @p8(i64)                                     // register
  gcc:   f8 and p8 both take the value in %rdi

Caller side agrees: gcc emits 'movq .LC0(%rip), %rdi; call f8', clang builds the value on the stack and passes a pointer. The two are ABI-incompatible here. Atomic scalars are unaffected (_Atomic int is i32 in both).

Why it matters: ir-spec says native_c 'leaves an unclassified record to the target's ordinary C ABI for repr(C) emission ... so Rust lowering does not mistake a guessed coercion for a verified one'. A repr(C) aggregate is passed in a register by rustc, which reproduces gcc but not clang. So native_c is silently wrong for an atomic aggregate parameter under the clang personality -- the exact failure native_c exists to prevent.

Same GNU-vs-Clang personality root as the layout half in slate-parser-lh7.2.30; settle the personality switch once for both.

Acceptance: an atomic-qualified aggregate parameter does not resolve to native_c; its passing shape matches the selected flavor's compiler, pinned by a fixture against both clang and gcc output.
notes:
Re-verified independently during slate-parser-9ve.5 (clang 22.1.8, gcc 16.2.1, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu):
  clang: declare void @f8(ptr noundef byval(%struct.s8) align 8)  -- MEMORY
  gcc:   movq -16(%rbp), %rax; movq %rax, %rdi; call f8@PLT       -- register
Confirmed as described.

NOT fixed in 9ve.5. Status of the plumbing that bead asked for:
- DONE: the compiler personality now reaches AbiClassifier. It holds &TypeResolver, and TypeResolver carries CompilerFlavor as of 9ve.5, so the clang-vs-gcc switch itself needs no new plumbing.
- BLOCKER: the C type does not reach it. AbiClassifier::from_parts takes Option<&Type>/&[Type] (IR types), which have already lost _Atomic on aggregates -- _Atomic int survives as a qualifier but _Atomic struct S lowers to the same Type::Defined as struct S.

Threading QualTypes through the 7 call sites is mostly mechanical (module.rs:86/596 and expression.rs:1435 have the QualType in hand; atomic.rs:628/687 synthesize their signatures), except for types.rs:1810/1857. That is resolve_type_module, the --dump-ir-types path, which reconstructs the ABI from a finished Module and has no C types at all. Fixing it means giving that path a real TypeResolver -- the same gap the 9ve epic notes for resolve_expression_roots. That is a phase of its own, not a local change, so no speculative parameter was added here.

title: _Atomic on a variable binding is invisible in the IR dump
description:
An _Atomic-qualified object's promoted layout is computed correctly (slate-parser-lh7.2.20) but nothing in the default dump says the object is atomic, and the IR prints no size for a global or a let, so its 4/4 layout cannot be recovered from the dump:

  struct odd3 { char a[3]; };
  _Atomic struct odd3 object;
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c
  Observed: global %1 object: @type0 -- same as a plain struct odd3.

ir::Variable carries restrict but no Access. The fact reaches accesses (read<..., atomic=seq_cst>) only where the object is actually read or written; a declaration with no access in the TU carries nothing. Slate needs it to pick the Rust type (AtomicU32 vs a plain field), which is a property of the object, not of one access.

Same struct and same binding-level-qualifier theme as slate-parser-lh7.2.16 (const on a variable); settle them together.

Acceptance: a fixture declares an _Atomic global and an _Atomic local with no accesses; each prints the fact on the let/global in the default dump.
close_reason: ir::Variable and ir::Parameter gained an Access (volatile + atomic), printed as a prefix on the type exactly as a record field's already was: 'global %1 counter: atomic i32', 'let %9 flag: volatile i32', '%13 a: atomic i32'. The fact is a property of the object, so it now appears on a declaration the translation unit never reads or writes. Volatile was invisible on declarations for the same reason and is fixed by the same change. All four qualifier bits (const, restrict, volatile, atomic) derive from one qualifiers value per declaration site, and declare_global re-derives them from the merged composite on a redeclaration. Fixture sema/ir_declaration_qualifiers.c. Note: the cross-reference in this bead to lh7.2.16 as the 'const on a variable' case was stale; lh7.2.16 is about unnamed parameters.

title: sizeof of a declared object is rejected in constant expressions
close_reason: object types resolve through name resolution in the lowerer's TypeResolver; fixture sema/ir_sizeof_object_bound.c

title: Top-level const on a variable binding is dropped in the IR
description:
ir::Variable carries restrict but not const, so a top-level const on an object is lost:

  int g(void) { int x; int *const q = &x; return *q; }
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c
  Observed: let %4 q: ptr<i32> [storage=automatic] -- the const on q is gone.

Parameters now print [const] for the same fact (slate-parser-lh7.2.15); variables should match. Slate needs it to choose let vs let mut, and nothing else in the IR records it (Type::Pointer::is_const is the pointee's).

Acceptance: a fixture covers a const scalar, a const pointer object, and a const-qualified global; each prints [const] on the let/global in the default dump.
close_reason: ir::Variable.is_const from the declarator's top-level qualifiers, printed [const] on let/global

title: Accept ISA feature flags and make predefines and vector ABI follow them
description:
slate-parser has no -mavx/-march knob: compiler_args.rs (enum Opt) accepts only long-double and stack-alignment among the -m spellings, and an unrecognized option is a hard error. A target triple therefore means its baseline ISA everywhere, and two things are pinned to that baseline:

1. Predefines. src/predefines/clang-22.1.8_x86_64_linux_gnu.h defines __MMX__, __SSE__, __SSE2__ and no __AVX__; each header is a fixed capture selected in src/pp/mod.rs by (os, environment, family, flavor) via include_str!. clang -mavx adds 8 macros over baseline on x86-64 (__AVX__, __SSE3__, __SSSE3__, __SSE4_1__, __SSE4_2__, __POPCNT__, __CRC32__, __XSAVE__); -march=x86-64-v3 adds 17.

2. Vector ABI. sema/abi.rs::vector_abi passes a >16-byte vector as byval on sysv64. Verified against clang 22: baseline passes both <8 x i32> and <16 x i32> byval; -mavx makes the 32-byte argument direct and leaves the 64-byte one byval; -mavx512f makes both direct. Clang flags the baseline choice with -Wpsabi, which fires on tests/fixtures/sema/ir_vector_abi.c today.

The two halves are consistent right now (an #ifdef __AVX__ header block stays unselected, so no wider vector reaches the ABI layer expecting register passing), and they must stay consistent: a flag that changes one has to change the other in the same step.

Work: parse -m<feature> and -march= into an ISA level on TargetInfo; layer the feature macro block over the baseline predefine header rather than capturing a whole new header per combination; key the sysv64 >16-byte row off the level. Decide how far to go beyond x86 (aapcs64 SVE, arm32 -mfpu=neon) or scope it to x86 explicitly. Fixtures: predefine coverage per level, and an ir_vector_abi variant under -mavx.

See wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md (vector ABI table, which states baseline as the assumption) and the 2026-09-19 log entry.
close_reason: x86 ISA flags resolve to TargetInfo.x86_isa; ISA/CPU macros stripped from clang x86 headers and generated at configure; sysv64 vector byval threshold follows the ISA. Verified against clang 22 on 34 flag combinations. ARM deferred to a follow-up.

title: Lower vector lane subscripts and ext_vector swizzles
description: v[i] on a vector place and the ext_vector_type component syntax (v.x, v.xy, v.lo/.hi) do not lower: a vector lane is neither a pointer offset nor a record field, so PlaceKind needs a lane projection whose base is a place (PlaceKind::Index exists but takes a value base and is unused). Out of scope for slate-parser-lh7.2.17.3, which covered the type, storage, and arithmetic contracts.
notes:
Done (finishes the bead). ext_vector component syntax now lowers:

swizzle_lanes maps a component name to lane indices for x/y/z/w, r/g/b/a, sN in hex (either case), and lo/hi/even/odd, where the half is the lane count rounded up to a power of two, so a 3-lane .hi names one lane that does not exist. One component in range is a lane(..) place; several distinct components in range are the new PlaceKind::Swizzle, printed swizzle<lanes=[..]>(place), so v.zw = w stays a write; a repeated (v.xx) or out-of-range selection is not assignable and becomes a one-operand ValueKind::Shuffle.

Expression::member mirrors Expression::subscript: it lowers the base once and returns a place or a value, so a swizzle of an rvalue ((a+b).lo, f().even) works too.

Clang accepts these only on ext_vector_type; Type::Vector does not record which spelling declared it, so we accept them on vector_size vectors as well, per feature-availability-not-target-gated.

Verified against clang -ast-dump for the result types of .x, .xy, .lo/.hi/.even/.odd, .sN, .rgba, 3-lane .lo/.hi, mixed-set and uppercase-xyzw rejection, and assignability of a repeated swizzle. ir-spec.md and ir-grammar.md updated; tests/fixtures/sema/ir_vector.c pins each form.
close_reason: Closed

title: Classify vector arguments and results in the target ABIs
description: Vector parameters and results currently pass as AbiPass::NativeC on every target: the ABI layer records that the vector is unclassified rather than guessing a coercion. Real ABIs pass vectors in SSE/NEON registers up to a target- and ISA-extension-dependent width and spill wider ones to memory, and Windows x86-64 passes vectors indirectly. Model this per convention the way complex_abi already does, with abi_target.c fixtures diffed against clang IR signatures.
close_reason: Vectors classify per convention with the new AbiPass::Direct; sysv64/win64/x86_cdecl/aapcs64/win_arm64/aapcs32(+hf) all diffed against clang IR signatures, including the gcc one-lane-double and i386 MMX corners and variadic vector arguments

title: Block-scope typedef of a VLA type, and VLA empty initializers
description: typedef int T[n]; at block scope is rejected ('block scoped typedef or tag definition'); C evaluates the bound once at the typedef, not at each use, so the alias must refer to a captured extent. Separately, int a[n] = {}; (C23, the only valid VLA initializer) is rejected with 'variable length array initializer' in sema/module.rs declaration().
acceptance_criteria: Fixture covers a block-scope VLA typedef used twice after its bound variable changes (one capture), and a C23 {} VLA initializer.
close_reason: Block-scope typedefs accepted with lexical TypeResolver scopes; VLA typedef captures its bound once; C23 {} VLA initializer lowers to zero_fill aggregate

title: VLA type names in expressions: sizeof(int[n]), casts, compound literals
description: A variably modified type name inside an expression has no extent capture. Repro: printf 'int f(int n){ return sizeof(int[n]); }\n' > t.c; slate-parser ir t.c -> 'nonconstant or unknown identifier'. Same for (int(*)[n])p casts. capture_extents only runs for block-scope declarators and definition parameters (sema/module.rs); a type name's bound is evaluated where the expression is, so it must be hoisted as a synthetic temporary through the side-effect hoisting pass (effects.rs) rather than at a declaration.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture covers sizeof(int[n]) and a cast to a pointer-to-VLA type; each bound is evaluated once at the expression's evaluation point.
close_reason: sizeof(type) and casts capture VLA bounds at the expression via ValueKind::Capture, hoisted to synthetic temporaries; _Alignof on VLA types works; compound literals split out

title: Lex integer imaginary literals (3i, 3ui, 0x10i) as integers
description: GNU integer imaginary literals such as 3i have type _Complex int (gcc and clang agree). The lexer emits them as FloatLit because the i/j suffix makes the digits non-integer, so const_expr parses them as FloatLiteral and sema now rejects them with 'integer imaginary literals' (sema/numeric.rs is_integer_spelling). Strip i/j in Lexer::integer_digits / parse_integer_literal, add an imaginary flag to IntegerLiteral (update ast-spec.md), reject it in #if evaluation, and lower to aggregate<complex<iN>>(0, v) like floating imaginary literals (slate-parser-lh7.2.17.2).
close_reason: Integer imaginary literals lex as IntLit with IntegerLiteral.imaginary, lower to complex integer aggregates matching clang types, rejected in constant evaluation

title: Atomic builtins: macro-provenance c_builtin, __sync_*, lock_free, float fetch, non-constant weak
description: Follow-up to lh7.2.21. Not done there: (1) c_builtin metadata records only the builtin name (__c11_atomic_fetch_add); the design asked for the <stdatomic.h> macro name (atomic_fetch_add_explicit) via macro provenance. (2) __sync_* legacy builtins (always seq_cst) are unresolved; they can map onto the same update/compare_exchange nodes. (3) __c11_atomic_is_lock_free / __atomic_always_lock_free / __atomic_is_lock_free are unresolved. (4) Floating-point fetch_add/sub (clang extension) returns Unsupported. (5) A non-constant weak argument to __atomic_compare_exchange(_n) returns Unsupported.
close_reason: c_macro metadata (innermost macro), all __sync_* builtins, lock-free queries (folded per clang, libatomic call otherwise), floating fetch add/sub, and dynamic compare-exchange weak. Float fetch min/max split out.

title: Lower remaining object attributes: aligned, common/nocommon, weakref, selectany
description: lh7.2.9 added SymbolAttributes (asm_name, visibility, weak, alias, section, used, retain, tls_model, dllimport/dllexport) on Global and Function. Any other declaration attribute on an object still fails with 'unsupported in numeric IR lowering: declaration attribute' (sema/module.rs symbol_attributes). aligned(N) needs a required-constant fold and changes the object's alignment, which is layout rather than a symbol property. common/nocommon interacts with -fcommon for tentative definitions. weakref("t") is weak plus alias. selectany is the MSVC COMDAT form. Repro: printf 'int x __attribute__((aligned(16)));\n' > t.c && target/release/slate-parser ir t.c
acceptance_criteria: Each attribute lowers to an IR property printed on the global and is covered by a FileCheck fixture.
close_reason: aligned/_Alignas -> Global [align=N] (flavor-dependent), common/nocommon + new -fcommon/-fno-common -> [common] on external tentative definitions, weakref -> [weakref="t"] (extern, internal linkage required; also on functions), selectany -> [selectany] (external linkage required). Fixtures cover each.

title: _Atomic types use the unqualified type's size and alignment
description: lh7.2.10 models _Atomic as an access property, but layout still uses the unqualified type. Clang pads _Atomic(T) to a power-of-two size and raises alignment up to the max inline atomic width (e.g. _Atomic struct { char a[3]; } is size 4, align 4 on x86_64), which changes record offsets and sizeof.
acceptance_criteria: sizeof/_Alignof and record layout of _Atomic-qualified objects match clang on x86_64 for odd-sized structs and scalars; fixture covers it.
close_reason: _Atomic value types are padded to a power of two and over-aligned up to the target's max promote width (16 bytes x86_64/AArch64, 8 i386/ARM32), per element for arrays. Covers sizeof/_Alignof of atomic type names and objects, and record field layout. Fixtures: ir_atomic_layout.c, i386-unknown-linux-gnu/atomic_layout.c

title: Braced initializers for complex values
description: _Complex float c = {re, im} failed with 'scalar initializer list must hold exactly one element'. Lowered as aggregate<complex<T>>(index0, index1). Brace elision into complex pairs not modeled.
close_reason: Closed

title: Initialize flexible array member elements
description: struct F g = {1, {2,3}} is Unsupported ('flexible array member initializer'). Layout (size 0, element alignment) and omitted-member init work. Needs an IR decision on how an object's type carries the FAM extent.
close_reason: Closed

title: Outer pointer plus grouped declarator resolves wrong type
description: 'int *(*q)[4];' lowers to array<ptr<ptr<i32>>, 4>; expected ptr<array<ptr<i32>, 4>>. Parser nests the base pointer inside the Array node so TypeResolver::derive applies it in the wrong order. Pre-existing; found while fixing multi-dimensional array order.
close_reason: Closed

title: sizeof of brace-inferred array fails in static_assert
description: sema/assertion.rs declaration() only infers 'T a[] = ...' length from Initializer::Expr string literals. 'int a[] = {1,2}; static_assert(sizeof(a) == 8);' reports 'incomplete field type'. Lowering (sema/initializer.rs) already infers it; share the count rather than duplicating designator/elision logic.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reject digit separators in numeric literals before C23
description: clang and gcc both hard-error on 1'000 in every mode before C23 (checked clang 22.1, gcc 16.2, c89..c17/gnu17). slate-parser's lexer accepts it ungated (src/lexer.rs integer_digits strips '). Add a StandardFeatures field (Rejected before C23) and a source-located error. Split out of slate-parser-47s.7.
close_reason: Decided to keep accepting digit separators as an extension; recorded in ast-spec.md

title: Preserve and lower fixed-point types into IR
description: First preserve signedness in FixedPointType and parser for signed/unsigned _Fract/_Accum. Resolve target width, scale, storage, saturation, and rounding into a distinct IR Type and arithmetic contract, with FileCheck fixtures for saturating and nonsaturating operations.

title: Lower vector types and operations into IR
description: Resolve GNU vector_size and ext_vector_type AST forms to scalar element plus validated lane count. Implement target size/alignment and ABI treatment, vector arithmetic/comparison contracts, and FileCheck fixtures for both size forms.
close_reason: Type::Vector lowers both size forms with clang-matched storage, elementwise arithmetic, lane-mask comparisons, lax conversions, and ir_vector.c/ir_vector_invalid.c fixtures; ABI classification and lane subscripts split into .6/.7

title: Lower imaginary types and literals into IR
description: Add a structural imaginary Type and imaginary literal value. Define conversions and result-family rules for real/imaginary/complex operators, plus target storage/ABI. Pin declarations, literal bits, arithmetic, and comparisons with FileCheck fixtures.
close_reason: Type::Imaginary with Annex G conversions and result families, GNU imaginary literals lowered as complex aggregates; fixtures ir_imaginary.c/ir_imaginary_invalid.c; integer 3i literals split to lh7.2.17.5

title: Lower complex types and arithmetic into IR
description: Add a structural complex Type with resolved component and target storage/ABI. Resolve float and GNU integer-complex declarations, conversions, arithmetic, equality, and component access where supported. Pin type and operation contracts with FileCheck fixtures; update ir-spec.md as implementation lands.
notes: Implemented Type::Complex(NumericType), target pair storage, GNU int _Complex suffix parsing, scalar/complex conversions, arithmetic/equality/conditions, and real/imag lvalue access. Fixture tests/fixtures/sema/ir_complex.c covers operations, precision, casts, writes, sizes. clang confirms 16/32 byte complex double/long double sizes. General target ABI argument/return classification remains slate-parser-lh7.2.18; module signatures retain complex semantic types. Validation: cargo clippy --allow-dirty --fix, cargo fmt, cargo nextest run --release passed.
close_reason: Complex IR representation, lowering, arithmetic, component access, storage, and FileCheck coverage implemented; general call ABI classification split to slate-parser-lh7.2.18

title: Lower _Decimal32/64/128 types and DF/DD/DL literals to IR
description:
Follow-up to slate-parser-ixa.36, which added FloatingType::Decimal32/64/128 to the AST. IR lowering doesn't handle them: `slate-parser ir` on `_Decimal64 d = 1.0DD;` fails with 'unsupported in numeric IR lowering: floating type'.

Where it fails:
- src/sema/types.rs resolve_scalar: FloatingType match falls through to Unsupported("floating type").
- src/sema/numeric.rs cast_type: same fallthrough ("floating cast type").
- src/sema/numeric.rs resolve: FloatValue::Decimal32/64/128 returns Unsupported("decimal floating literals").
- src/ir/numeric.rs FloatType has only binary formats (F16/F32/F64/F80/F128), so there's no IR type to lower to.

Needs a decimal format in the IR: either new FloatType variants (D32/D64/D128) or a separate NumericType::Decimal. Storage layout is 4/8/16 bytes with natural alignment on the gcc targets. Literals should keep their decimal digit spelling (FloatValue::Decimal* already stores a String) rather than being converted to binary, since the value is exact in decimal. Arithmetic, conversions and the usual arithmetic conversions (C23 6.3.1.8: mixing decimal and binary floating types is a constraint violation) are part of this. Per ir-required-constant-folding, don't fold decimal arithmetic.

Availability stays ungated (see bd memory feature-availability-not-target-gated): lower on every target; Slate decides usability.
acceptance_criteria: `slate-parser ir` succeeds on declarations, casts, sizeof/_Alignof and literals of all three decimal types; ir-spec.md's type table lists the decimal formats; a fixture covers it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Raise -Wlong-long for long long declarations, not just literals
description: slate-parser-47s.8 wired -Wlong-long only at integer literal selection in sema/validate.rs. clang also raises it for the *type* in c89: 'long long x;' warns under -pedantic with no literal involved. Needs a hook where declaration specifiers resolve a long long type, gated on StandardFeatures::long_long_type != Standard.
acceptance_criteria: A c89 fixture with 'long long x;' and no large literal emits -Wlong-long under -pedantic and errors under -pedantic-errors.
close_reason: Closed

title: Plain character constant with a non-ASCII character follows gcc, not clang
description: 'Ω' lowers to 52905 (0xCEA9, the UTF-8 bytes packed as a multicharacter constant), which is what gcc does. clang rejects it outright: 'character too large for enclosing character literal type'. slate-parser has --flavor=gcc|clang|msvc but sema::numeric::Context carries no flavor, so sema::types::character_constant cannot branch on it. Decide whether the clang flavor should reject plain character constants whose execution encoding needs more than one byte, and thread the flavor into sema if so.
close_reason: Closed

title: Preprocessor #if ignores char signedness for character constants
description: fold_char_code_units (src/const_expr.rs) returns the raw code unit for a single-character constant, so '\\xff' evaluates to 255 in #if. clang and gcc give -1 on targets where plain char is signed: '#if '\\xff' < 0' takes the true branch under clang and the false branch under slate-parser. sema::types::character_constant now models this correctly; the #if evaluator cannot, because const_expr::Parser::evaluate_expr has no TargetInfo. Fixing it means threading the target into preprocessor conditional evaluation.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower encoded character constants as values
description: sema::expression rejects any non-plain or multicharacter character constant with ResolveError::Unsupported("wide or multicharacter literal") (src/sema/expression.rs). u'a', U'a', L'a' and (C23) u8'a' therefore cannot be used as values, even though the lexer decodes their code units. Types: u8'c' is unsigned char in C23, u'c' is char16_t, U'c' is char32_t, L'c' is wchar_t (int here); a plain multicharacter constant 'ab' is int with implementation-defined value. The string-literal side of this landed in slate-parser-j66; this is the character-constant half.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pointer sign mismatch is a hard error where clang warns
description: Assigning unsigned char[] to const char* (or any pointer-to-integer pair differing only in signedness) fails with 'incompatible or unsupported conversion' in numeric IR lowering. clang accepts it with -Wpointer-sign. This now bites real C23 code: 'const char *p = u8"a";' is a warning under clang -std=c23 but an error in slate-parser. Decide whether to accept with a recorded diagnostic or keep rejecting, and pin it by fixture.
close_reason: Accepted as pointer_cast (IR records the implicit cast); warning channel deferred to slate-parser-x5r

title: libc-shim ucontext.h and stddef.h break under strict -std=c23
description:
Now that __STRICT_ANSI__ is honored, the shim's features.h stops auto-defining _BSD_SOURCE/_XOPEN_SOURCE 700 (include/features.h:120), which exposes two shim inconsistencies in strict modes.

1. include/ucontext.h declares getcontext/makecontext/setcontext/swapcontext taking 'struct __ucontext *' unconditionally, but bits/<arch>/signal.h defines that struct only under '#if defined(_GNU_SOURCE) || defined(_BSD_SOURCE)'. In strict mode sema fails with 'unknown tag __ucontext'. Reproduce: slate-parser parse tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-dg/split-5.c -std=c23. Real glibc guards the whole of ucontext.h behind its feature macros instead.
2. bits/types.h gates wchar_t on __NEED_wchar_t, which is no longer set in strict mode, so <stddef.h> stops providing wchar_t. wchar_t is ISO C and must be declared by stddef.h in every mode.

Not reachable from the default standard any more (slate-parser-r37 moved the default to gnu23, matching clang/gcc), so this only bites an explicit -std=c89/c99/c11/c17/c23. Lives in ~/Projects/slate/libc-shim, not this repo.

title: Token pasting lexes with default standard features
description: src/pp/mod.rs lex()/lex_spanned() build a Lexer without .with_features(), so a '##' paste that forms a word like 'restrict', 'inline', 'typeof' or 'constexpr' is classified against StandardFeatures::default() (c23) rather than the active standard. The other two Lexer construction sites now thread features through. Fix needs the free functions to take features, or to move them onto the preprocessor.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two gcc-dg fixtures have stale tag-id CHECK lines
description:
tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-dg/pr85388-4.c and tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-dg/split-4.c fail FileCheck on the DEFAULT prefix: both expect tag[25] where the renderer now produces tag[24] (and the ids below it shift by one).

Pre-existing, not caused by any current change -- verified 2026-09-17 by running `cargo nextest run --release` on the tree with and without the slate-parser-47s.1 changes stashed: identical failure both times, and with just these two fixtures moved aside the whole suite passes on both trees.

Same class as commit 507589c5 (Regenerate stale tag-id CHECK lines in gcc-dg fixtures). Both fixtures pull in system headers via SLATE-FILECHECK-ISYSTEM ~/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include and /usr/lib/clang/22/include, so their tag numbering depends on the local header snapshot -- which is the same environment fragility that aab9f17f addressed for provenance line numbers.
design: Regenerating with tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place fixes the symptom but re-pins the numbering to whichever headers the regenerating machine has. Decide first whether absolute tag ids belong in expectations that include system headers at all, or whether these fixtures should match relatively the way provenance line numbers now do.
acceptance_criteria: cargo nextest run --release passes with both fixtures present; the fix does not depend on the regenerating machine's header snapshot, or the fixtures stop asserting absolute tag ids.
notes:
Fixed 2026-09-17 by loosening the ids in the generator rather than restamping the two fixtures.

tools/update_filecheck.py gains loosen_ids(), a post-pass beside loosen_system_provenance(). tag[N] and decl[N] labels become {{[0-9]+}}; each distinct TagId value binds a FileCheck numeric variable ([[#TAG0:]]) on first sight and reuses it ([[#TAG0]]) afterwards.

The variable matters: a tag id is a cross-reference, not just a label. In anon_local_struct.c two anonymous structs are defined and two declarations reference them; a blanket {{[0-9]+}} would have stopped checking that each declaration names the tag it named before. Verified by pointing one reference at the other tag's variable -- the fixture fails, as it should.

The tag[N] and decl[N] labels carry nothing a variable would preserve: render.rs formats tag[{}] from tag.value.id.0, which is the same field the id: TagId(..) line below it already checks, so their agreement was tautological.

Regenerated all 2532 fixtures: 2377 files changed, 17913 insertions and 17913 deletions -- a 1:1 line rewrite, and every added line is one of the three expected forms (no content drift). Full suite passes with no fixtures moved aside.
close_reason: Generator now loosens tag ids (via FileCheck numeric variables, preserving the cross-reference) and decl indices; all fixtures regenerated; full suite passes with no fixtures excluded.

title: Enumerators cannot carry attributes
description:
ast::Enumerator is { name, value } with no attributes field, though FieldDeclaratorKind, InitDeclaratorKind, ParameterDeclarationKind, and TagDefinition all have one.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf 'enum E { A [[deprecated]] = 1 };\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser parse t.c
Observed: expected `,` or `}` in enum body.

C23 6.7.2.2 permits an attribute-specifier-seq on an enumeration constant, and gcc has accepted __attribute__((deprecated)) there for much longer. deprecated on an enumerator is exactly the kind of fact worth preserving for Slate. Enumerators are the one declaration-like node in the AST still missing the field.
acceptance_criteria:
Enumerator carries attributes; both the [[...]] and __attribute__((...)) spellings parse between the name and the =, with and without a value; a fixture covers deprecated and an unknown attribute.

CORRECTION (2026-09-18): the original criterion said the spellings must parse 'before and after the = value'. The after-value position is invalid — C23 6.7.2.2 places the attribute-specifier-seq only between the enumeration-constant and the =, and both clang 22 and gcc reject 'enum E { A = 1 [[deprecated]] };' in either spelling. Implemented the real grammar and pinned the rejection.
close_reason: Closed

title: _Decimal32/64/128 type specifiers are unknown type names
description:
ast::FloatingType has BFloat16, Float, Float16, Fp16, Float64x, Double, LongDouble, Float128, Float128Ext -- no decimal formats.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf '_Decimal64 d;\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser parse t.c
Observed: semantic analysis failed -- unknown type name `_Decimal64`.

These are C23 Annex H (optional, gated on __STDC_IEC_60559_DFP__) and a long-standing gcc extension. sema/numeric.rs:109 already has a FloatValue::Decimal arm returning 'decimal floating literals' unsupported, so part of the literal path anticipates them while the type specifier does not exist -- that arm is currently unreachable.

Scope here is the AST: the three type specifiers, the DF/DD/DL literal suffixes, and target availability. Decimal arithmetic in the IR is a separate question and should not block this.
acceptance_criteria: _Decimal32, _Decimal64, and _Decimal128 parse into FloatingType variants with their literal suffixes; availability follows the target; ast-spec.md's type specifier table lists them.
close_reason: Decimal types parse into FloatingType variants in every standard mode and on every target; DF/DD/DL literals already parsed; ast-spec updated

title: Complex, imaginary, vector, and fixed-point types have no IR representation
description:
TypeSpecifier has Complex, Imaginary, Vector (with byte or lane sizing), and FixedPoint (_Fract/_Accum with saturation), and all four parse. ir::Type has Void | Bool | Numeric | Defined | Pointer | Array | Function -- none of them. sema/numeric.rs:100 also rejects imaginary literals outright.

'_Complex double z;' parses and then has nowhere to lower. _Complex is C99 (Annex G), and both clang and gcc support the GNU vector and fixed-point extensions; all four appear in real headers (complex.h, arm_neon.h, embedded DSP headers).

Lower priority than the qualifier, VLA, and initializer work because the affected headers are narrower, but the shape decision matters early: each is a value type whose arithmetic rules are not the scalar rules the numeric seed implements, so bolting them onto NumericType later would be worse than deciding now whether they are distinct Type variants.
design: Likely separate variants rather than NumericType members: a complex value is a pair with its own arithmetic and its own comparison semantics, a vector is elementwise with a lane count, and a fixed-point type has a saturation policy that does not fit ArithSema's integer/floating/exact split. Check whether the ArithSema enum needs a fourth case for saturating arithmetic before committing. Split into one bead per family once the shape is settled.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four families is either represented in ir::Type with arithmetic pinned by a fixture, or explicitly recorded in ir-spec.md as out of scope with the reason.
close_reason: Shape decided in wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md; each family explicitly deferred with technical reason and tracked in child issues .1-.4

title: Unnamed parameters in a function definition are rejected unconditionally
description:
sema/module.rs:193 errors with 'unnamed definition parameter' whenever a definition's parameter has no name. C23 6.7.6.3 permits it; before C23 a definition's parameters had to be named.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf 'int f(int) { return 0; }\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c -std=c23
Observed: unsupported in numeric IR lowering: unnamed definition parameter.
Expected: accepted. ir::Parameter.name is already Option<String>, so the IR can represent it today.

Gate the check on the standard (via slate-parser-47s.1) instead of removing it -- an unnamed definition parameter really is invalid before C23.
acceptance_criteria: An unnamed definition parameter lowers in c23/gnu23 and is diagnosed in c89 through c17; the lowered parameter has no name in the dump.
close_reason: Unnamed definition parameters lower in every standard with a fresh binding; before C23 they raise -Wc23-extensions (on by default, error under -pedantic-errors), matching clang 22 which accepts them as an extension rather than rejecting.

title: Array parameter 'static' and qualifiers are dropped at pointer adjustment
description:
Declarator::Array carries is_static and qualifiers, and the parser fills them, but the adjustment of an array parameter to a pointer discards both.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf 'int f(int n, int a[static 3]) { return a[0]; }\n' > t.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir t.c
Observed: fn %0 @f(%1 n: i32, %2 a: ptr<i32>) -- the 'static 3' is gone.

C99 6.7.6.3p7: 'static N' guarantees the argument provides access to at least N elements, which implies non-null. 'int a[const]' likewise qualifies the adjusted pointer, not the element type. These are guarantees the source states explicitly and nothing else in the IR records, so losing them is a fidelity loss of the kind the parser-preserves-structure memory rules out.
design: Attach to the parameter, not the type: the adjusted type really is a pointer and should keep printing as one. A minimum-element-count fact and the adjusted pointer's qualifiers are parameter properties. Overlaps with slate-parser-lh7.2.10 for where pointer qualifiers live; settle that shape first if the two land close together.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture covers [static N], [const], [restrict], [static const N], and [*] on parameters; each fact is visible on the parameter in the default dump.
close_reason: Array parameter static/qualifiers now survive adjustment as [array=...] and [const] on the parameter; element const no longer dropped from the adjusted pointee. Fixture: tests/fixtures/sema/ir_array_parameter.c

title: C99-and-later constructs are accepted in c89 without diagnostics
description:
A sweep bead for constructs slate-parser accepts unconditionally that C89 does not have. None are currently gated, so -std=c89 silently accepts C99/C11/C23 source:

- variable length arrays and [*] parameters (C99)
- compound literals (C99), designated initializers (C99)
- declarations after statements in a block (C99)
- // line comments (C99; gnu89 extension)
- flexible array members (C99)
- digit separators in numeric literals and 0b binary literals (C23; clang rejects 1'000 under -std=c17)
- _Static_assert / _Generic / _Alignof / _Atomic / _Noreturn (C11)
- [[...]] attribute syntax (C23)

Most of these are accepted by clang and gcc as extensions in earlier modes, which by the _BitInt precedent in ir-spec.md argues for recording them as extensions rather than rejecting them. The work here is to check each against both compilers in each mode and write the decision down, not to reject them by default.
design: Produce a table in wiki/concepts/ast-spec.md: construct, standard that introduced it, clang and gcc behavior per mode (accept silently / accept with -pedantic warning / reject), and slate-parser's chosen behavior. Split out any construct that turns out to be genuinely rejected by both compilers into its own bead; leave the rest as recorded extensions in StandardFeatures.
acceptance_criteria: The table exists in ast-spec.md with per-compiler evidence; every construct listed is either gated or explicitly recorded as an accepted extension; digit separators and 0b literals are settled one way or the other.
close_reason: Closed

title: u8 string literal element type differs between C17 and C23
description:
A u8"..." literal has type char[] in C11 and C17 and unsigned char[] in C23 (which introduced char8_t as unsigned char). The distinction changes the lowered element type and therefore what Slate emits.

slate-parser does not model this: string literal lowering rejects any encoded literal outright (sema/expression.rs:708, 'encoded string literal'), tracked as slate-parser-j66. This bead is the standard-mode half -- when j66 lowers encoded literals, the u8 element type must come from StandardFeatures rather than being fixed. The u8 character constant u8'a' is separately C23-only (C17 has no u8 character constant); slate-parser accepts it in every mode.
acceptance_criteria: Once encoded string literals lower, a u8 literal's element type is unsigned char in c23 and char in c11/c17, pinned by fixture; u8 character constants are diagnosed before c23 or recorded as an accepted extension with the clang/gcc evidence.
close_reason: Closed

title: K&R definitions are accepted in c23, where they were removed
description:
C23 removed old-style function definitions and identifier lists (6.7.6.3). slate-parser accepts them in every mode.

Repro (2026-09-17):
  printf 'int knr(a,b) char a; float b; { return a; }\n' > k.c
  target/release/slate-parser ir k.c -std=c23
Observed: fn %0 @knr(%1 a: i32, %2 b: f64) -> i32
Expected in c23: a diagnostic. clang -std=c23 reports 'unknown type name a'.

The promotion itself is correct and deliberate (slate-parser-ixa.3: char -> i32, float -> f64, declared type recoverable via declared_specifiers). Only the mode gating is missing. Scope is the acceptance check, not the AST shape -- do not reintroduce a K&R lane in the AST.
acceptance_criteria: A K&R definition is diagnosed in c23/gnu23 and still parses and promotes identically in c89 through c17; tests/fixtures/knr_promoted_parameters.c is unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: No fixture covers user-header provenance (kind: User)
description: All 7121 provenance entries across tests/fixtures render kind: System; none render kind: User, even tests/fixtures/header-provenance.c which includes a quoted header via "header-provenance-headers/local.h". HeaderKind::User is constructed in src/pp/include.rs:162,168 for quoted includes resolved relative to the includer, so either the fixtures never reach that path or the outermost-header provenance is labelled System when it should be User. Worth a fixture either way: update_filecheck.py now only loosens a provenance line number when the enclosing kind is System, and that guard has no fixture exercising it.

title: Diagnose _BitInt as an extension before C23
description: clang warns '_BitInt in C17 and earlier is a Clang extension' (-Wbit-int-extension); gcc warns 'ISO C does not support _BitInt before C23' under -pedantic. slate-parser accepts _BitInt silently in every standard mode. The conversion rules are correctly mode-independent (see wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md); only the acceptance diagnostic is missing. Severity::Warning exists in main.rs, so there is a channel for it.
close_reason: Added pedantic _BitInt extension diagnostics, parameter coverage, generated fixture checks, and documentation.

title: Reject sizeof and _Alignof on a bit-field member
description: C forbids sizeof/_Alignof on a bit-field lvalue. sema::expression::unevaluated_type resolves the place and reports the declared storage type's size instead of diagnosing. Address-of is already rejected (PlaceKind::Field { bits: Some(_), .. }); the unevaluated path needs the same check.
