close_reason: sizeof/_Alignof on a bit-field now reject via ResolveError::Invalid; also fixed _Generic selecting the promoted type

title: Support block-scoped tag definitions in IR lowering
description: src/sema/module.rs::declaration rejects a local declaration whose specifier is a TagSpecifier::Definition. Removing that guard is unsound today: two functions each defining 'struct Local' with different fields collapse onto one TypeId, so the type table emits one record and the second function's field accesses are typed against the first one's layout. Repro: `int one(void){struct Local{int a;}l;l.a=4;return l.a;} int two(void){struct Local{long b;}l;l.b=5;return (int)l.b;}` — both locals get @type0 and two()'s field0 prints as i64 while @type0.field0 is i32. Anonymous local tags are fine since they cannot collide by name. Needs the Lowerer's TypeResolver to scope tag identity per block (it already has tag_names push_scope/pop_scope; module.rs statement lowering does not drive it). Tag *references* to file-scope tags were the over-broad half of this guard and are fixed in slate-parser-6id.
close_reason: The guard in module.rs::declaration rejecting block-scoped tag definitions was stale: the unsoundness it described does not reproduce. TypeResolver::push_scope/pop_scope are already driven by Lowerer::scoped for function bodies, blocks, ifs and loops, and tag_ids is keyed by the AST TagId while define_tag only looks for a previous tag in the *current* scope. The bead's own repro now gives '@type0 Local { field0 a: i32 }' to one() and '@type1 Local { field0 b: i64 }' to two(), each with correct field layouts. Removing the guard produced no fixture churn. Fixture sema/ir_tag_scopes.c.

title: Diagnose non-ICE static assertion conditions instead of skipping
description: ice_shape still returns false (silent skip) for call expressions, string literals, compound literals, and the comma operator at assertion top level. Clang rejects all of these with 'static assertion expression is not an integral constant expression'. Emitting that diagnosis means being sure every fold-able form is modelled first, otherwise valid C gets rejected; blocked on a builtin signature table.
close_reason: Diagnose static assertion calls to non-foldable functions using a hand-owned FOLDABLE_BUILTINS table. String/compound-literal/comma forms are left alone: clang folds them as a GNU extension in C.

title: Fold __builtin_types_compatible_p and remaining builtin ICEs
description: TypeResolver::constant_value has no arm for ExprKind::TypesCompatible, so `static_assert(__builtin_types_compatible_p(int, int))` is skipped by ice_shape rather than folded. GCC and clang treat it as an integer constant expression. The same gap covers __builtin_constant_p and __builtin_offsetof-adjacent builtins. sema::types::builtin_result_type currently knows only __builtin_{add,sub,mul}_overflow (bool), added for _Generic controlling-expression typing; a real builtin signature table belongs there.
notes: 2026-09-19: __builtin_constant_p folds (IR bodies, static_assert, array bounds); ice_shape now admits it and __builtin_types_compatible_p; enum constants now visible to the lowerer's resolver so int a[K] lowers. The builtin signature table is tracked by epic slate-parser-6lz.
close_reason: constant_p and types_compatible_p fold as ICEs; signature table is slate-parser-6lz

title: Fix tag-id drift in gcc-dg/pr85388-4.c FileCheck fixture
description: cargo nextest run --release fails: tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-dg/pr85388-4.c expects tag[27] but actual output is tag[25] (and onward), a 2-id numbering drift in the generated CHECK lines vs current tag-numbering output. Unrelated to typeof work (slate-parser-9d0); found while running the full test suite. Fix by re-running tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place on the fixture and confirming the drift is expected, or find+fix the underlying cause of the numbering shift.
close_reason: Fixed by regenerating CHECK lines with tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place; tag ids shifted 27->25 in both pr85388-4.c and split-4.c (same shared header pattern), consistent with a real upstream tag-numbering change, not test flakiness. Full suite green now.

title: Bit-precise integers follow standard promotion and usual-arithmetic rules
description: sema/numeric.rs promotes any integer narrower than int to int, including _BitInt(N), and usual_arith picks the wider operand type with bit_precise carried along by width. C23 6.3.1.1/6.3.1.8 exempt bit-precise integers from integer promotion and constrain mixing them with standard types. Now that Type carries bit_precise (slate-parser-8cs), the rules are expressible; implement them and add fixtures.
close_reason: Bit-precise integers now exempt from integer and default argument promotions; same-width bit-precision changes emit an explicit reinterpret. Verified against clang and gcc.

title: Macro expansion constant factor is ~80x clang
description: Expansion scales linearly (no algorithmic blowup) but the per-expansion constant is high: 800 uses of a 59-deep object-macro chain inside a #if takes ~0.38s versus ~0.005s of real work for clang -E on the same input, about 8us versus 0.1us per expansion. Suspects, none measured individually yet: Preprocessor::expand_macros clones the whole MacroEntry (self.macros.get(name).cloned()) on every identifier that names a macro; origin_for_expansion builds an Rc<MacroOrigin> per expansion and MacroOrigin::append walks the parent chain; Token carries owned Strings so every replacement token clone allocates. Measure before optimizing. Note a naive benchmark measures AST pretty-printing instead, which dominates at 96% of 'slate-parser parse' on macro-heavy input; put the expansion work in a #if to isolate it.

title: Lower encoded string literals as values
description: sema::expression still rejects a non-plain string literal used as a value (ResolveError::Unsupported("encoded string literal")); ValueKind::Bytes holds bytes, so u"...", U"..." and L"..." need an IR representation carrying wider code units. StringLiteral::execution_units already produces the right units for every encoding, and sizeof of an encoded literal now works through sema::types::string_literal_type, so only the value path is missing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Assertion pass reimplements scoping instead of sharing one resolver
description: src/sema/assertion.rs carries its own scope and shadowing implementation (hide_name, hide_tag, assertion_scope on TypeResolver, and a TypeResolver clone saved and restored at every block, function, for-init and statement expression) parallel to the one in sema::names and the rest of sema. It is correct today and matches clang on the shadowing cases covered by tests/fixtures/sema/static_assert_validation.c, but it is a second implementation of the same rules that will drift as scoping is fixed elsewhere, and it clones the whole resolver per scope rather than pushing and popping a scope. Consider running assertions inside the existing resolution walk once that walk can evaluate constants, or give TypeResolver a real scope stack both can use.
close_reason: Closed

title: _BitInt(128) and __int128 share one IR type and cannot get distinct layouts
description: Both lower to Type::Numeric(NumericType::Integer { width: 128 }), so ScalarLayouts cannot give them different layouts. clang gives __int128 size 16 align 16 and _BitInt(128) size 16 align 8; we report align 16 for both. ScalarLayouts::bit_precise (src/target_info.rs) deliberately declines the tabulated widths 8/16/32/64/128 for this reason, which also keeps arm32 rejecting __int128 after it removes those entries. Fix needs bit-precise integers marked at the type level, not a layout tweak; the same distinction is what lets targets reject __int128 while still accepting _BitInt of the same width.
close_reason: Closed

title: Static assertion validation runs twice per translation unit
description: super::assertion::validate is called from TranslationUnit::analyze (src/sema/validate.rs) and again from resolve_module (src/sema/module.rs). The pass walks every declaration and function body and clones a TypeResolver per scope, so the work is duplicated outright. The two call sites also report differently: analyze collects every SemaError, resolve_module takes only the first and wraps it in ResolveError::StaticAssertion, so the same source yields one diagnostic or many depending on entry point. Run it once and share the result, or have resolve_module rely on analyze having run.
close_reason: Closed

title: Complete Windows MSVC target semantics
description: Follow-up to slate-parser-lh7.1.20 selection scaffolding. Implement and validate Microsoft record/bit-field layout, packing and explicit alignment, calling conventions, target/compiler option constraints, native MSVC standard-dependent macros and extended-type availability, Windows shim/SDK integration, and remaining 32-bit profiles. Current 64-bit profiles select predefines and basic LLP64 types only; they do not promise MSVC ABI compatibility.

title: Document compiler argument rule buckets
description: Add a short wiki guide for using the compiler argument rules engine and link it from AGENTS.md.
close_reason: Closed

title: check_literals doesn't cover enum values, bitfield widths, or static_assert conditions
description: resolve_integer_literal/resolve_float/resolve_char_literal are only invoked from check_literals (function bodies) and check_declaration_literals (global initializers). Enumerator values, record bitfield widths, and static_assert conditions can also contain IntegerLiteral/FloatLiteral/CharLiteral nodes but are never walked, so an out-of-range literal there won't currently be diagnosed.
acceptance_criteria: Extend sema's literal-resolution pass (or add walk_tag helper) to also validate literals inside TagBody::Enum values, bitfield width exprs, and Decl::StaticAssert/Stmt::StaticAssert conditions; add a FileCheck fixture.
close_reason: Added exhaustive shared AST visitor, migrated validation and name resolution traversal, and covered literal diagnostics in enumerators, bit-field widths, and static assertions.

title: Preserve comment groups inside enum bodies
description: Enum bodies drop comments; the spec lists CommentGroup as an EnumItem. Emit CommentGroup between enumerators (see tests/fixtures/comments.c).
close_reason: Added EnumItem { Comment(CommentGroup) | Enumerator(Enumerator) } and changed TagBody::Enum to Vec<SpannedEnumItem>. Multi-line enum bodies now emit CommentGroup items between enumerators via a new parse_enum_items (mirrors parse_field_items); same-line and inline-typeof enum parsing (parse_enumerators, declarator.rs::parse_enumerator_list) updated to wrap enumerators in EnumItem::Enumerator. reachability.rs updated for the new shape. Fixtures regenerated; cargo nextest/clippy/fmt clean.

title: Clang asm goto duplicate label operand check
description: clang rejects an asm goto that lists the same label twice: 'duplicate use of asm operand name "l1"' (clang 22, verified with clang -fsyntax-only). Clang flavor only. Currently accepted by both the parser and sema (slate-parser-25m.7). Repro: void f(void){ asm goto("" : : : : l1, l1); l1: ; }
close_reason: Implemented Clang duplicate asm goto label operand validation with FileCheck coverage

title: Clang asm goto jump-scope check
description: clang rejects asm goto whose target label is inside a scope it cannot jump into (e.g. a GNU statement expression): 'cannot jump from this asm goto statement to one of its possible targets' (clang 22, JumpDiagnostics.cpp). Clang flavor only, in sema.rs. Sema currently only resolves asm goto labels by name (slate-parser-25m.7). Repro: void f(void){ asm goto("" : : : : l); ({ l: ; }); }
close_reason: Implemented Clang asm goto statement-expression jump-scope validation with FileCheck coverage

title: FileCheck harness error path ignores SLATE-FILECHECK-ISYSTEM
description: tests/filecheck.rs run_error_fixture takes defines and flavor but not isystem paths, while tools/update_filecheck.py render_error passes -isystem. An error fixture that needs an -isystem header would regenerate one diagnostic and be checked against another. Pass isystem through run_error_fixture like run_fixture. Found while fixing slate-parser-niv.

title: update_filecheck.py and tests/filecheck.rs disagree on line numbers when a directive precedes code
description: An error fixture with '// SLATE-FILECHECK-FLAVOR gcc' on line 1 (above the code) regenerates with '╭─[fixture.c:3:14]' but the harness renders '4:14', so fixtures_are_filechecked fails even though the updater output is stable. The updater's fixture_source strips directive lines before rendering; the harness keeps them. Workaround: put SLATE-FILECHECK-* directives after the code (as compiler-flavor-unknown.c does). Found while adding asm-goto-no-labels-gcc.c (slate-parser-25m.5).
close_reason: Harness run_error_fixture now parses a stripped same-directory copy (like run_fixture) and maps its name back; update_filecheck.py render_error mirrors it exactly. Fixes directive-above-code line shifts and CHECK lines leaking into EOF-spanning diagnostics; all 33 error fixtures regenerate unchanged

title: Sema for structured asm
description: Lax sema over structured asm: output operands are modifiable lvalues, goto/%l labels resolve to function labels, register-variable rules (register storage required, no static, no initializer at file scope), clang alternative-count consistency. Low priority: input C is assumed valid.
close_reason: clang-flavor asm sema: output lvalues, alternative counts, asm goto labels, register variable rules

title: Top-level dispatch silently drops later statements when multiple full items share one macro-expanded PPNode
description:
va-arg-22.c fails on a heavy macro-expansion pattern where a single physical source line like 'D(0) D(1)' expands (via a multi-statement macro D) into TWO complete top-level typedef statements packed into one PPNode::Code node (e.g. 'typedef struct{char x[0];}A0; typedef struct{char x[1];}A1;'). The dedicated typedef-with-inline-body dispatch (parser.rs's parse_top_level_item, the 'typedef' text-guard arm feeding into has_inline_body/tag-definition handling) only ever parsed the FIRST such statement per node and returned a node-granularity 'consumed' count that swallowed the whole node, silently dropping the second typedef -- so 'A1' was never registered as a typedef name, and 'A1 a1;' later misparsed as an expression statement ('unexpected tokens after expression').

Notably, the *generic* Code-arm dispatch already had logic for this exact scenario (split_top_level_items + per-item recursive parsing, gated on 'top_level_items.len() > 1 && spelling != expansion' i.e. macro-generated content) but it lived inside one specific match arm, so it never ran for nodes that matched the typedef-specific guard first. Fixed by hoisting that multi-item-split check to the very top of parse_top_level_item (before the match), so ANY node containing multiple complete macro-expanded top-level items -- typedefs, tag definitions, functions, plain declarations -- gets split via split_top_level_items and each item is recursively re-dispatched through parse_top_level_item on its own synthetic single-item node, rather than being hardcoded to only declaration-or-function as the old in-arm special case assumed. Removed the now-superseded old special case from inside the generic Code arm. Affects 1 fixture in wf8.7: va-arg-22.c.
close_reason: Implementation and named generated fixtures already landed; verified with regeneration and full FileCheck suite.

title: Adjacent string literal concatenation not implemented in general expression parsing
description: pr65369.c fails on 'static const char data[] = "123..." "123...";' (two adjacent string literal tokens meant to concatenate per C 6.4.5) with 'expected ;' -- const_expr.rs's parse_primary took exactly one string-literal token and returned, leaving the second literal dangling as an unexpected trailing token. Existing string concatenation support (parser.rs's coalesce_string_literals/concatenated_string_literal) was previously wired into only two narrow call sites (typeof-operand parsing and top-level expression-statement parsing), not into general expression parsing, so any other context hitting adjacent string literals (initializers, function-call arguments, etc.) was still broken. Fixed at the root: parse_primary's string-literal match arm now loops consuming further adjacent string-literal-family tokens and merges them via parser.rs's (now pub(crate)) string_literal_content/concatenated_string_literal helpers, so concatenation works everywhere const_expr expressions are parsed. The two narrow call sites in parser.rs are now redundant but harmless; worth removing in a follow-up cleanup pass. Affects 1 fixture in wf8.7: pr65369.c.
close_reason: Implementation and named generated fixtures already landed; verified with regeneration and full FileCheck suite.

title: const_expr.rs cast/compound-literal type-names don't support a leading __attribute__ before the base type
description: scal-to-vec1.c/scal-to-vec3.c also fail on '(vector(4, float)){2., 2., 2., 2.}' where vector(...) expands to '__attribute__((vector_size(...))) float' -- i.e. the attribute precedes the base type inside a cast/compound-literal type-name, not just trailing it (wf8.6.3 only fixed the trailing case). Two related gaps: (1) const_expr::starts_type_name's Ident arm didn't recognize '__attribute__'/'__attribute', so the '(' was never even detected as starting a type-name/cast, and it fell through to being misparsed as a call expression; (2) try_parse_type_name only called DeclaratorParser::parse_attributes() after the base type, never before it. Fixed by adding '__attribute__'/'__attribute' to starts_type_name, and by parsing (and applying, via apply_vector_attributes) a leading attribute group before take_qualifiers()/parse_base_type() in try_parse_type_name, in addition to the existing trailing one. Affects 2 fixtures in wf8.7: scal-to-vec1.c, scal-to-vec3.c (same fixtures as the starts_declaration bug above -- two independent bugs in the same 2 files).
close_reason: Implementation and named generated fixtures already landed; verified with regeneration and full FileCheck suite.

title: Top-level typedef dispatch guard doesn't strip a leading __extension__ prefix
description: pr71083.c fails on '__extension__ typedef __UINT32_TYPE__ uint32_t;' at top level -- the type never gets registered as a typedef name, so a later 'uint32_t' field type errors as unknown. Root cause: parser.rs's parse_top_level_item dispatches to the dedicated typedef-parsing arm via a guard 'text.trim_start().starts_with("typedef")', which doesn't account for a leading '__extension__ ' prefix (unlike several other dispatch sites in the same file that already strip it). When the guard fails, the line falls through to the generic Code arm and gets parsed as an ordinary Declaration with storage=Typedef instead of the dedicated Decl::Typedef variant, and record_typedefs() only registers names from Decl::Typedef, so the name is silently dropped. Fixed by adding a text_starts_with_typedef() helper that strips one optional leading '__extension__' word before checking, and adjusted the arm's has_inline_body token scan to also skip a leading __extension__ ident (same class of oversight, for the 'typedef struct {...}' inline-body case). Affects 1 fixture in wf8.7: pr71083.c.
close_reason: Implementation and generated fixture already landed; validated with an idempotent regeneration and full FileCheck suite.

title: starts_declaration doesn't recognize a leading __attribute__/__attribute as starting a declaration
description: scal-to-vec1.c/scal-to-vec3.c fail on local declarations like '__attribute__((vector_size(32))) short v0 = {...};' inside a function body -- the general statement dispatch (starts_declaration in parser.rs) checks for storage-class keywords, _Alignas/alignas/__auto_type, and const_expr::starts_type_name, but never for a leading __attribute__ or __attribute token, so such a statement is misparsed as an expression instead of a declaration. Fixed by adding '__attribute__' | '__attribute' to the Ident match arm alongside _Alignas et al. Affects 2 fixtures in wf8.7: scal-to-vec1.c, scal-to-vec3.c.
close_reason: Implementation and named generated fixtures already landed; verified with regeneration and full FileCheck suite.

title: Bare-string-literal initializer shortcut swallowed only one token of a larger expression
description: pr53084.c fails on 'static const char *const foo[] = {"foo" + 1};' -- parser.rs's parse_initializer and const_expr.rs's parse_initializer_value both special-case a leading string-literal token as a complete initializer value (for the char-array-from-string-literal shorthand) and consumed exactly one token unconditionally, regardless of what followed. When the string literal is actually the start of a larger expression ('"foo" + 1'), the '+' was left dangling, which the initializer-list loop then rejected via an assert!(...) panic ('expected  in initializer') instead of a graceful error. Fixed by gating the shortcut on the next token actually being Comma or RBrace in both call sites, and changed the panic to remain (still worth revisiting -- see below) only as a true invariant since the guard now prevents the false trip; the leftover assert! should probably become a proper ParseError in a future pass since it's still user-input-triggerable in other shapes. Affects 1 fixture in wf8.7: pr53084.c.
close_reason: Implementation and generated fixture already landed; validated with an idempotent regeneration and full FileCheck suite.

title: GNU elvis operator (a ?: b) not supported
description: pr68249.c fails on 'm = b || c < 0 || c > 1 ?: c;' with 'unexpected token Colon'. const_expr.rs's parse_conditional always required a then_value between '?' and ':', with no support for the GNU extension where an omitted then-branch reuses the condition's value (evaluated once in real C semantics; our AST just clones the condition expression, which is fine since ConstExpr is cheaply Clone and the parser doesn't model side-effect-once evaluation elsewhere either). Fixed by checking for an immediate ':' after '?' and using a clone of condition as then_value in that case. Affects 1 fixture in wf8.7: pr68249.c.
close_reason: Represented GNU omitted-middle conditionals as ConstExpr::Elvis, preserving single evaluation.

title: const_expr::starts_type_name doesn't recognize target-builtin type names (__builtin_va_list, __m128, ...)
description: pr38151.c fails on '__builtin_va_list ap;' inside a function body with 'unexpected tokens after expression' -- it's parsed as an expression statement instead of a declaration. parser.rs's is_target_builtin_name() (used when actually building the CType via parse_base_type, and by the top-level function-vs-declaration dispatch) already recognizes __builtin_va_list/__m128/__m256/etc, but const_expr.rs's starts_type_name() -- used by the general statement dispatch's starts_declaration() to decide whether a leading identifier begins a declaration -- only special-cased char8_t/atomic_char8_t/nullptr_t. Fixed by making is_target_builtin_name pub(crate) and having starts_type_name's Ident arm call it (superseding the narrower hardcoded list, since is_target_builtin_name already includes those three). Affects 1 fixture in wf8.6: pr38151.c (same fixture as the __extension__ bug -- two independent bugs in one file).
close_reason: Fixed directly in-session; all 250 batch-4 fixtures ported and passing FileCheck

title: __attribute (without trailing double underscore) not recognized as __attribute__ alias
description: pr39120.c fails on 'void __attribute((noinline)) bar() { ... }' with 'expected declaration type, found LParen'. parser.rs's parse_attribute_groups only matched the exact ident __attribute__; GCC also accepts the single-underscore-suffix spelling __attribute. Fixed by also consuming Token::Ident("__attribute") alongside __attribute__ at that one call site. Affects 1 fixture in wf8.6: pr39120.c.
close_reason: Fixed directly in-session; all 250 batch-4 fixtures ported and passing FileCheck

title: const_expr.rs's cast/compound-literal type-name parser drops trailing __attribute__ (breaks vector_size casts)
description: pr123625.c fails on 'BS_VAR_3 = (int64_t __attribute__((vector_size(...)))){};' with 'expected ), found __attribute__'. const_expr.rs's try_parse_type_name (used for casts, sizeof(type), and compound-literal type-names) only calls take_qualifiers before/after the base type, never parse_attribute_groups -- unlike parser.rs's DeclaratorParser::parse_declaration_tokens path, which loops attribute-parsing in with qualifiers. Fixed by: making DeclaratorParser::parse_attributes() and parser.rs's apply_vector_attributes pub(crate), then calling both from try_parse_type_name right after qualifiers are folded into the base type, so attributes like vector_size correctly reshape the CType before the (abstract) declarator is parsed. Affects 1 fixture in wf8.6: pr123625.c.
close_reason: Fixed directly in-session; all 250 batch-4 fixtures ported and passing FileCheck

title: __extension__ not handled as an expression prefix in const_expr.rs
description: pr38151.c fails to parse 'x + y * __extension__ 1i' -- const_expr.rs's parse_unary has no case for a leading __extension__ identifier, so it falls through and misparses as a call/errors. __extension__ was already stripped at several declaration-dispatch call sites in parser.rs (per wf8.5.2's fix) but never handled inside general expression parsing. Fixed by adding a check at the top of parse_unary: consume a leading __extension__ ident and recurse into parse_cast(), matching GNU's 'unary-expression: __extension__ cast-expression' grammar. Affects 1 fixture in wf8.6: pr38151.c.
close_reason: Fixed directly in-session; all 250 batch-4 fixtures ported and passing FileCheck

title: __volatile / __volatile__ GNU keyword aliases not recognized by lexer
description:
ffs-1.c fails to parse `__volatile int a = 0;` ("expected declarator", the lexer treats `__volatile` as a plain identifier so the declarator parser sees `int` after an unexpected leading ident and gets confused).

Root cause: src/lexer.rs's keyword-spelling match (~line 687-701) already recognizes `const`/`__const`/`__const__` as `Keyword::Const` and `__restrict`/`__restrict__` as `Keyword::Restrict`, but line 688 only matches the bare `"volatile"` spelling for `Keyword::Volatile` -- `__volatile` and `__volatile__` are missing from that arm. Same class of bug as the __const fix in wf8.4.5 (see llog/wiki gcc-typeof-aliases-style memory for the pattern).

Fix: change `"volatile" => Token::Keyword(Keyword::Volatile)` to also match `"__volatile" | "__volatile__"`.

Affects 1 fixture in this batch: ffs-1.c.
close_reason: Both remaining triaged bugs fixed; batch complete, all 250 fixtures pass FileCheck

title: GNU old-style field designator (field: value) unsupported in compound-literal initializers
description:
compndlit-1.c fails with "expected `}`, found `:`" on `x = (struct S){ b : 0, a : 0, c : ({ ... }) };" (a compound literal whose initializer uses the obsolete GNU `field: value` designator spelling instead of C99 `.field = value`, plus a GNU statement-expression value -- statement expressions themselves already parse fine per wf8.3.8).

Minimal repro: `struct S { int a; int b; }; struct S x; void f(void) { x = (struct S){ a: 1, b: 2 }; }` fails; the same designator syntax at top level (`struct S x = { a: 1, b: 2 };`) already works.

Root cause: there are two separate initializer-list parsers. src/parser.rs's `parse_initializer` (~line 2627-2670, used for top-level/local declaration initializers) already recognizes the old-style form via an `else if let Some(Token::Ident(name)) = ... && tokens.value_at(pos+1) == Some(&Token::Colon)` branch (~line 2654-2658) alongside the C99 `.field =` form. src/const_expr.rs's `parse_initializer_list` (~line 1022-1069, used for compound-literal initializers reached via `parse_compound_literal`/ConstExpr::CompoundLiteral) only handles `[index] =` and `.field =` designators (~line 1030-1059) and has no equivalent ident-then-colon branch, so it stops at the bare identifier and then errors when it hits the unexpected `:`.

Fix: port the same ident+colon lookahead branch from parser.rs's parse_initializer into const_expr.rs's parse_initializer_list.

Affects 1 fixture in this batch: compndlit-1.c.
close_reason: Both remaining triaged bugs fixed; batch complete, all 250 fixtures pass FileCheck

title: __attribute__((aligned)) with no arguments rejected as invalid
description:
990326-1.c and alloca-1.c both use the bare, argument-less GNU form `__attribute__((aligned))` (e.g. `struct c { unsigned int c : 4, b : 14, a : 14; } __attribute__((aligned));` in 990326-1.c, and `int x __attribute__((aligned));` inside a struct field in alloca-1.c). This spelling means 'use the maximum useful alignment for the target' per GCC docs (on x86-64 that's typically 16, driven by the widest vector type GCC will use by default), as opposed to `aligned(N)` which takes an explicit constant.

Root cause: src/parser.rs's attribute-argument parser (~line 1404-1412, the `match canonical_name { "aligned" => ... }` arm) only builds `Attribute::Aligned(ConstExpr)` when `single_int()` finds exactly one IntLit argument or `parse_attribute_expression` succeeds on a non-empty argument list; when `arguments` is empty it falls through to `None => invalid_attribute(name, arguments)`, which src/sema.rs:246-251 (`check_attributes`) turns into a hard 'invalid arguments for attribute aligned' semantic error.

Fix needs a decision on what constant to synthesize for the argument-less form (`Attribute::Aligned` requires a `ConstExpr`, there's no 'default' variant) -- e.g. `ConstExpr::Integer(16)` matching this project's x86_64-linux-gnu target predefines (src/predefines/clang_x86_64_linux_gnu.h), added as a special case in the "aligned" arm before falling through to `invalid_attribute`.

Affects 2 fixtures in this batch: 990326-1.c, alloca-1.c.
close_reason: Argument-less __attribute__((aligned)) now resolves to __BIGGEST_ALIGNMENT__, looked up live from the preprocessor's macro table (Parser::biggest_alignment, resolved once after preprocessing via resolve_biggest_alignment(&pp.macros)) rather than a hardcoded duplicate constant. Threaded through parse_attribute_groups/parse_attribute (both now take biggest_alignment: i64) and DeclaratorParser (new biggest_alignment field, Parser call sites use with_biggest_alignment; the one const_expr.rs-originated DeclaratorParser::new() caller falls back to FALLBACK_BIGGEST_ALIGNMENT=16, same value, since that path has no live macro access). Ported 990326-1.c and alloca-1.c.

title: Leading __extension__ not stripped before top-level tag-definition dispatch
description:
991228-1.c fails to parse `__extension__ union { double d; int i[2]; } u = {d : -0.25};` at top level ("expected `(`" with a garbled/OutOfBounds diagnostic location). Minimal repro: `__extension__ union { double d; int i[2]; } u = {d : -0.25};` -- removing the leading `__extension__` makes it parse cleanly (confirms the union body + old-style field-designator initializer are both already supported; only the prefix handling is missing).

Root cause: `__extension__` is a GNU no-op silencing prefix that several call sites in src/parser.rs already skip explicitly (grep for `Token::Ident("__extension__".to_string())` at parser.rs:209, 2377, 3000), but parse_top_level_item's tag-keyword-index scan (src/parser.rs ~line 599-621, the loop that skips storage-class keywords like static/extern/const to find the struct/union/enum keyword) does not also skip a leading `__extension__` identifier token. So for a top-level item starting with `__extension__ union ...`, `tag_keyword_index` stays at 0 (pointing at the `__extension__` ident, not `union`), the struct/union/enum dispatch check at line ~622 fails to match, and the item falls through to the generic declaration/signature parsing path, which chokes on the union body.

Fix: extend the tag_keyword_index skip loop (and likely the equivalent skip-loop inside parse_tag_definition itself, ~line 728-746, which also doesn't special-case __extension__) to also consume a leading `__extension__` token, consistent with the other three call sites that already strip it.

Affects 1 fixture in this batch: 991228-1.c.
close_reason: Fixed two separate spots that failed to skip a leading __extension__: (1) parse_top_level_item's tag_keyword_index scan now also skips __extension__ so 'extension__ union {...}' at file scope dispatches to parse_tag_definition instead of falling through to the generic declaration path; parse_tag_definition itself now strips a leading __extension__ prefix (extension_prefix, folded into node0_offset for the same-line trailing-token alignment fixed in wf8.4.4). (2) starts_declaration (used by local/statement-level parsing) treated '__extension__ union {...}' as not starting a declaration at all since __extension__ isn't a storage-class keyword or a typedef name, so it fell into expression-statement parsing and errored; it now looks past a leading __extension__ before checking. parse_declaration_tokens already stripped __extension__ once dispatched, so only detection needed fixing. Ported 991228-1.c.

title: Parse macro-expanded bit-field declaration in 20040629-1.c
description: After slate-parser-wf8.4.1 permits the fixture's terminating driver-macro self-include, tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20040629-1.c advances from IncludeCycle to parser error 'unexpected tokens after declaration' at FIELDS1 unsigned int i : 6, j : 11, k : 15. The empty FIELDS1 macro is expanded before parsing, so this is an independent record-field/bit-field parsing issue. Fix it and port 20040629-1.c plus dependent 20040705-{1,2}.c to FileCheck.
notes: Correction: 20040629-1.c now parses successfully after the self-include fix. The remaining parser error occurs in dependent 20040705-{1,2}.c, which define FIELDS1 as 'long long l;' before including 20040629-1.c; parsing then fails at the following bit-field declaration.
close_reason: Split macro-expanded semicolon-separated record fields and ported all three affected GCC torture fixtures.

title: __const (GNU alias for const) not recognized by lexer
description:
tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20111208-1.c fails with "expected
`Comma` between parameters" pointing at `__const` in:

    extern void *memcpy(void *__restrict __dest, __const void *__restrict __src,
                        size_t __n) __attribute__((__nothrow__))
    __attribute__((__nonnull__(1, 2)));

Minimal repro:

    void f(__const void *p);

Root cause: src/lexer.rs recognizes `__restrict`/`__restrict__` as
`Keyword::Restrict` (line 701) and `_Complex`/`__complex__`/`__complex` as
`Keyword::Complex`, but has no equivalent alias for `const` -- only the
literal spelling `const` maps to `Keyword::Const`. GCC/glibc headers use
`__const` pervasively (so headers work under `-std=c89`/strict modes where
plain `const` might be a macro-able identifier). `__const` therefore lexes
as a plain `Token::Ident("__const")`.

Downstream, `DeclaratorParser::parse_base_type` has a catch-all arm
`Token::Ident(name) => CType::Named(name)` (src/parser.rs, end of the big
match in `parse_base_type`) with no typedef-name check guarding it, so
`__const` gets silently accepted as a bogus named type instead of erroring
or being treated as a qualifier. That consumes `__const` as the *entire*
second parameter's type, leaving `void *__restrict __src` to be parsed as
its declarator -- but `void` can't start a declarator, so
`parse_declarator`'s `allow_abstract` fallback yields `Declarator::Abstract`
without consuming anything, and the parameter-list loop then expects `,`
or `)` and instead finds `void`, producing "expected `Comma` between
parameters" (location is approximate/misattributed, per
parser-diagnostic-token-spans -- points near `__const`, the true start of
the malformed parameter, rather than the exact `void` token).

Fix sketch: add `"__const" | "__const__"` alongside `"const"` in the
lexer's keyword table (mirroring the existing `__restrict`/`__complex`
alias handling).

Affects 1 fixture in this batch: 20111208-1.c. Likely affects other
not-yet-ported fixtures too, since `__const` is common in glibc-style
header declarations.
close_reason: Recognized GNU __const aliases and added generated FileCheck coverage for 20111208-1.c.

title: parse_tag_definition's trailing-declarator scan doesn't look past the closing-brace node
description:
Two fixtures fail because the tag/typedef alias declarator, initializer,
or terminating `;` that follows a struct/union/enum body spills onto a
PPNode *after* the one where the closing `}` was found, and
`parse_tag_definition` (src/parser.rs, ~line 680) never looks past that one
node.

**20100416-1.c** ("expected declaration type, found LBrace"). Minimal repro:

    struct test {
      long long val;
      int       ret;
    } tests[] = {
        {1, -1}, {2, 1},
    };

Struct body spans lines 1-4 (multiple PPNodes, since each source line is
its own PPNode::Code), so the *fallback* multi-line-body branch of
`parse_tag_definition` runs (the one starting ~line 828, mirroring the
`single-line-tag-body-brace-bug` fix but for the trailing side). It finds
`close` = the node index containing the struct's closing `}` (line 4:
`} tests[] = {`), builds the record decl from `nodes[1..close]`, then looks
for a trailing alias declarator *only* in `nodes[close]` (~line 870-882:
`if let PPNodeKind::Code { .. } = &nodes[close].value { let closing_tokens
= self.node_tokens(&nodes[close]); ... }`). It correctly parses `tests[]`
as the alias declarator (stopping at `=`), but then hard-codes
`consumed = close + 1` (~line 882) -- so nodes for line 5 (the actual
initializer body, `{1, -1}, {2, 1},`) and line 6 (`};`) are never consumed
by this declaration at all. The top-level loop then tries to parse line 5
as a *new* top-level item, which starts with `{` and immediately fails
with "expected declaration type, found LBrace". (Confirmed: the same
source with the initializer joined onto one line, e.g.
`} tests[] = { {1,-1}, {2,1}, };`, parses fine -- it's entirely a node-count
bug, not an initializer-parsing bug.) Also note: even when this doesn't
error (e.g. a non-nested-brace initializer `tests[] = {1, 2};` all on one
line), `build_tag_alias_decl` still silently drops the initializer --
`Declaration.initializer` is hardcoded `None` (src/parser.rs
`build_tag_alias_decl`, added in slate-parser-wf8.3.7) since that fix only
needed to plumb the *declarator* through, not an initializer. Fixing the
node-scanning here should also thread the initializer through.

**20050215-1.c** ("expected declaration type, found Semi"). Minimal repro
(needs `__ELF__` predefined, true for this project's default Linux target):

    typedef struct {
      char c[8];
    } V
    #ifdef __ELF__
        __attribute__((aligned(8)))
    #endif
        ;

Here the struct body closes on the *same* line as `} V` (line "} V"), so
the *same-line fast path* of `parse_tag_definition` runs instead (the
`matching_brace` branch starting ~line 724). `trailing_tokens` is computed
as `tokens[same_line_close + 1..]` from *that single node* only, i.e. just
`V` (nothing else -- the `#ifdef`/`__attribute__`/`#endif`/`;` are later,
separate PPNodes since the `#ifdef`/`#endif` directives force a node
break). The new trailing-declarator parsing (`DeclaratorParser` +
`declarator.name()`) happily parses `V` as a complete `Declarator::Name`
and returns `Ok((decls, 1))` -- consuming only the first node. The
`__attribute__((aligned(8)))` line then gets reparsed as a bogus new
top-level item on its own, which eventually hits the bare `;` on the next
line and fails with "expected declaration type, found Semi".

Both are the same underlying gap: the code that looks for "what comes
after the tag body's `}` " only ever inspects the single PPNode it already
has in hand (either `nodes[0]` for the same-line path, or `nodes[close]`
for the multi-line path), instead of scanning forward across further
PPNodes -- attributes, declarator, initializer, terminating `;` -- the way
`declaration_node_span`/`signature_node_span` already do for plain
(non-tag) declarations elsewhere in this file. Fixing both call sites
likely wants a shared helper: given a starting node index, walk forward
(joining node text/tokens as needed, same pattern as
`join_node_text`/`nodes_tokens`) until a top-level `;` is found, then parse
attributes + declarator + `= initializer` from that combined span, and
return the correct total node count consumed.

Affects 2 fixtures in this batch: 20050215-1.c, 20100416-1.c.
close_reason: Fixed token-index misalignment in tag_trailing_tokens same-line branch: same_line_close was computed against the typedef/storage-class-trimmed tokens slice but tag_trailing_tokens indexed into raw node tokens, causing an off-by-N (is_typedef + skip count) misread. Adding node0_offset fixes both original repros (20050215-1.c, 20100416-1.c) without regressing single-line-tag-body/20050107-1/gnu_libc_algorithms/array_indexed_struct_field_named_enum.

title: __builtin_va_arg (and va_arg macro) unsupported
description:
8 fixtures in this batch fail on `__builtin_va_arg`/`va_arg`:
20041214-1.c (`__builtin_va_arg(ap, unsigned long int)`) and
931004-{2,4,6,8,10,12,14}.c (`va_arg(ap, struct tiny)` etc., where
`va_arg(ap, type)` is `#define`d as `__builtin_va_arg(ap, type)` in
clang's <__stdarg_va_arg.h>).

Errors seen: "expected `)`, found `long`" / "expected `)`, found `tiny`" --
both are the *second argument's type keyword* (`long`, `struct`) leaking
past a failed expression parse.

Root cause: `__builtin_va_arg` has no special-cased handling in
const_expr.rs, unlike `__builtin_offsetof`/`__builtin_bit_cast`/
`__builtin_types_compatible_p`/`_Generic` (see `parse_primary` in
src/const_expr.rs, ~line 1299-1305, which dispatches those by name before
falling through to `ConstExpr::Identifier`). So `__builtin_va_arg(ap, T)`
falls through to being parsed as a plain call: `ConstExpr::Identifier(
"__builtin_va_arg")` applied to comma-separated *assignment-expressions*.
The first argument (`ap`) parses fine as an identifier. The second argument
is a type-name (`long`, or `struct tiny`), not an expression -- and because
`parse_primary`'s fallback for any bare keyword is
`Some(Token::Keyword(keyword)) => Ok(ConstExpr::Identifier(<&str>::from(*keyword).into()))`
(so `struct` gets swallowed as a bogus one-word "identifier" expression
named "struct"), the parser then expects `,` or `)` and instead finds the
tag name (`tiny`) or, for `long`, expects `)` and finds `long` directly
since `long` alone isn't consumed as an identifier-keyword substitute the
same way -- either way the type-name never gets parsed as a type, so the
argument list desyncs.

Fix sketch: add a `__builtin_va_arg` case alongside offsetof/bit_cast in
`parse_primary`, parsing `(<assignment-expr>, <type-name>)` via
`try_parse_type_name` (same helper `parse_offsetof`/`parse_bit_cast`
already use) and producing a new `ConstExpr::VaArg { ap: Box<Self>, ty:
Box<CType>, declarator: Declarator }` variant. Per
wiki/concepts/ast-enum-touchpoints.md's "Adding a ConstExpr variant"
checklist: update `impl Display for ConstExpr`, `Parser::evaluate_expr`
(-> `ConstExprError::NotConstant("va_arg")`), and
`sema.rs::is_integer_constant_expression` (-> `false`).

Affects 8 fixtures in this batch: 20041214-1.c, 931004-2.c, 931004-4.c,
931004-6.c, 931004-8.c, 931004-10.c, 931004-12.c, 931004-14.c.
close_reason: Implemented __builtin_va_arg parsing and builtin va_list type support; regenerated affected FileCheck fixtures.

title: Top-level dispatch mishandles a macro expansion emitting multiple sibling declarations
description:
tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20040709-1.c fails with "expected `(`"
at a `return y.k;` line inside a macro *definition* (misattributed span,
per parser-diagnostic-token-spans) -- the real failure is at the macro's
*use site*.

Minimal repro:

    struct A { unsigned int k; };
    #define T(S) struct S s##S; struct S retme##S(struct S x) { return x; }
    T(A)

`T(A)` expands (after `##` pasting) to two sibling top-level constructs on
one logical line: `struct A sA;` (a plain declaration) followed by
`struct A retmeA(struct A x) { return x; }` (a function definition). Both
land in a single PPNode::Code (macro expansion of one invocation is one
node), fails to parse.

Root cause: `Parser::parse_top_level_item` (src/parser.rs, the
`PPNodeKind::Code { .. }` arm around line 537 onward) assumes a given
PPNode contains *at most one* top-level construct. Its `looks_like_declaration`
heuristic (~line 631) is: find the first top-level `{` and first top-level
`=`; if there's a `{` with no preceding `=`, treat the *entire* remaining
token stream as one function definition (falls through to
`self.parse_function(nodes)` at line 671). It never checks whether a
top-level `;` occurs *before* that `{` -- which would mean an earlier,
separate declaration ends there and the `{` belongs to a second,
independent top-level item. So `struct A sA; struct A retmeA(...) { ... }`
gets treated as a single function-definition parse, and `parse_function`
(or whatever it delegates to for the signature) trips over the stray
`struct A sA;` prefix once it starts looking for the parameter list's `(`.

Fix sketch: before committing to `has_lbrace` / `looks_like_declaration`
dispatch, scan for a top-level `;` that occurs strictly before
`first_lbrace` (already computed). If found, split the token stream there,
parse the prefix as one or more declarations via the existing
split_top_level+declaration_prefix_end machinery (same as the comma-list
handling already at line ~645), and then re-run this same
function-vs-declaration dispatch on the remainder -- likely as a loop that
returns a `Vec<Decl>` combining both, still consuming the same PPNode span
(since a single macro-expanded node can't be partially consumed).

Affects 1 fixture in this batch: 20040709-1.c.
close_reason: Split macro-emitted sibling top-level declarations and functions; ported 20040709-1.c and regenerated affected fixtures.

title: Recursive self-include with driver-macro guard misdetected as include cycle
description:
tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20040629-1.c (and 20040705-1.c,
20040705-2.c which #include it) fails with "include cycle detected:
.../20040629-1.c".

The fixture's top-level shape is:

    #ifndef T
      ... declarations ...
      #define T(n, pre, post, op)  ... /* generates functions using n */
      #include "20040629-1.c"          /* <-- self-include, T now defined */
      #undef T
      ... more code, then a second, differently-defined T + #include again ...
    #else
      #define opadd(x, y) ...           /* only reached when T IS defined */
      T(1, ...) T(2, ...) ...           /* expands the caller's T macro */
    #endif

This is a deliberate, terminating recursive-template idiom used by several
gcc-torture fixtures: the file includes itself while a driver macro (T) is
defined, and on the nested pass `#ifndef T` is false so it takes the
`#else` branch and expands `T(...)` using whatever the *including* level
just #defined. Recursion depth is always exactly 1 (the `#else` branch
never re-includes), so it always terminates.

Root cause: src/pp/include.rs `resolve_and_parse_include` rejects any
self-include of a file already on `open_stack` unless
`src/pp/mod.rs::include_guard` recognized it as a conventional header
guard (see the `guarded-self-includes` wiki memory / llog). `include_guard`
only matches a file whose *entire* body is a single `#ifndef X` conditional
with exactly one branch and an immediate `#define X` as the branch's first
item (src/pp/mod.rs:626-648). This fixture's `#ifndef T ... #else ... #endif`
has two branches and no `#define T` right after the `#ifndef`, so
`include_guard` returns `None`, `include_guards` has no entry for the file,
and `resolve_and_parse_include` unconditionally raises `IncludeCycle`.

Even if `include_guard` were loosened to accept the 2-branch `#ifndef X /
#else / #endif` shape, the existing skip behavior in
`resolve_and_parse_include` (return `Ok(Vec::new())`, i.e. treat the
re-include as a no-op) would be *semantically wrong* here: the whole point
of this idiom is that the nested pass produces different, real output (the
`#else` branch's function definitions), not nothing. A correct fix needs to
actually let the preprocessor recurse into the file again and parse its
`#else` branch for real, rather than either erroring or silently skipping.
That likely means: only treat same-file re-entry as a hard cycle when doing
so would recurse without bound (e.g. track a recursion depth per file and
cap it, or detect that the exact same macro state repeats) rather than
flagging every re-entrant self-include unconditionally.

Repro (minimal):

    #ifndef T
    #define T() int x;
    #include "self.c"
    #undef T
    #else
    T()
    #endif

(saved as self.c, included via `-include` or from another file) currently
raises "include cycle detected" instead of expanding to `int x;` once.

Affects 3 fixtures in this batch: 20040629-1.c, 20040705-1.c, 20040705-2.c.
close_reason: Allowed self-includes when macro state changes; added driver-macro FileCheck coverage and preserved unguarded cycle rejection.

title: 20030910-1.c: GNU __real/__imag complex part operators
description: tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20030910-1.c uses the GNU '__real'/'__imag' operators to take the real/imaginary part of a __complex value, including taking its address: 'double *dp = &(__real dc);'. Parser fails with 'unexpected tokens after expression', meaning __real/__imag aren't recognized as unary operators producing an lvalue.
close_reason: Fixed and ported to FileCheck fixtures

title: 20020402-3.c: register storage-class specifier on function parameters
description: tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20020402-3.c declares function parameters and locals with 'register' (e.g. 'blockvector_for_pc_sect(register CORE_ADDR pc, ...)' and 'register struct block *b;'). Parser fails with 'expected declaration type, found Keyword(Register)' (diagnostic location is misattributed to an earlier struct, a known class of issue per parser-diagnostic-token-spans). Need to accept 'register' as a storage-class specifier in parameter-declaration and local-declaration contexts.
close_reason: Fixed and ported to FileCheck fixtures

title: 20011113-1.c: typedef combining a tag definition with a pointer declarator
description: tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20011113-1.c has 'typedef struct t { ... } *T;' -- the typedef name T is declared via a pointer declarator alongside the inline tag definition. Later uses of T (e.g. 'T bar(U, unsigned int);') fail sema with 'unknown type name T', meaning T never gets registered in the typedef namespace when the declarator is a pointer rather than a bare name.
close_reason: Fixed and ported to FileCheck fixtures

title: GNU statement expressions '({ ... })' unsupported
description: Both tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20020206-1.c ('d = ({ ({ bar(); }); });') and 20020320-1.c ('fixed = ({ int temp1 = 2; temp1; }) - ({ int temp2 = 1; temp2; });') use the GNU statement-expression extension, where a braced compound statement is used as an expression. Parser fails with 'unexpected token LBrace' at the opening brace of the outer struct/function context (diagnostic location looks misattributed per the parser-diagnostic-token-spans issue, but root cause is missing statement-expression support in the expression grammar).
close_reason: Fixed and ported to FileCheck fixtures

title: 20001203-2.c: nested tag definition with pointer declarator as a field
description: tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20001203-2.c declares a nested tag inline as a field type with a pointer declarator: 'struct field { union field_location {...} loc; ...; } *fields;' inside struct type. Parser fails with 'unexpected token LBrace'. Likely the nested-record-field-declarator handling (see wiki concept for nested record fields) doesn't cover a nested tag definition whose enclosing field declarator is a pointer.
close_reason: Fixed and ported to FileCheck fixtures

title: 20010325-1.c: wide/narrow string literal concatenation and literal indexing
description: tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20010325-1.c has 'if (L"a" "b"[1] != L'b') abort();' -- adjacent wide+narrow string literal concatenation, then subscripting the concatenated literal. Parser fails with 'unexpected tokens after expression'. Need support for mixed-width adjacent string literal concatenation and indexing a string literal expression directly.
close_reason: Fixed and ported to FileCheck fixtures

title: 20000717-4.c: struct tag and member sharing an identifier
description: tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20000717-4.c declares 'struct slot { int field[6]; } slot[4];' inside an outer struct: the tag name 'slot' and the member name 'slot' are the same identifier, which is legal C (tags and ordinary identifiers are separate namespaces). Sema fails with 'unknown tag slot' when resolving 's.slot[0]', suggesting the tag and member namespaces are getting confused during lookup.
close_reason: Fixed and ported to FileCheck fixtures

title: 20000917-1.c: compound literal directly after return
description: tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20000917-1.c has 'int3 one(void) { return (int3){1, 1, 1}; }' -- a compound literal used directly as a return expression. Parser fails with 'unexpected token LBrace', so compound-literal parsing isn't reachable from the return-statement expression context.
close_reason: Fixed and ported to FileCheck fixtures

title: 20000402-1.c: #if constant expression rejects ull-suffixed integers
description: tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20000402-1.c has '#if ULONG_LONG_MAX != 18446744073709551615ull && ...'. The preprocessor's #if integer-constant-expression evaluator fails with 'invalid #if expression: invalid integer constant expression' on the ull suffix. Need to accept standard integer suffixes (u/l/ll in any case/order) when evaluating #if expressions.
close_reason: Fixed: widened Add/Sub/Mul in const_expr.rs evaluate_expr to compute in i128 and truncate, and fixed lexer.rs integer_value() to bit-reinterpret u64 literals instead of clamping to i64::MAX. Migrated 20000402-1.c.

title: 20000227-1.c: raw non-UTF-8 byte in string literal
description: Upstream torture fixture tests/upstream/fixtures.gcc-torture/20000227-1.c embeds a literal raw 0xff byte inside a narrow string literal (alongside an equivalent \377 octal escape), which is valid C but not valid UTF-8. The lexer/parse pipeline requires the source stream to be valid UTF-8 and rejects the file with 'failed to read source: stream did not contain valid UTF-8'. Needs either byte-oriented source reading or a documented decision to skip such fixtures.
close_reason: Fixed: added decode_source_bytes()/raw_byte_for_char() in src/files.rs to round-trip non-UTF-8 source bytes through Vec<char> via private-use codepoints (U+10FF00-U+10FFFF), instead of requiring strict UTF-8. Migrated 20000227-1.c.

title: Apply declarator shape before sema void-object validation
description: After prior-enumerator resolution, split-5.c reaches sema and incorrectly diagnoses 'static void *s1[10]' and s2 as objects of type void. The declaration base type is void, but the pointer/array declarator makes the declared object type valid; sema's void-object check is ignoring or incompletely applying the declarator shape.
acceptance_criteria: Sema accepts objects declared through pointer/array declarators over void while continuing to reject actual void objects, and split-5.c advances past s1/s2.
close_reason: Applied declarator shape before void-object validation; added generated valid/invalid coverage and advanced split-5 past s1/s2.

title: Resolve prior enumerators in enum initializer expressions
description: After nested comma-separated record fields were fixed, split-5.c reaches libc-shim signal.h and fails on 'SS_FLAG_BITS = SS_AUTODISARM' because enum initializer evaluation treats the previously declared enumerator SS_AUTODISARM as an unsupported identifier. The diagnostic also falls back to the main fixture instead of the header token.
acceptance_criteria: Enum initializer expressions can reference earlier enumerators in the same enum, split-5.c advances past SS_FLAG_BITS, and any evaluation error retains the initializer's source span.
close_reason: Implemented across multiline, same-line, and nested enum parsers with generated coverage; split-5.c advances to wf8.2.18.

title: Support comma-separated fields in nested record types
description: After multi-declarator typedef support, split-5.c advances to bits/x86_64/signal.h and fails on the valid nested anonymous-struct field declaration 'unsigned short significand[4], exponent, padding[3];'. DeclaratorParser::parse_field_list handles only one declarator per field statement, unlike the top-level record parser paths.
acceptance_criteria: Nested struct/union type bodies parse comma-separated field declarators with shared specifiers, including mixed scalar and array fields, and split-5.c advances past the _fpstate._st declaration.
close_reason: Implemented and covered mixed array/scalar nested record fields; split-5.c advances to wf8.2.17.

title: Support comma-separated typedef declarators
description: Valid declarations such as 'typedef long long greg_t, gregset_t[23];' currently stop at the comma with 'expected ;'. The diagnostic now points to the real comma, but the parser should split typedef declarators and apply the shared declaration specifiers to each alias.
acceptance_criteria: Comma-separated typedef declarators produce one typedef declaration per alias, including array and pointer declarators, and split-5.c advances past the greg_t/gregset_t declaration.
close_reason: Implemented and covered scalar, array, and pointer aliases; split-5.c advances to the separate nested-record field issue wf8.2.16.

title: has-include-predicates.c: checker.h not found during FileCheck rendering
description: The FileCheck renderer fails tests/fixtures/has-include-predicates.c because its explicit #include <checker.h> cannot be resolved. Diagnose whether fixture include-path metadata or the harness omits the fixture support directory, then make the fixture render under the standard cargo nextest invocation.
acceptance_criteria: cargo nextest r --no-fail-fast renders and checks tests/fixtures/has-include-predicates.c successfully without weakening header lookup behavior.
close_reason: Fixed and verified with fixture regeneration; full nextest advances past all three fixtures.

title: cpp__embed-13.c: #embed __FILE__ needs __FILE__ support
description: tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/cpp__embed-13.c fails with 'expected resource name after #embed' because it writes '#embed __FILE__ limit(128)', and __FILE__ is not implemented (falls through macro expansion as a bare unexpanded Ident instead of a StringLit, so the #embed resource-name parser rejects it). This is the exact same root cause already tracked by slate-parser-wf8.2.2 (#embed directive unsupported, itself blocked on slate-parser-ojp.8's __FILE__/__LINE__/#line work) -- not an independent bug.
acceptance_criteria: Once slate-parser-ojp.8 implements __FILE__, cpp__embed-13.c parses without further work here.
close_reason: Fixed by slate-parser-ojp.8: __FILE__ is now implemented, so #embed __FILE__ resolves correctly. cpp__embed-13.c parses and its FileCheck block was regenerated.

title: c23-complit-1.c: compound literal inside parameter-list array bound breaks function-body detection
description: tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/c23-complit-1.c fails with 'expected function body'. The fixture declares parameters whose array bound is a compound-literal expression, e.g. 'void f(int a[(int){x}]);' and 'void g(int a, int b[fp((int[2]){a, a + 2})]) { ... }'. Likely cause: whatever brace/paren-depth scan locates the function's parameter-list close and body open (matching_paren/matching_brace or signature_node_span in src/parser.rs) doesn't account for a compound literal's own '{ ... }' appearing inside the '[...]' array-bound expression within the parameter list, so it either closes the parameter scan too early or misidentifies where the real body '{' is. Uninvestigated beyond confirming the repro. Repro: ./target/release/slate-parser parse tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/c23-complit-1.c -isystem$HOME/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include -isystem/usr/lib/clang/22/include
acceptance_criteria: c23-complit-1.c parses, including both the prototype-only and defined-with-body forms of a compound-literal array bound in a parameter list.
close_reason: Fixed and verified with fixture regeneration; full nextest advances past all three fixtures.

title: guality__pr59776.c: struct field with multiple comma-separated declarators (float f, g;) misparsed
description: tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/guality__pr59776.c fails sema with 'unknown type name `g`' for 'struct S { float f, g; };'. Root cause: parse_tag_definition's same-line/matching_brace fast path (src/parser.rs, around the 'let mut fields = Vec::new(); for mut segment in split_top_level(body_tokens, &Token::Semi)' loop near line 745) only splits the struct body on top-level Semi, then hands each whole segment (e.g. 'float f, g') to parse_field_declaration_tokens as a single field -- it never further splits on top-level Comma the way parse_top_level_item's declaration path does (see its 'split_top_level(declaration_tokens, &Token::Comma)' call). So a field statement declaring more than one name off a shared base type breaks. Repro: ./target/release/slate-parser parse tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/guality__pr59776.c -isystem$HOME/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include -isystem/usr/lib/clang/22/include
acceptance_criteria: 'struct S { float f, g; };' and similar multi-declarator field statements parse into one FieldDecl per name, matching how multi-declarator top-level declarations already work.
close_reason: Fixed and verified with fixture regeneration; full nextest advances past all three fixtures.

title: torture__vec-cvt-1.c: unexpected tokens after expression
description: tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/torture__vec-cvt-1.c fails with an 'unexpected tokens after expression'-class error inside a macro-heavy FLTTEST-style body (nested backslash-continued #define expanding to a for-loop with volatile locals, comma expressions in the for-init/step, and an embedded asm("")). Uninvestigated beyond confirming the repro; may be a comma-expression-in-for-clause parsing gap, or an artifact of macro expansion inside a multi-line #define. Repro: ./target/release/slate-parser parse tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/torture__vec-cvt-1.c -isystem$HOME/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include -isystem/usr/lib/clang/22/include
acceptance_criteria: torture__vec-cvt-1.c parses; root cause documented in the fix.
close_reason: Recognized GCC __typeof/__typeof_unqual aliases, added focused generated cast coverage, generated torture__vec-cvt-1.c checks, and verified the full nextest suite passes.

title: torture__bitint-1.c: panic on _BitInt literal suffix (1wbu)
description: tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/torture__bitint-1.c panics (not a clean error) at src/parser.rs's initializer-expression handling: 'unsupported initializer expression: invalid floating literal `1wbu`'. Root cause: C23 _BitInt integer-literal suffixes like wb/uwb/WB/UWB are not recognized by the number-literal parsing in src/const_expr.rs (FloatLiteral::parse or wherever integer suffixes are classified), so a bit-precise integer literal like 1wbu falls through to float-literal parsing and panics instead of erroring cleanly or being parsed as a _BitInt-typed integer constant. Repro: ./target/release/slate-parser parse tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/torture__bitint-1.c -isystem$HOME/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include -isystem/usr/lib/clang/22/include
acceptance_criteria: _BitInt integer-literal suffixes (wb/uwb, case-insensitive) parse as integer constants instead of panicking; no panic anywhere in the crate for any literal suffix (unsupported forms should return a ParseError, never panic).
close_reason: Accepted wb/uwb/wbu suffix orders case-insensitively, propagated initializer literal errors without panic, and generated regression coverage; full suite advances to wf8.2.10.

title: split-5.c: expected ; parse error
description: tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/split-5.c fails to parse with 'expected `;`' and a malformed diagnostic label ('Failed to read contents for label ... OutOfBounds'), meaning the error location itself is out of bounds of the reported source -- likely a second, independent bug in how the error's Loc/offset is computed for whatever construct trips the parser here. Uninvestigated beyond confirming the repro. Repro: ./target/release/slate-parser parse tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/split-5.c -isystem$HOME/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include -isystem/usr/lib/clang/22/include
acceptance_criteria: split-5.c parses (or fails with a correctly-located diagnostic if some construct is legitimately unsupported), and the OutOfBounds label rendering bug is fixed or explained.
notes: The malformed OutOfBounds diagnostic was fixed by preserving preprocessor token expansion spans through typedef parsing and by making error_at_tokens walk backward past synthetic/unreadable tokens to the nearest valid source token. The resulting error identifies bits/x86_64/signal.h:66:25 and the comma in 'typedef long long greg_t, gregset_t[23];'. Actual support for this valid multi-declarator typedef is split into slate-parser-wf8.2.15.
close_reason: Fixed the malformed diagnostic and identified the valid unsupported construct; parser support continues in slate-parser-wf8.2.15.

title: pr85388-4.c / split-4.c: include cycle detected in sys/time.h
description: Both tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/pr85388-4.c and tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/split-4.c fail to parse with 'include cycle detected: .../libc-shim/include/sys/time.h', pointing at sys/time.h:50 '#include <sys/time.h>' (a self-include). Root cause is unconfirmed: could be a real self-include bug in the libc-shim's sys/time.h (missing/broken include guard or pragma once interaction), or a slate-parser #include_next/search-path resolution bug that makes the guard ineffective. Repro: ./target/release/slate-parser parse tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/pr85388-4.c -isystem$HOME/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include -isystem/usr/lib/clang/22/include
acceptance_criteria: Both fixtures parse without an include-cycle error, and it's documented in the fix which side (libc-shim header vs. slate-parser #include handling) had the bug.
close_reason: Fixed preprocessor cycle detection to honor defined include guards; pr85388-4.c, split-4.c, and a hermetic guarded-self-include fixture pass while the unguarded cycle fixture still errors.

title: C23 true/false not usable in #if expressions
description: tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/c23-bool-2.c fails: '#if true != 1' hits the #error branch, meaning the preprocessor doesn't treat C23's true/false keywords as 1/0 when evaluating #if without stdbool.h included. Discovered while working wf8.2.4; unrelated to _Generic, pre-existing on main at 4c3ab77.
close_reason: Duplicate/subset of slate-parser-wf8.2.5 (C23 dialect gaps), which already tracks this exact fixture (c23-bool-2.c) plus related digit-separator and imaginary-constant gaps and flags the needed design decision. Closing to avoid duplicate tracking.

title: Investigate remaining scattered gcc-dg failures (include cycle, bitint, misc)
description: Leftover gcc-dg fixtures not yet triaged in depth: pr85388-4.c and split-4.c report 'include cycle detected' (may be an isystem/environment issue rather than a real parser bug -- worth checking header search order before assuming it's a bug); split-5.c hits 'expected ;' (uninvestigated); torture__bitint-1.c panics in FloatLiteral parsing on a _BitInt literal suffix like '1wbu' (src/const_expr.rs FloatLiteral::parse does not recognize BitInt integer-literal suffixes, panics instead of erroring); torture__vec-cvt-1.c hits 'unexpected tokens after expression' (uninvestigated, may just need -isystem flags matching the real update_filecheck.py invocation); guality__pr59776.c fails sema with 'semantic analysis failed' (uninvestigated); c23-complit-1.c hits 'expected function body' (uninvestigated, likely a compound-literal-as-function-body-adjacent parse dispatch issue).
close_reason: Split into concrete per-fixture children for handoff: slate-parser-wf8.2.7 (pr85388-4.c/split-4.c include cycle), slate-parser-wf8.2.8 (split-5.c expected ; + OutOfBounds label bug), slate-parser-wf8.2.9 (torture__bitint-1.c _BitInt suffix panic), slate-parser-wf8.2.10 (torture__vec-cvt-1.c unexpected tokens), slate-parser-wf8.2.11 (guality__pr59776.c multi-declarator struct field), slate-parser-wf8.2.12 (c23-complit-1.c compound literal in parameter-list array bound), slate-parser-wf8.2.13 (cpp__embed-13.c, dup root cause of wf8.2.2/ojp.8).

title: C23 dialect gaps: __STDC_VERSION__ gated headers, digit separators, imaginary _Float16 constants
description: Several gcc-dg fixtures request -std=c23 but our SLATE-FILECHECK-DEFINES DEFAULT config does not define __STDC_VERSION__, so version-gated shim macros (stddef.h's unreachable(), stdbool.h dialect switch) never activate, tripping #error directives in the fixtures (c23-unreachable-1.c, c23-bool-2.c). Separately: c23-digit-separators-1.c hits an obscure interaction between digit separators, token pasting, and a universal-character-name inside a char literal ('expected )'). c23-imaginary-constants-1.c and -7.c: a top-level declaration like '_Complex _Float16 a = ...;' whose initializer/semicolon lands in a later PPNode gets misclassified by parse_top_level_item's function-vs-declaration heuristic (the no-brace-or-semi-in-first-node check) as a function signature, producing expected-function-name/paren errors. Needs a design decision on whether to model -std dialects at all (project currently targets a single default C23-ish configuration per architecture docs) before fixing the header-gating half; the misclassification and digit-separator halves are independent parser bugs.
notes: Fixed: (b) digit-separator lexer bug (numeric_end consumed any apostrophe unconditionally, not just genuine digit-separator '<alnum> sequences, corrupting 0'\\u00c0'-style char-literal-after-number cases); (c) parse_top_level_item misclassification (signature_node_span bailed out early on hitting a Comment PPNode instead of skipping it, and nodes_tokens re-lexed Comment node text as if it were code). Both fixed, verified via full fixture regression scan (no new failures) and FileCheck regen. Remaining: (a) __STDC_VERSION__ dialect-gating needs a design decision, raising to user now.
close_reason: Fixed all three sub-parts: (b) digit-separator lexer bug, (c) parse_top_level_item comment-in-span misclassification, (a) __STDC_VERSION__ defined as C23 (202311L) per user decision, plus discovered/fixed a blocking void* sema bug and a #if true/false evaluation bug along the way.

title: #embed directive unsupported
description: C23 #embed preprocessor directive (for embedding binary resource files as initializer lists) is not implemented. Affects tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/cpp__embed-13.c.
notes: #embed itself is already implemented (Preprocessor::expand_embed in src/pp/mod.rs, handles prefix/suffix/if_empty/limit). tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/cpp__embed-13.c fails because it uses '#embed __FILE__ ...', and __FILE__ is not implemented at all (falls through expand_macros as a bare, unexpanded identifier, so the #embed resource-name check sees an Ident instead of a StringLit and errors with ExpectedEmbedResource). __FILE__/__LINE__/__COUNTER__/#line is already tracked as its own larger feature, slate-parser-ojp.8, with its own design notes and acceptance criteria (per-Loc-dependent expansion, #line adjusting a per-file offset, header/macro-expansion-site correctness) -- reimplementing a narrow slice of it here to unblock this one fixture would duplicate and likely diverge from that work. Added a dependency on ojp.8; this fixture should be revisited once __FILE__ lands.
close_reason: Fixed by slate-parser-ojp.8: __FILE__ is now implemented, so #embed __FILE__ resolves correctly. cpp__embed-13.c parses and its FileCheck block was regenerated.

title: __builtin_complex unsupported
description: __builtin_complex(re, im) construct-a-complex-value builtin is not recognized/parsed specially (takes two real args, produces a _Complex value). Affects tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/complex__builtin-complex-1.c.
close_reason: Fixed. Root cause wasn't __builtin_complex parsing (already worked) but a preprocessor bug: multi-line function-like macro invocations were never expanded. Fixed via merge_open_lines in src/pp/syntax.rs. See wiki/concepts/pp-logical-line-merging.md and wiki/log/2026-09-12-20-07.md.

title: typeof() only supports single-token operand expressions
description: DeclaratorParser::parse_typeof_operand only handles a bare identifier, integer literal, or string literal as the expression operand of typeof(...); anything else (e.g. a ternary like 'typeof(*(1 ? &x : &y))') returns UnsupportedTypeofExpression. DeclaratorParser has no access to the enclosing Parser's full expression grammar (it only holds tokens+pos, no typedef_names), so this needs either plumbing a general expression parser into DeclaratorParser or converting a const_expr::Parser::parse_expression result into ast::Expr. Affects tests/fixtures/gcc-dg/c23-tag-alias-7.c and c23-tag-composite-10.c.
close_reason: Fixed: DeclaratorParser now carries typedef_names and routes typeof()'s operand through const_expr::Parser::parse_expression instead of a single-token match. See wiki/log/2026-09-12-19-48.md.

title: README: refresh preprocessor open questions
description:
README.md is stale in two places.

1. 'Open questions to revisit' (around lines 333-346) says include guards/#pragma once aren't implemented and macro provenance is missing. Both are wrong.
2. The pipeline/phase sections still describe the polyvariant design: Conditional<T> nodes, an eval visitor, and per-branch macro tables. That design was removed in slate-parser-crw.1. The front end now preprocesses and parses once per concrete -D/target configuration.

Rewrite both to describe the single-configuration pipeline, outermost-header token provenance (slate-parser-crw), and planned GNU/Clang/MSVC modes. List the real remaining preprocessor gaps: __has_*, builtin macros, __VA_OPT__, macro-expanded #include, and #embed.
acceptance_criteria: README open questions match the current preprocessor, with no claims about missing guard, once or provenance support.

title: Seed compiler builtin type macros (__SIZE_TYPE__, __UINTPTR_TYPE__, etc.)
description:
Real-world headers processed under clang's -isystem resource dir (e.g. libc-shim's stdlib.h/string.h) use compiler-predefined macros like __SIZE_TYPE__ and __UINTPTR_TYPE__ as type names in declarations (e.g. '__UINTPTR_TYPE__ v = (__UINTPTR_TYPE__)p;'). Slate-parser doesn't seed any of these, so such declarations aren't recognized as declarations and fall through to expression parsing, which then fails with 'unexpected tokens after expression'.

Found while bisecting slate-parser-wf8.1.18 (string.h/stdlib.h chain parse failure): stdlib.h alone (no string.h) already fails on __UINTPTR_TYPE__ inside a static __inline helper (memalignment). Root cause confirmed via minimal repro: a typedef'd __UINTPTR_TYPE__ resolves fine, but without it, the parser can't tell '__UINTPTR_TYPE__ v = ...;' is a declaration.

Fix direction: seed the standard clang/gcc builtin type macros (__SIZE_TYPE__, __PTRDIFF_TYPE__, __UINTPTR_TYPE__, __INTPTR_TYPE__, __WCHAR_TYPE__, __WINT_TYPE__, etc.) into the preprocessor's macro table before parsing, matching what 'clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null' reports for the target, or otherwise make the parser recognize *_TYPE__-shaped macro names as builtin type positions similar to is_target_builtin_name in parser.rs.

Not fixed as part of wf8.1.18 -- that issue's actual root causes (lexer __inline alias, pointer-return-type parsing, multi-line function signatures) are unrelated and were fixed there; this is a separate, pre-existing gap surfaced by the same bisection.
close_reason: Seeded the full clang -dM predefine set (src/predefines/clang_x86_64_linux_gnu.h) for the x86_64-pc-linux-gnu target, parsed via the normal #define machinery at Preprocessor::new. Fixed the fallout: (1) hardcoded FileId(0)-is-root assumption in parse_nodes, now tracked via Preprocessor::main_file; (2) parse_base_type didn't accept 'long unsigned int' ordering; (3) parse_top_level_item's declaration-vs-function heuristic broke on single-line function bodies containing an assignment; (4) macro expansion required exact condition equality, making unconditionally-defined macros invisible inside any nested #ifndef/#if guard; (5) generalized multi-line-signature joining to plain bodyless declarations too. The original wf8.1.18 repro (stdio.h+stdlib.h+string.h prelude) now parses end-to-end. New fixtures: predefined-type-macros.c, multiline-declaration.c. Full cargo test + clippy pass.

title: string.h/stdlib.h chain via libc-shim + clang resource headers fails to parse
description:
Sweeping tests/upstream/fixtures/atoi_atol_prelude_dynamic.c under the real -isystem chain (libc-shim/include + clang resource dir) fails with 'expected `}`' at tests/upstream/fixtures/atoi_atol_prelude_dynamic.c:3 (right after '#include <string.h>' following '#include <stdlib.h>'). A minimal repro of just '#include <string.h>\nint main(void) { return 0; }' alone (no stdlib.h first) fails differently, with 'expected function name' -- so the exact failure depends on what's already been pulled in/defined by the time string.h is processed (likely interacting with the header-guard macro-visibility bug slate-parser-wf8.1.16, and/or bits/types.h's __NEED_* macro-driven conditional typedef idiom in libc-shim). Not yet root-caused past this point.

Repro: ./target/debug/slate-parser parse tests/upstream/fixtures/atoi_atol_prelude_dynamic.c -isystem ~/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include -isystem /usr/lib/clang/22/include
Minimal-ish repro: ./target/debug/slate-parser parse <(printf '#include <string.h>\nint main(void) { return 0; }\n') -isystem ~/Projects/slate/libc-shim/include -isystem /usr/lib/clang/22/include

Found while sweeping tests/upstream/fixtures for slate-parser-wf8.1.13/.14. Recommend re-triaging after slate-parser-wf8.1.16 (header-guard macro visibility) lands, since that may already resolve or change this one's symptom.
close_reason: Fixed three unrelated parser bugs found via bisection of the string.h/stdlib.h repro: (1) lexer missing __inline/__inline__ keyword aliases, (2) parse_function not consuming pointer '*' tokens for function *definitions* returning pointer types, (3) parse_function assuming a signature fits in one PPNode, breaking on wrapped multi-line parameter lists. Added FileCheck fixtures for all three. Full cargo test + clippy pass. The original repro's remaining failure is a separate, unrelated gap (compiler builtin type macros like __UINTPTR_TYPE__ not seeded) -- filed as slate-parser-g6b.

title: Sized __sync_*_N builtins are unsupported
