description: clang accepts the legacy size-suffixed forms __sync_fetch_and_add_1/_2/_4/_8/_16 and the same for sub/and/or/xor/nand (and __sync_val/bool_compare_and_swap_N, __sync_lock_test_and_set_N, __sync_lock_release_N), lowering them the same as the unsuffixed builtins. Verified in clang 22.1.8; slate-parser reports 'unsupported Clang builtin `__sync_fetch_and_add_1`' because sync_builtin's strip_prefix("fetch_and_") leaves 'add_1', which FetchOp::parse rejects. Pure name plumbing: strip a trailing _1|_2|_4|_8|_16 before parsing the op.

title: __scoped_atomic_* builtins are entirely unsupported
description:
clang's __scoped_atomic_* family (load/load_n/store/store_n/exchange/exchange_n/compare_exchange/compare_exchange_n, fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor/nand/min/max/uinc/udec and the *_fetch forms, thread_fence) takes a trailing memory-scope argument and emits atomicrmw/load/store with a syncscope("..."). Verified unsupported in slate-parser against clang 22.1.8, which accepts them all.

atomic_builtin only strips the __sync_, __c11_atomic_ and __atomic_ prefixes, so none of these are recognized. This is not an arith-op gap -- the operations are the same ones __atomic_* already lowers. What is missing is a scope on the IR's atomic nodes (update/read/write/compare_exchange/fence currently carry only a MemoryOrder), plus the extra argument in each arm.

title: __atomic_fetch_uinc/udec do not lower
description:
clang has __atomic_fetch_uinc / __atomic_fetch_udec (no _wrap suffix in the builtin name), emitting atomicrmw uinc_wrap / udec_wrap. Verified in clang 22.1.8; expanding with opt -passes=atomic-expand gives exactly:
  uinc_wrap: new = (old >= v) ? 0 : old + 1
  udec_wrap: new = (old == 0 || old > v) ? v : old - 1
Both are integer-only, so they need no new ArithOp: the existing compare + conditional form expresses them exactly (unlike floating min/max, lh7.2.33). It is pure builtin plumbing -- FetchOp::parse does not know the names, so atomic_builtin never matches and sema reports 'unsupported Clang builtin'. The __scoped_atomic_fetch_uinc/udec spellings depend on scoped-atomic support separately.

title: Atomic fetch fminimum/fmaximum builtins are unsupported
description:
clang has __atomic_fetch_fminimum/_fmaximum and the _num variants (plus the __scoped_atomic_ ones), lowering to atomicrmw fminimum/fmaximum/fminimum_num/fmaximum_num. Unlike __atomic_fetch_min/max on floats (lh7.2.33, now minnum/maxnum), these are NaN-propagating and order -0 below +0, so they do need their own ArithOp variants -- no compare-and-select form expresses them. Currently 'unsupported Clang builtin `__atomic_fetch_fminimum`' -- FetchOp::parse does not recognize the names at all.

NOTE: the locally installed clang 22.1.8 does not have these builtins; src/sema/clang_builtins.rs is ahead of it. There is no local oracle to diff against, so check a newer clang before implementing.
close_reason: Closed

title: sizeof of an incomplete type reports 'incomplete field type'
description:
'struct X; int n = sizeof(struct X);' is correctly rejected, but the message is ResolveError::Unsupported("incomplete field type") -- there is no field involved. clang says "invalid application of 'sizeof' to an incomplete type 'struct X'" and gcc says "invalid application of 'sizeof' to incomplete type".

Pre-existing at file scope; noticed in slate-parser-8lv.4 because block-scope forward declarations now reach the same path (C11 6.7.2.3p8 hiding). Not introduced by that change.
close_reason: Improved sizeof incomplete-type diagnostics and regenerated error coverage.

title: C23 tag redefinition: enum member vs its underlying type splits clang and gcc
Warn on int/long redeclaration conflicts when they share a layout
description: On targets where int and long are the same size (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc), 'int f(int); long f(int);' and 'int x; long x;' lower to identical IR types, so slate-parser-wxs.3's conflicting-types check sees no difference and stays silent. clang/gcc error, MSVC warns C4142. Needs the C-level type (c_types / CTypeMetadata) at declare_function/declare_global, like slate-parser-4o9.
notes:
Fixed in slate-parser-9ve.4. Redeclaration merging now runs on C types in TypeResolver::merge_redeclaration; when the C types are incompatible but types::same_layout says the lowered types coincide (ignoring integer signedness), it is a conflicting-types warning instead of an error.

Oracle confirmed this is MSVC's own rule, not an invention: C4142 'benign redefinition of type' fires exactly when the layouts coincide (int/long and int/unsigned under LLP64), and C2371 'different basic types' when they do not (int/long long, distinct structs). clang 22 and gcc 16 reject all of them.

So on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc 'int x; long x;' and 'int f(int); long f(int);' now warn; on LP64 they stay errors because long is 64-bit there. Fixture: tests/fixtures/sema/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/ir_redeclaration_layout.c. ir-spec.md conflict table generalized from 'same-size integers differing only in sign' to 'incompatible C types of identical layout'.
close_reason: Closed

title: Distinguish plain char from signed/unsigned char for -Wpointer-sign
description: Plain char lowers to the same i8/u8 as signed/unsigned char, so clang's 'unique plain char' -Wpointer-sign case (char* <-> signed char* where char is signed) is never raised by Lowerer::convert. Needs the C-level type (c_types metadata) at conversion time. See slate-parser-x5r.
notes: Fixed in slate-parser-9ve.3. Signedness is now compared on C types (CTypes::integer_shape in src/sema/ctype/convert.rs), where plain Char, SChar and UChar are three distinct kinds of the same shape, so char* <-> signed char* warns pointer-sign in both directions. The old differ_only_in_sign compared IR widths, which collapsed all three to i8. Fixture: tests/fixtures/sema/ir_conversion_rules.c (plain_char, signed_char).
close_reason: Closed

title: Point IR lowering warnings at the conversion site, not the operand
description: Converted values reuse the operand's node span, so pointer conversion warnings point at p in take((unsigned *)p) and at the initializer instead of the declarator (clang points at the argument / declarator name). Pass the conversion-site span into Lowerer::warn. See slate-parser-x5r.

title: Reject implicit conversions that drop _Atomic from a pointee
description: int *p = (_Atomic int *)q is an -Wincompatible-pointer-types error in clang 22 but Lowerer::convert accepts it silently as pointer_cast because compatible() ignores atomic in the dropped direction. See slate-parser-x5r.
notes: Resolved in slate-parser-9ve.3, but in the OPPOSITE direction from this bead's title. Oracle 2026-09-19: int *p = (_Atomic int *)q is an error in clang 22.1.8 (-Wincompatible-pointer-types) and gcc 16.2.1, but MSVC 14.51 accepts it silently. The project rule rejects only where all three compilers agree, so dropping _Atomic from a pointee is accepted with the incompatible-pointer-types warning (clang's name for it), not rejected. Fixture: tests/fixtures/sema/ir_atomic_pointee.c; recorded in wiki/concepts/diagnostic-severity.md.
close_reason: Closed

title: Report -Wpointer-sign and discards-qualifiers from IR lowering
description: Implicit pointer conversions that clang accepts with a warning (pointee differing only in signedness: -Wpointer-sign; dropped pointee qualifiers: -Wincompatible-pointer-types-discards-qualifiers) are lowered silently as pointer_cast. Warnings only come from the AST-level TranslationUnit::analyze pass; resolve_module returns Result with no diagnostics channel, and these warnings need resolved types. Add a warnings channel to lowering and Warning::PointerSign / IncompatiblePointerTypesDiscardsQualifiers (both on by default in clang 22, not pedantic) if these are worth reporting.
close_reason: IR lowering now emits -Wpointer-sign and -Wincompatible-pointer-types-discards-qualifiers through a Lowerer diagnostics channel; nested qualifier mismatches accepted

title: Initialized locals print their C type metadata twice
description: With --show-metadata, 'typedef int T[3]; int f(void){ T b = {}; return b[0]; }' prints [c="T"] [c_canon="int[3]"] [typedef_chain="T"] twice on the let. The initializer value node is anchored at the declarator span, so it shares declarator.id with the Let and the metadata keyed by that NodeId prints on both. Pre-existing; the VLA {} path copies the same anchoring.
close_reason: Declarator C type metadata is annotated on the Let/Global, and the initializer value anchored at the declarator gets its own id, so the keys print once. Covered by ir_metadata_single_owner.c.

title: Floating atomic fetch min/max have no exact IR form
description: lh7.2.23 lowers floating __atomic_fetch_add/sub, but clang also accepts __atomic_fetch_min/max (and _fetch variants) on float/double, emitting atomicrmw fmin/fmax. Those are NaN-ignoring (minnum/maxnum), which the existing compare+conditional computation does not express: lt(old, v) ? old : v returns NaN when v is NaN, where fmin returns old. Needs a min/max arith op (or a floating flag on the compare) before it can lower. Currently 'unsupported in numeric IR lowering: atomic arithmetic on non-integer'.
acceptance_criteria: __atomic_fetch_min/max on float lower to a computation with minnum/maxnum semantics, covered by a FileCheck fixture.
close_reason: Closed

title: GCC flavor x86 ISA predefine parity (__FP_FAST_FMA*, __MMX_WITH_SSE__)
description: GCC flavor reuses the clang x86 predefine snapshot with ISA macros generated from TargetInfo.isa (src/target/x86_isa.rs). gcc 16 also defines __FP_FAST_FMA, __FP_FAST_FMAF, __FP_FAST_FMAF32, __FP_FAST_FMAF32x, __FP_FAST_FMAF64 when FMA is enabled, and __MMX_WITH_SSE__ on x86_64. __BIGGEST_ALIGNMENT__ is already handled. Carried over from slate-parser-d2e.

title: MSVC __asm block parsing
description: Punted. MSVC __asm/_asm: instruction ends at end of expansion line, next __asm, or closing brace; ; starts a comment; braces nest. Proposed skeleton: MsAsm { instructions: label, mnemonic string, comma-split operands with tokens classified as Register | Ident (C symbol candidate) | Token }. x86 (32-bit) only. Needs line lookup from preprocessor line tables and MASM radix literals (100h). No fixtures exist.

title: Builtin macros __DATE__/__TIME__ unimplemented
description: slate-parser-ojp.8 implemented __LINE__/__FILE__/__FILE_NAME__/__BASE_FILE__/__INCLUDE_LEVEL__/__COUNTER__ and #line, but deliberately skipped __DATE__/__TIME__: they need calendar math (day-of-week, month name) from a raw timestamp, and the crate has no time/chrono dependency. Not required by ojp.8's acceptance criteria since these are inherently non-reproducible across builds anyway.
close_reason: Implemented __DATE__/__TIME__ builtin expansion with translation-start local timestamp formatting, non-Unix Gregorian fallback, and stable FileCheck coverage.
